### 231. Next Permutation of String
**ID:** `STRING-0231`

**Problem:** Rearrange string into the lexicographically next greater permutation.

**Example Input:** `s = "1234"`

**Example Output:** `Next permutation: "1243"`

**Explanation:** Find rightmost ascent; swap with next greater to its right; reverse suffix.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static String nextPerm(String s){char[]a=s.toCharArray();int i=a.length-2;while(i>=0&&a[i]>=a[i+1])i--;if(i>=0){int j=a.length-1;while(a[j]<=a[i])j--;char t=a[i];a[i]=a[j];a[j]=t;}int l=i+1,r=a.length-1;while(l<r){char t=a[l];a[l++]=a[r];a[r--]=t;}return new String(a);}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println("1234 → "+nextPerm("1234"));System.out.println("4321 → "+nextPerm("4321"));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 233. Minimum Window Substring
**ID:** `STRING-0233`

**Problem:** Find the smallest window in s containing all chars of t.

**Example Input:** `s="ADOBECODEBANC", t="ABC"`

**Example Output:** `Minimum window: "BANC"`

**Explanation:** Sliding window with char frequency maps; shrink when all t chars covered.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static String minWindow(String s,String t){Map<Character,Integer>need=new HashMap<>();for(char c:t.toCharArray())need.merge(c,1,Integer::sum);int have=0,required=need.size(),l=0;int[]best={-1,0,0};Map<Character,Integer>win=new HashMap<>();for(int r=0;r<s.length();r++){char c=s.charAt(r);win.merge(c,1,Integer::sum);if(need.containsKey(c)&&win.get(c).equals(need.get(c)))have++;while(have==required){if(best[0]==-1||r-l+1<best[0]-best[1]){best[0]=r+1;best[1]=l;best[2]=r;}char lc=s.charAt(l);win.merge(lc,-1,Integer::sum);if(need.containsKey(lc)&&win.get(lc)<need.get(lc))have--;l++;}}return best[0]==-1?"":s.substring(best[1],best[0]);}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println(minWindow("ADOBECODEBANC","ABC"));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 234. Check Word Pattern
**ID:** `STRING-0234`

**Problem:** Check if string s follows the same pattern as word array.

**Example Input:** `pattern="abba", s="dog cat cat dog"`

**Example Output:** `Follows pattern: true`

**Explanation:** Two-way map: pattern char ↔ word; verify consistency.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static boolean wordPattern(String pat,String s){String[]words=s.split(" ");if(pat.length()!=words.length)return false;Map<Character,String>m1=new HashMap<>();Map<String,Character>m2=new HashMap<>();for(int i=0;i<pat.length();i++){char c=pat.charAt(i);String w=words[i];if(m1.containsKey(c)&&!m1.get(c).equals(w))return false;if(m2.containsKey(w)&&m2.get(w)!=c)return false;m1.put(c,w);m2.put(w,c);}return true;}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println("abba/dog cat cat dog: "+wordPattern("abba","dog cat cat dog"));System.out.println("abba/dog cat cat fish: "+wordPattern("abba","dog cat cat fish"));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 235. Check Pangram
**ID:** `STRING-0235`

**Problem:** A pangram contains every letter of the alphabet at least once.

**Example Input:** `s = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"`

**Example Output:** `Is Pangram: true`

**Explanation:** Add each lowercase letter to a Set; check size == 26.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
```

### 236. Zigzag Conversion
**ID:** `STRING-0236`

**Problem:** Convert string to zigzag on n rows and read row by row.

**Example Input:** `s="PAYPALISHIRING", numRows=3`

**Example Output:** `"PAHNAPLSIIGYIR"`

**Explanation:** Assign each char to a row using a pointer that bounces 0..numRows-1.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static String zigzag(String s,int rows){if(rows==1)return s;StringBuilder[]sb=new StringBuilder[rows];for(int i=0;i<rows;i++)sb[i]=new StringBuilder();int row=0,dir=-1;for(char c:s.toCharArray()){sb[row].append(c);if(row==0||row==rows-1)dir=-dir;row+=dir;}StringBuilder res=new StringBuilder();for(StringBuilder b:sb)res.append(b);return res.toString();}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println(zigzag("PAYPALISHIRING",3));System.out.println(zigzag("PAYPALISHIRING",4));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 237. Longest Common Substring
**ID:** `STRING-0237`

**Problem:** Find the length of the longest common substring (contiguous) of two strings.

**Example Input:** `s1="abcdef", s2="zcdemf"`

**Example Output:** `Longest common substring length = 3  ("cde")`

**Explanation:** DP: dp[i][j] = length of common suffix ending at s1[i-1] and s2[j-1].

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int lcSubstr(String a,String b){int m=a.length(),n=b.length(),max=0;int[][]dp=new int[m+1][n+1];for(int i=1;i<=m;i++)for(int j=1;j<=n;j++){dp[i][j]=a.charAt(i-1)==b.charAt(j-1)?dp[i-1][j-1]+1:0;max=Math.max(max,dp[i][j]);}return max;}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println("abcdef / zcdemf: "+lcSubstr("abcdef","zcdemf"));System.out.println("ABAB / BABA: "+lcSubstr("ABAB","BABA"));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(m×n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(m×n)

### 238. Distinct Subsequences Count
**ID:** `STRING-0238`

**Problem:** Count distinct subsequences of s that equal t.

**Example Input:** `s="rabbbit", t="rabbit"`

**Example Output:** `Distinct subsequences = 3`

**Explanation:** DP: dp[i][j] = ways to form t[0..j-1] from s[0..i-1].

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int numDistinct(String s,String t){int m=s.length(),n=t.length();long[][]dp=new long[m+1][n+1];for(int i=0;i<=m;i++)dp[i][0]=1;for(int i=1;i<=m;i++)for(int j=1;j<=n;j++){dp[i][j]=dp[i-1][j]+(s.charAt(i-1)==t.charAt(j-1)?dp[i-1][j-1]:0);}return(int)dp[m][n];}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println("rabbbit/rabbit: "+numDistinct("rabbbit","rabbit"));System.out.println("babgbag/bag: "+numDistinct("babgbag","bag"));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(m×n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(m×n)

**Example Output:** `[0,1]`

**Explanation:** Use HashMap to store seen value and index.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 1 - Two Sum
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
        Map<Integer, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
            int complement = target - nums[i];
            if (map.containsKey(complement)) return new int[]{map.get(complement), i};
            map.put(nums[i], i);
        }
        return new int[]{};
    }
}
```

### 242. LeetCode 53 - Maximum Subarray

**Example Input:** `nums=[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4]`

**Example Output:** `6`

**Explanation:** Kadane algorithm keeps best running sum.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 53 - Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
class Solution {
    public int maxSubArray(int[] nums) {
        int maxSum = nums[0], currentSum = nums[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < nums.length; i++) {
            currentSum = Math.max(nums[i], currentSum + nums[i]);
            maxSum = Math.max(maxSum, currentSum);
        }
        return maxSum;
    }
}
```

**Example Output:** `[24,12,8,6]`

**Explanation:** Use prefix and suffix products without division.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 238 - Product of Array Except Self
class Solution {
    public int[] productExceptSelf(int[] nums) {
        int n = nums.length;
        int[] result = new int[n];
        result[0] = 1;
        for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) result[i] = result[i-1] * nums[i-1];
        int right = 1;
        for (int i = n-1; i >= 0; i--) { result[i] *= right; right *= nums[i]; }
        return result;
    }
}
```

```java
// LeetCode 49 - Group Anagrams
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public List<List<String>> groupAnagrams(String[] strs) {
        Map<String, List<String>> map = new HashMap<>();
        for (String s : strs) {
            char[] arr = s.toCharArray(); Arrays.sort(arr);
            map.computeIfAbsent(new String(arr), k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(s);
```

### 246. LeetCode 3 - Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0246`

**Problem:** Solve Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `s=abcabcbb`

**Example Output:** `3`

**Explanation:** Sliding window with HashSet.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 3 - Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) {
        Map<Character, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
        int max = 0, left = 0;
        for (int right = 0; right < s.length(); right++) {
            char c = s.charAt(right);
            if (map.containsKey(c)) left = Math.max(left, map.get(c) + 1);
            map.put(c, right);
            max = Math.max(max, right - left + 1);
        }
        return max;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(min(n,charset))

### 247. LeetCode 20 - Valid Parentheses
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0247`

**Problem:** Solve Valid Parentheses using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `s={[()]}`

**Example Output:** `true`

**Explanation:** Stack tracks expected closing order.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 20 - Valid Parentheses
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public boolean isValid(String s) {
        Deque<Character> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) {
            if (c == '(' || c == '[' || c == '{') { stack.push(c); continue; }
            if (stack.isEmpty()) return false;
            char top = stack.pop();
            if (c == ')' && top != '(') return false;
            if (c == ']' && top != '[') return false;
            if (c == '}' && top != '{') return false;
        }
        return stack.isEmpty();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 206 - Reverse Linked List
class Solution {
    public ListNode reverseList(ListNode head) {
        ListNode prev = null, curr = head;
        while (curr != null) {
            ListNode next = curr.next;
            curr.next = prev;
            prev = curr;
            curr = next;
        }
        return prev;
    }
}
```

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 141 - Linked List Cycle (Floyd's algorithm)
class Solution {
    public boolean hasCycle(ListNode head) {
        ListNode slow = head, fast = head;
        while (fast != null && fast.next != null) {
            slow = slow.next;
            fast = fast.next.next;
            if (slow == fast) return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}
```

### 250. LeetCode 102 - Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0250`

**Problem:** Solve Binary Tree Level Order Traversal using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `root=[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]`

**Example Output:** `[[3],[9,20],[15,7]]`

**Explanation:** BFS using queue.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 102 - Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public List<List<Integer>> levelOrder(TreeNode root) {
        List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<>();
        if (root == null) return result;
        Queue<TreeNode> q = new LinkedList<>();
        q.offer(root);
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            int size = q.size();
            List<Integer> level = new ArrayList<>();
            for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
                TreeNode node = q.poll();
                level.add(node.val);
                if (node.left != null) q.offer(node.left);
                if (node.right != null) q.offer(node.right);
            }
            result.add(level);
        }
        return result;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 251. LeetCode 200 - Number of Islands
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0251`

**Problem:** Solve Number of Islands using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `grid=[11110,11010,11000,00000]`

**Example Output:** `1`

**Explanation:** DFS/BFS marks connected land.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 200 - Number of Islands (BFS)
class Solution {
    public int numIslands(char[][] grid) {
        int count = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < grid.length; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < grid[0].length; j++)
                if (grid[i][j] == '1') { bfs(grid, i, j); count++; }
        return count;
    }
    void bfs(char[][] grid, int r, int c) {
        int[][] dirs = {{0,1},{0,-1},{1,0},{-1,0}};
        java.util.Queue<int[]> q = new java.util.LinkedList<>();
        q.offer(new int[]{r, c}); grid[r][c] = '0';
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            int[] cur = q.poll();
            for (int[] d : dirs) {
                int nr = cur[0]+d[0], nc = cur[1]+d[1];
                if (nr>=0 && nr<grid.length && nc>=0 && nc<grid[0].length && grid[nr][nc]=='1') {
                    grid[nr][nc] = '0'; q.offer(new int[]{nr, nc});
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m×n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(m×n)

### 253. LeetCode 322 - Coin Change
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0253`

**Problem:** Solve Coin Change using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `coins=[1,2,5], amount=11`

**Example Output:** `3`

**Explanation:** DP minimum coins for each amount.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 322 - Coin Change (BFS / DP)
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public int coinChange(int[] coins, int amount) {
        int[] dp = new int[amount + 1];
        Arrays.fill(dp, amount + 1);
        dp[0] = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i <= amount; i++)
            for (int coin : coins)
                if (coin <= i) dp[i] = Math.min(dp[i], dp[i - coin] + 1);
        return dp[amount] > amount ? -1 : dp[amount];
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(amount×coins) &nbsp; **Space:** O(amount)

### 254. LeetCode 15 - 3Sum
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0254`

**Problem:** Solve 3Sum using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `Use LeetCode sample input`

**Example Output:** `Use LeetCode sample output`

**Explanation:** Use the commonly accepted medium solution pattern for 3Sum.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 15 - 3Sum
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public List<List<Integer>> threeSum(int[] nums) {
        Arrays.sort(nums);
        List<List<Integer>> res = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length - 2; i++) {
            if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i-1]) continue;
            int left = i+1, right = nums.length-1;
            while (left < right) {
                int sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];
                if (sum == 0) {
                    res.add(Arrays.asList(nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]));
                    while (left < right && nums[left] == nums[left+1]) left++;
                    while (left < right && nums[right] == nums[right-1]) right--;
                    left++; right--;
                } else if (sum < 0) left++;
                else right--;
            }
        }
        return res;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n²) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 256. LeetCode 42 - Trapping Rain Water
**ID:** `ARRAYLC-0256`

**Problem:** Solve Trapping Rain Water using Java with optimal interview approach.

**Example Input:** `Use LeetCode sample input`

**Example Output:** `Use LeetCode sample output`

**Explanation:** Use the commonly accepted hard solution pattern for Trapping Rain Water.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 42 - Trapping Rain Water
class Solution {
    public int trap(int[] height) {
        int left = 0, right = height.length - 1, water = 0;
        int leftMax = 0, rightMax = 0;
        while (left < right) {
            if (height[left] < height[right]) {
                if (height[left] >= leftMax) leftMax = height[left];
                else water += leftMax - height[left];
                left++;
            } else {
                if (height[right] >= rightMax) rightMax = height[right];
                else water += rightMax - height[right];
                right--;
            }
        }
        return water;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
// LeetCode 56 - Merge Intervals
import java.util.*;
class Solution {
    public int[][] merge(int[][] intervals) {
        Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> a[0] - b[0]);
        List<int[]> res = new ArrayList<>();
        int[] cur = intervals[0];
        for (int i = 1; i < intervals.length; i++) {
            if (intervals[i][0] <= cur[1]) cur[1] = Math.max(cur[1], intervals[i][1]);
            else { res.add(cur); cur = intervals[i]; }
        }
        res.add(cur);
        return res.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }
}
```

### 258. LeetCode 75 - Sort Colors

**Example Input:** `Use LeetCode sample input`

**Example Output:** `Use LeetCode sample output`

**Explanation:** Use the commonly accepted medium solution pattern for Sort Colors.

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 75 - Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
class Solution {
    public void sortColors(int[] nums) {
        int low = 0, mid = 0, high = nums.length - 1;
        while (mid <= high) {
            if (nums[mid] == 0) { swap(nums, low++, mid++); }
            else if (nums[mid] == 1) { mid++; }
            else { swap(nums, mid, high--); }
        }
    }
    private void swap(int[] a, int i, int j) { int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

**Answer:**
```java
// LeetCode 88 - Merge Sorted Array
class Solution {
    public void merge(int[] nums1, int m, int[] nums2, int n) {
        int i = m - 1, j = n - 1, k = m + n - 1;
        while (i >= 0 && j >= 0) {
            nums1[k--] = (nums1[i] > nums2[j]) ? nums1[i--] : nums2[j--];
        }
        while (j >= 0) nums1[k--] = nums2[j--];
    }
}
```

### 260. LeetCode 33 - Search in Rotated Sorted Array
**ID:** `LC-0260`

**Problem:** LeetCode 33 - Search in Rotated Sorted Array.

**Example Input:** `nums=[4,5,6,7,0,1,2], target=0`

**Example Output:** `4 (index of 0)`

**Explanation:** Binary search: determine which half is sorted, then check if target is in that half.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public int search(int[] nums, int target) {
        int lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;
        while (lo <= hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (nums[mid] == target) return mid;
            if (nums[lo] <= nums[mid]) {            // left half sorted
                if (target >= nums[lo] && target < nums[mid]) hi = mid - 1;
                else lo = mid + 1;
            } else {                                 // right half sorted
                if (target > nums[mid] && target <= nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1;
                else hi = mid - 1;
            }
        }
        return -1;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution s = new Solution();
        int[] nums = {4,5,6,7,0,1,2};
        System.out.println(s.search(nums, 0));   // 4
        System.out.println(s.search(nums, 3));   // -1
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 261. LeetCode 34 - Find First and Last Position
**ID:** `LC-0261`

**Problem:** LeetCode 34 - Find First and Last Position.

**Example Input:** `nums=[5,7,7,8,8,10], target=8`

**Example Output:** `[3,4]`

**Explanation:** Two binary searches: one for leftmost, one for rightmost occurrence.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public int[] searchRange(int[] nums, int target) {
        return new int[]{findFirst(nums,target), findLast(nums,target)};
    }
    int findFirst(int[] nums, int target) {
        int lo=0,hi=nums.length-1,idx=-1;
        while(lo<=hi){int mid=lo+(hi-lo)/2;if(nums[mid]==target){idx=mid;hi=mid-1;}else if(nums[mid]<target)lo=mid+1;else hi=mid-1;}
        return idx;
    }
    int findLast(int[] nums, int target) {
        int lo=0,hi=nums.length-1,idx=-1;
        while(lo<=hi){int mid=lo+(hi-lo)/2;if(nums[mid]==target){idx=mid;lo=mid+1;}else if(nums[mid]<target)lo=mid+1;else hi=mid-1;}
        return idx;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution s = new Solution();
        int[] nums = {5,7,7,8,8,10};
        System.out.println(java.util.Arrays.toString(s.searchRange(nums, 8))); // [3,4]
        System.out.println(java.util.Arrays.toString(s.searchRange(nums, 6))); // [-1,-1]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 262. LeetCode 704 - Binary Search
**ID:** `LC-0262`

**Problem:** LeetCode 704 - Binary Search.

**Example Input:** `nums=[-1,0,3,5,9,12], target=9`

**Example Output:** `4`

**Explanation:** Classic binary search: compare mid element with target, adjust lo/hi accordingly.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public int search(int[] nums, int target) {
        int lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;
        while (lo <= hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (nums[mid] == target) return mid;
            if (nums[mid] < target) lo = mid + 1;
            else hi = mid - 1;
        }
        return -1;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution s = new Solution();
        int[] nums = {-1,0,3,5,9,12};
        System.out.println(s.search(nums, 9));   // 4
        System.out.println(s.search(nums, 2));   // -1
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 263. LeetCode 153 - Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
**ID:** `LC-0263`

**Problem:** LeetCode 153 - Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array.

**Example Input:** `nums=[3,4,5,1,2]`

**Example Output:** `1`

**Explanation:** Binary search: minimum is at the inflection point. If left < right the left side is sorted.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public int findMin(int[] nums) {
        int lo = 0, hi = nums.length - 1;
        while (lo < hi) {
            int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
            if (nums[mid] > nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1;
            else hi = mid;
        }
        return nums[lo];
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution s = new Solution();
        System.out.println(s.findMin(new int[]{3,4,5,1,2}));   // 1
        System.out.println(s.findMin(new int[]{4,5,6,7,0,1,2})); // 0
        System.out.println(s.findMin(new int[]{11,13,15,17}));  // 11
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 264. LeetCode 125 - Valid Palindrome
**ID:** `LC-0264`

**Problem:** LeetCode 125 - Valid Palindrome.

**Example Input:** `s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"`

**Example Output:** `true`

**Explanation:** Two pointers: skip non-alphanumeric, compare case-insensitively.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public boolean isPalindrome(String s) {
        int l = 0, r = s.length() - 1;
        while (l < r) {
            while (l < r && !Character.isLetterOrDigit(s.charAt(l))) l++;
            while (l < r && !Character.isLetterOrDigit(s.charAt(r))) r--;
            if (Character.toLowerCase(s.charAt(l)) != Character.toLowerCase(s.charAt(r)))
                return false;
            l++; r--;
        }
        return true;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution s = new Solution();
        System.out.println(s.isPalindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama")); // true
        System.out.println(s.isPalindrome("race a car")); // false
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 265. LeetCode 242 - Valid Anagram
**ID:** `LC-0265`

**Problem:** LeetCode 242 - Valid Anagram.

**Example Input:** `s="anagram", t="nagaram"`

**Example Output:** `true`

**Explanation:** Count character frequencies in both strings and compare.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public boolean isAnagram(String s, String t) {
        if (s.length() != t.length()) return false;
        int[] count = new int[26];
        for (char c : s.toCharArray()) count[c-'a']++;
        for (char c : t.toCharArray()) count[c-'a']--;
        for (int c : count) if (c != 0) return false;
        return true;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution sol = new Solution();
        System.out.println(sol.isAnagram("anagram","nagaram")); // true
        System.out.println(sol.isAnagram("rat","car"));         // false
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 266. LeetCode 5 - Longest Palindromic Substring
**ID:** `LC-0266`

**Problem:** LeetCode 5 - Longest Palindromic Substring.

**Example Input:** `s = "babad"`

**Example Output:** `bab`

**Explanation:** Expand around center for each character; try both odd and even length palindromes.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public String longestPalindrome(String s) {
        if (s.isEmpty()) return "";
        int start=0, maxLen=1;
        for (int i=0;i<s.length();i++) {
            int odd  = expand(s,i,i);
            int even = expand(s,i,i+1);
            int len = Math.max(odd,even);
            if (len > maxLen) { maxLen=len; start=i-(len-1)/2; }
        }
        return s.substring(start, start+maxLen);
    }
    int expand(String s, int l, int r) {
        while(l>=0&&r<s.length()&&s.charAt(l)==s.charAt(r)){l--;r++;}
        return r-l-1;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Solution sol = new Solution();
        System.out.println(sol.longestPalindrome("babad")); // bab
        System.out.println(sol.longestPalindrome("cbbd"));  // bb
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n^2) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 267. LeetCode 76 - Minimum Window Substring
**ID:** `LC-0267`

**Problem:** LeetCode 76 - Minimum Window Substring.

**Example Input:** `s="ADOBECODEBANC", t="ABC"`

**Example Output:** `BANC`

**Explanation:** Sliding window: expand right to include all chars of t, then shrink left to minimize.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public String minWindow(String s, String t) {
        Map<Character,Integer> need=new HashMap<>(), window=new HashMap<>();
        for(char c:t.toCharArray()) need.merge(c,1,Integer::sum);
        int l=0,valid=0,minLen=Integer.MAX_VALUE,minL=0;
        for(int r=0;r<s.length();r++){
            char c=s.charAt(r);
            window.merge(c,1,Integer::sum);
            if(need.containsKey(c)&&window.get(c).equals(need.get(c))) valid++;
            while(valid==need.size()){
                if(r-l+1<minLen){minLen=r-l+1;minL=l;}
                char lc=s.charAt(l++);
                window.merge(lc,-1,Integer::sum);
                if(need.containsKey(lc)&&window.get(lc)<need.get(lc)) valid--;
            }
        }
        return minLen==Integer.MAX_VALUE?"":s.substring(minL,minL+minLen);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(new Solution().minWindow("ADOBECODEBANC","ABC")); // BANC
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m+n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(m+n)
---

### 268. LeetCode 438 - Find All Anagrams in a String
**ID:** `LC-0268`

**Problem:** LeetCode 438 - Find All Anagrams in a String.

**Example Input:** `s="cbaebabacd", p="abc"`

**Example Output:** `[0,6]`

**Explanation:** Sliding window of size p.length; compare frequency arrays.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public List<Integer> findAnagrams(String s, String p) {
        List<Integer> res=new ArrayList<>();
        if(s.length()<p.length()) return res;
        int[] pc=new int[26], sc=new int[26];
        for(char c:p.toCharArray()) pc[c-'a']++;
        for(int i=0;i<p.length();i++) sc[s.charAt(i)-'a']++;
        if(Arrays.equals(pc,sc)) res.add(0);
        for(int i=p.length();i<s.length();i++){
            sc[s.charAt(i)-'a']++;
            sc[s.charAt(i-p.length())-'a']--;
            if(Arrays.equals(pc,sc)) res.add(i-p.length()+1);
        }
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(new Solution().findAnagrams("cbaebabacd","abc")); // [0,6]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m+n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 269. LeetCode 567 - Permutation in String
**ID:** `LC-0269`

**Problem:** LeetCode 567 - Permutation in String.

**Example Input:** `s1="ab", s2="eidbaooo"`

**Example Output:** `true`

**Explanation:** Sliding window of size s1.length; frequency array comparison.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    public boolean checkInclusion(String s1, String s2) {
        if(s1.length()>s2.length()) return false;
        int[] c1=new int[26], c2=new int[26];
        for(char c:s1.toCharArray()) c1[c-'a']++;
        for(int i=0;i<s1.length();i++) c2[s2.charAt(i)-'a']++;
        if(Arrays.equals(c1,c2)) return true;
        for(int i=s1.length();i<s2.length();i++){
            c2[s2.charAt(i)-'a']++;
            c2[s2.charAt(i-s1.length())-'a']--;
            if(Arrays.equals(c1,c2)) return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        Solution s=new Solution();
        System.out.println(s.checkInclusion("ab","eidbaooo")); // true
        System.out.println(s.checkInclusion("ab","eidboaoo")); // false
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m+n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 270. LeetCode 344 - Reverse String

**Example Output:** `['o','l','l','e','h']`

**Explanation:** Two-pointer swap in-place from both ends toward the center.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    public void reverseString(char[] s) {
        int l=0, r=s.length-1;
        while(l<r){char tmp=s[l];s[l++]=s[r];s[r--]=tmp;}
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        char[] s={'h','e','l','l','o'};
        new Solution().reverseString(s);
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(s)); // [o,l,l,e,h]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 271. LeetCode 14 - Longest Common Prefix

**Example Output:** `fl`

**Explanation:** Use first string as prefix; shrink it until all strings start with it.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public String longestCommonPrefix(String[] strs) {
        if(strs.length==0) return "";
        String prefix=strs[0];
        for(int i=1;i<strs.length;i++)
            while(!strs[i].startsWith(prefix))
                prefix=prefix.substring(0,prefix.length()-1);
        return prefix;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        Solution s=new Solution();
        System.out.println(s.longestCommonPrefix(new String[]{"flower","flow","flight"})); // fl
        System.out.println(s.longestCommonPrefix(new String[]{"dog","racecar","car"}));    // ""
    }
}
```

```java
public class Solution {
    public int strStr(String haystack, String needle) {

        for(int i=0;i<=haystack.length()-needle.length();i++){
```

### 273. LeetCode 22 - Generate Parentheses
**ID:** `LC-0273`

**Problem:** LeetCode 22 - Generate Parentheses.

**Example Input:** `n=3`

**Example Output:** `["((()))","(()())","(())()","()(())","()()()"]`

**Explanation:** Backtracking: track open/close counts; add '(' if open<n, add ')' if close<open.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public List<String> generateParenthesis(int n) {
        List<String> res=new ArrayList<>();
        backtrack(res,new StringBuilder(),0,0,n);
        return res;
    }
    void backtrack(List<String> res, StringBuilder cur, int open, int close, int n){
        if(cur.length()==2*n){res.add(cur.toString());return;}
        if(open<n){cur.append('(');backtrack(res,cur,open+1,close,n);cur.deleteCharAt(cur.length()-1);}
        if(close<open){cur.append(')');backtrack(res,cur,open,close+1,n);cur.deleteCharAt(cur.length()-1);}
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(new Solution().generateParenthesis(3));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(4^n/sqrt(n)) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 274. LeetCode 21 - Merge Two Sorted Lists
**ID:** `LC-0274`

**Problem:** LeetCode 21 - Merge Two Sorted Lists.

**Example Input:** `l1=[1,2,4], l2=[1,3,4]`

**Example Output:** `[1,1,2,3,4,4]`

**Explanation:** Dummy head pointer; repeatedly attach smaller node, advance that list's pointer.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static class ListNode { int val; ListNode next; ListNode(int v){val=v;} }
    public ListNode mergeTwoLists(ListNode l1, ListNode l2) {
        ListNode dummy=new ListNode(0), cur=dummy;
        while(l1!=null && l2!=null){
            if(l1.val<=l2.val){cur.next=l1;l1=l1.next;}
            else{cur.next=l2;l2=l2.next;}
            cur=cur.next;
        }
        cur.next=(l1!=null)?l1:l2;
        return dummy.next;
    }
    static void print(ListNode n){while(n!=null){System.out.print(n.val+" ");n=n.next;}System.out.println();}
    public static void main(String[] args){
        ListNode l1=new ListNode(1); l1.next=new ListNode(2); l1.next.next=new ListNode(4);
        ListNode l2=new ListNode(1); l2.next=new ListNode(3); l2.next.next=new ListNode(4);
        print(new Solution().mergeTwoLists(l1,l2)); // 1 1 2 3 4 4
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m+n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 275. LeetCode 19 - Remove Nth Node From End
**ID:** `LC-0275`

**Problem:** LeetCode 19 - Remove Nth Node From End.

**Example Input:** `head=[1,2,3,4,5], n=2`

**Example Output:** `[1,2,3,5]`

**Explanation:** Two pointers gap of n: advance fast n steps, then move both until fast reaches end.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static class ListNode { int val; ListNode next; ListNode(int v){val=v;} }
    public ListNode removeNthFromEnd(ListNode head, int n) {
        ListNode dummy=new ListNode(0); dummy.next=head;
        ListNode fast=dummy, slow=dummy;
        for(int i=0;i<=n;i++) fast=fast.next;
        while(fast!=null){fast=fast.next;slow=slow.next;}
        slow.next=slow.next.next;
        return dummy.next;
    }
    static void print(ListNode n){while(n!=null){System.out.print(n.val+" ");n=n.next;}System.out.println();}
    public static void main(String[] args){
        ListNode h=new ListNode(1);h.next=new ListNode(2);h.next.next=new ListNode(3);
        h.next.next.next=new ListNode(4);h.next.next.next.next=new ListNode(5);
        print(new Solution().removeNthFromEnd(h,2)); // 1 2 3 5
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 276. LeetCode 143 - Reorder List
**ID:** `LC-0276`

**Problem:** LeetCode 143 - Reorder List.

**Example Input:** `head=[1,2,3,4,5]`

**Example Output:** `[1,5,2,4,3]`

**Explanation:** Find mid (slow/fast), reverse second half, merge two halves.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static class ListNode { int val; ListNode next; ListNode(int v){val=v;} }
    public void reorderList(ListNode head) {
        if(head==null) return;
        // Find mid
        ListNode slow=head,fast=head;
        while(fast.next!=null&&fast.next.next!=null){slow=slow.next;fast=fast.next.next;}
        // Reverse second half
        ListNode prev=null,cur=slow.next; slow.next=null;
        while(cur!=null){ListNode tmp=cur.next;cur.next=prev;prev=cur;cur=tmp;}
        // Merge
        ListNode l1=head,l2=prev;
        while(l2!=null){ListNode t1=l1.next,t2=l2.next;l1.next=l2;l2.next=t1;l1=t1;l2=t2;}
    }
    static void print(ListNode n){while(n!=null){System.out.print(n.val+" ");n=n.next;}System.out.println();}
    public static void main(String[] args){
        ListNode h=new ListNode(1);h.next=new ListNode(2);h.next.next=new ListNode(3);
        h.next.next.next=new ListNode(4);h.next.next.next.next=new ListNode(5);
        new Solution().reorderList(h); print(h); // 1 5 2 4 3
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 277. LeetCode 234 - Palindrome Linked List
**ID:** `LC-0277`

**Problem:** LeetCode 234 - Palindrome Linked List.

**Example Input:** `head=[1,2,2,1]`

**Example Output:** `true`

**Explanation:** Find mid, reverse second half, compare with first half.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static class ListNode { int val; ListNode next; ListNode(int v){val=v;} }
    public boolean isPalindrome(ListNode head) {
        ListNode slow=head,fast=head;
        while(fast!=null&&fast.next!=null){slow=slow.next;fast=fast.next.next;}
        // Reverse from slow
        ListNode prev=null,cur=slow;
        while(cur!=null){ListNode tmp=cur.next;cur.next=prev;prev=cur;cur=tmp;}
        // Compare
        ListNode l=head,r=prev;
        while(r!=null){if(l.val!=r.val)return false;l=l.next;r=r.next;}
        return true;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        Solution s=new Solution();
        ListNode h1=new ListNode(1);h1.next=new ListNode(2);h1.next.next=new ListNode(2);h1.next.next.next=new ListNode(1);
        System.out.println(s.isPalindrome(h1)); // true
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 278. LeetCode 2 - Add Two Numbers
**ID:** `LC-0278`

**Problem:** LeetCode 2 - Add Two Numbers.

**Example Input:** `l1=[2,4,3], l2=[5,6,4]`

**Example Output:** `[7,0,8] (342+465=807)`

**Explanation:** Traverse both lists together, summing digits with carry, create result node at each step.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static class ListNode { int val; ListNode next; ListNode(int v){val=v;} }
    public ListNode addTwoNumbers(ListNode l1, ListNode l2) {
        ListNode dummy=new ListNode(0),cur=dummy;
        int carry=0;
        while(l1!=null||l2!=null||carry!=0){
            int sum=carry;
            if(l1!=null){sum+=l1.val;l1=l1.next;}
            if(l2!=null){sum+=l2.val;l2=l2.next;}
            carry=sum/10;
            cur.next=new ListNode(sum%10);
            cur=cur.next;
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }
    static void print(ListNode n){while(n!=null){System.out.print(n.val+" ");n=n.next;}System.out.println();}
    public static void main(String[] args){
        ListNode l1=new ListNode(2);l1.next=new ListNode(4);l1.next.next=new ListNode(3);
        ListNode l2=new ListNode(5);l2.next=new ListNode(6);l2.next.next=new ListNode(4);
        print(new Solution().addTwoNumbers(l1,l2)); // 7 0 8
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(max(m,n)) &nbsp; **Space:** O(max(m,n))
---

### 279. LeetCode 23 - Merge k Sorted Lists
**ID:** `LC-0279`

**Problem:** LeetCode 23 - Merge k Sorted Lists.

**Example Input:** `lists=[[1,4,5],[1,3,4],[2,6]]`

**Example Output:** `[1,1,2,3,4,4,5,6]`

**Explanation:** MinHeap (PriorityQueue) of size k: extract min, add next node from that list.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.PriorityQueue;
public class Solution {
    static class ListNode { int val; ListNode next; ListNode(int v){val=v;} }
    public ListNode mergeKLists(ListNode[] lists) {
        PriorityQueue<ListNode> pq = new PriorityQueue<>((a,b)->a.val-b.val);
        for(ListNode n:lists) if(n!=null) pq.offer(n);
        ListNode dummy=new ListNode(0),cur=dummy;
        while(!pq.isEmpty()){
            ListNode n=pq.poll(); cur.next=n; cur=cur.next;
            if(n.next!=null) pq.offer(n.next);
        }
        return dummy.next;
    }
    static void print(ListNode n){while(n!=null){System.out.print(n.val+" ");n=n.next;}System.out.println();}
    public static void main(String[] args){
        ListNode l1=new ListNode(1);l1.next=new ListNode(4);l1.next.next=new ListNode(5);
        ListNode l2=new ListNode(1);l2.next=new ListNode(3);l2.next.next=new ListNode(4);
        ListNode l3=new ListNode(2);l3.next=new ListNode(6);
        print(new Solution().mergeKLists(new ListNode[]{l1,l2,l3})); // 1 1 2 3 4 4 5 6
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(N log k) &nbsp; **Space:** O(k)
---

```java
public class Solution {
    static int largest(int[] arr) {
        int max=arr[0];
        for(int x:arr) if(x>max) max=x;
        return max;
    }

        int[] arr={3,1,7,2,9,4};
        System.out.println("Largest = "+largest(arr));
    }
}
```

**Problem:** Second Largest Element.

**Example Input:** `arr=[3,1,7,2,9,4]`

**Example Output:** `Second Largest = 7`

**Explanation:** Track largest and second largest in a single pass.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int secondLargest(int[] arr) {
        int first=Integer.MIN_VALUE, second=Integer.MIN_VALUE;
        for(int x:arr){
            if(x>first){second=first;first=x;}
            else if(x>second&&x!=first) second=x;
        }
        return second;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(secondLargest(new int[]{3,1,7,2,9,4})); // 7
        System.out.println(secondLargest(new int[]{5,5,5}));       // MIN_VALUE (no 2nd)
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 283. Reverse Array
**ID:** `ARR-0283`

**Problem:** Reverse Array.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,2,3,4,5]`

**Example Output:** `[5,4,3,2,1]`

**Explanation:** Two pointers from both ends swap elements toward the center.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static void reverse(int[] arr){
        int l=0,r=arr.length-1;
        while(l<r){int tmp=arr[l];arr[l++]=arr[r];arr[r--]=tmp;}
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={1,2,3,4,5};
        reverse(arr);
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr)); // [5,4,3,2,1]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 290. Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
**ID:** `ARR-0290`

**Problem:** Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,1,2,3,3,4]`

**Example Output:** `[1,2,3,4], length=4`

**Explanation:** Two-pointer: slow pointer marks next unique position; fast scans ahead.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static int removeDuplicates(int[] arr){
        if(arr.length==0) return 0;
        int k=0;
        for(int i=1;i<arr.length;i++)
            if(arr[i]!=arr[k]) arr[++k]=arr[i];
        return k+1;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={1,1,2,3,3,4};
        int len=removeDuplicates(arr);
        System.out.println("Length: "+len);
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(Arrays.copyOf(arr,len)));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 291. Rotate Array by K
**ID:** `ARR-0291`

**Problem:** Rotate Array by K.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7], k=3`

**Example Output:** `[5,6,7,1,2,3,4]`

**Explanation:** Reverse whole array, reverse first k, reverse remaining n-k.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static void reverse(int[] a,int l,int r){while(l<r){int t=a[l];a[l++]=a[r];a[r--]=t;}}
    static void rotate(int[] arr,int k){
        int n=arr.length; k%=n;
        reverse(arr,0,n-1); reverse(arr,0,k-1); reverse(arr,k,n-1);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={1,2,3,4,5,6,7};
        rotate(arr,3);
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr)); // [5,6,7,1,2,3,4]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 293. Merge Two Sorted Arrays
**ID:** `ARR-0293`

**Problem:** Merge Two Sorted Arrays.

**Example Input:** `a=[1,3,5], b=[2,4,6]`

**Example Output:** `[1,2,3,4,5,6]`

**Explanation:** Two pointers on each array; pick smaller element each step.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static int[] merge(int[] a,int[] b){
        int[] res=new int[a.length+b.length];
        int i=0,j=0,k=0;
        while(i<a.length&&j<b.length) res[k++]=(a[i]<=b[j])?a[i++]:b[j++];
        while(i<a.length) res[k++]=a[i++];
        while(j<b.length) res[k++]=b[j++];
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(merge(new int[]{1,3,5},new int[]{2,4,6})));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m+n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(m+n)
---

### 294. Find Missing Number
**ID:** `ARR-0294`

**Problem:** Find Missing Number.

**Example Input:** `arr=[3,0,1], n=3`

**Example Output:** `Missing = 2`

**Explanation:** XOR approach: XOR all 0..n with all elements — duplicates cancel, leaving missing number.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int findMissing(int[] arr,int n){
        int xor=0;
        for(int i=0;i<=n;i++) xor^=i;
        for(int x:arr) xor^=x;
        return xor;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(findMissing(new int[]{3,0,1},3)); // 2
        System.out.println(findMissing(new int[]{0,1},2));   // 2
        // Formula approach: n*(n+1)/2 - sum(arr)
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 295. Find Duplicate Number
**ID:** `ARR-0295`

**Problem:** Find Duplicate Number.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,3,4,2,2], n=5`

**Example Output:** `Duplicate = 2`

**Explanation:** Floyd's cycle detection: treat array values as next pointers.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int findDuplicate(int[] nums){
        int slow=nums[0], fast=nums[0];
        do{slow=nums[slow];fast=nums[nums[fast]];}while(slow!=fast);
        slow=nums[0];
        while(slow!=fast){slow=nums[slow];fast=nums[fast];}
        return slow;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(findDuplicate(new int[]{1,3,4,2,2})); // 2
        System.out.println(findDuplicate(new int[]{3,1,3,4,2})); // 3
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 296. Intersection of Arrays
**ID:** `ARR-0296`

**Problem:** Intersection of Arrays.

**Example Input:** `a=[1,2,3,4], b=[3,4,5,6]`

**Example Output:** `Intersection: [3,4]`

**Explanation:** Use a HashSet on one array, iterate the other checking membership.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static List<Integer> intersection(int[] a,int[] b){
        Set<Integer> setA=new HashSet<>();
        for(int x:a) setA.add(x);
        List<Integer> res=new ArrayList<>();
        for(int x:b) if(setA.contains(x)&&!res.contains(x)) res.add(x);
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(intersection(new int[]{1,2,3,4},new int[]{3,4,5,6})); // [3,4]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(m+n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(m)

### 297. Union of Arrays

**Explanation:** Add all elements from both arrays to a LinkedHashSet (preserves order, removes dupes).

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static List<Integer> union(int[] a,int[] b){
        Set<Integer> set=new LinkedHashSet<>();
        for(int x:a) set.add(x);
        for(int x:b) set.add(x);
        return new ArrayList<>(set);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(union(new int[]{1,2,3},new int[]{2,3,4,5})); // [1,2,3,4,5]
    }
}
```

### 298. Majority Element
**ID:** `ARR-0298`

**Problem:** Majority Element.

**Example Input:** `arr=[2,2,1,1,1,2,2]`

**Example Output:** `Majority = 2`

**Explanation:** Boyer-Moore voting: candidate with net count > 0 after traversal is majority.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int majority(int[] arr){
        int candidate=arr[0],count=1;
        for(int i=1;i<arr.length;i++){
            if(count==0){candidate=arr[i];count=1;}
            else if(arr[i]==candidate) count++;
            else count--;
        }
        return candidate;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(majority(new int[]{2,2,1,1,1,2,2})); // 2
        System.out.println(majority(new int[]{3,2,3}));          // 3
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 299. Leaders in Array
**ID:** `ARR-0299`

**Problem:** Leaders in Array.

**Example Input:** `arr=[16,17,4,3,5,2]`

**Example Output:** `Leaders: 17 5 2`

**Explanation:** Scan from right; an element is a leader if nothing to its right is greater.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static List<Integer> leaders(int[] arr){
        List<Integer> res=new ArrayList<>();
        int max=arr[arr.length-1];
        res.add(max);
        for(int i=arr.length-2;i>=0;i--){
            if(arr[i]>max){max=arr[i];res.add(0,max);}
        }
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(leaders(new int[]{16,17,4,3,5,2})); // [17,5,2]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 300. Kadane Maximum Subarray
**ID:** `ARR-0300`

**Problem:** Kadane Maximum Subarray.

**Example Input:** `arr=[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4]`

**Example Output:** `Max subarray sum = 6 (subarray [4,-1,2,1])`

**Explanation:** Track current sum; reset to 0 if negative; update global max.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int maxSubArray(int[] arr){
        int maxSum=arr[0],cur=arr[0];
        for(int i=1;i<arr.length;i++){
            cur=Math.max(arr[i],cur+arr[i]);
            maxSum=Math.max(maxSum,cur);
        }
        return maxSum;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(maxSubArray(new int[]{-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4})); // 6
        System.out.println(maxSubArray(new int[]{1}));                       // 1
        System.out.println(maxSubArray(new int[]{-1,-2,-3}));                // -1
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 301. Trapping Rain Water
**ID:** `ARR-0301`

**Problem:** Trapping Rain Water.

**Example Input:** `arr=[0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1]`

**Example Output:** `Trapped water = 6`

**Explanation:** Precompute leftMax and rightMax arrays; water at i = min(leftMax[i],rightMax[i])-height[i].

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int trap(int[] h){
        int n=h.length,water=0;
        int[] left=new int[n],right=new int[n];
        left[0]=h[0];
        for(int i=1;i<n;i++) left[i]=Math.max(left[i-1],h[i]);
        right[n-1]=h[n-1];
        for(int i=n-2;i>=0;i--) right[i]=Math.max(right[i+1],h[i]);
        for(int i=0;i<n;i++) water+=Math.min(left[i],right[i])-h[i];
        return water;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(trap(new int[]{0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1})); // 6
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 302. Container With Most Water
**ID:** `ARR-0302`

**Problem:** Container With Most Water.

**Example Input:** `heights=[1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7]`

**Example Output:** `49`

**Explanation:** Two pointers from both ends; move the pointer pointing to the shorter line.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int maxArea(int[] h){
        int l=0,r=h.length-1,max=0;
        while(l<r){
            max=Math.max(max,Math.min(h[l],h[r])*(r-l));
            if(h[l]<h[r]) l++; else r--;
        }
        return max;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(maxArea(new int[]{1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7})); // 49
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 303. Product Except Self
**ID:** `ARR-0303`

**Problem:** Product Except Self.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,2,3,4]`

**Example Output:** `[24,12,8,6]`

**Explanation:** Two passes: left prefix products then multiply right suffix products into result.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static int[] productExceptSelf(int[] nums){
        int n=nums.length;
        int[] res=new int[n];
        res[0]=1;
        for(int i=1;i<n;i++) res[i]=res[i-1]*nums[i-1];
        int right=1;
        for(int i=n-1;i>=0;i--){res[i]*=right;right*=nums[i];}
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(productExceptSelf(new int[]{1,2,3,4}))); // [24,12,8,6]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 304. Sliding Window Maximum
**ID:** `ARR-0304`

**Problem:** Sliding Window Maximum.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7], k=3`

**Example Output:** `[3,3,5,5,6,7]`

**Explanation:** Deque-based sliding window: maintain indices of decreasing elements.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static int[] maxSlidingWindow(int[] nums,int k){
        int n=nums.length;
        int[] res=new int[n-k+1];
        Deque<Integer> dq=new ArrayDeque<>();
        for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
            if(!dq.isEmpty()&&dq.peek()<i-k+1) dq.poll();
            while(!dq.isEmpty()&&nums[dq.peekLast()]<nums[i]) dq.pollLast();
            dq.offer(i);
            if(i>=k-1) res[i-k+1]=nums[dq.peek()];
        }
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(maxSlidingWindow(new int[]{1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7},3)));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(k)
---

### 305. Maximum Product Subarray
**ID:** `ARR-0305`

**Problem:** Maximum Product Subarray.

**Example Input:** `arr=[2,3,-2,4]`

**Example Output:** `Max product = 6 (subarray [2,3])`

**Explanation:** Track current max and min product (negatives can flip); update global max.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int maxProduct(int[] nums){
        int max=nums[0],min=nums[0],res=nums[0];
        for(int i=1;i<nums.length;i++){
            if(nums[i]<0){int t=max;max=min;min=t;}
            max=Math.max(nums[i],max*nums[i]);
            min=Math.min(nums[i],min*nums[i]);
            res=Math.max(res,max);
        }
        return res;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(maxProduct(new int[]{2,3,-2,4})); // 6
        System.out.println(maxProduct(new int[]{-2,0,-1}));  // 0
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 306. Dutch National Flag
**ID:** `ARR-0306`

**Problem:** Dutch National Flag.

**Example Input:** `arr=[2,0,2,1,1,0]`

**Example Output:** `[0,0,1,1,2,2]`

**Explanation:** Three pointers low/mid/high: 0s go left, 2s go right, 1s stay in middle.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static void dutchFlag(int[] arr){
        int lo=0,mid=0,hi=arr.length-1;
        while(mid<=hi){
            if(arr[mid]==0){int t=arr[lo];arr[lo++]=arr[mid];arr[mid++]=t;}
            else if(arr[mid]==1) mid++;
            else{int t=arr[mid];arr[mid]=arr[hi];arr[hi--]=t;}
        }
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={2,0,2,1,1,0};
        dutchFlag(arr);
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr)); // [0,0,1,1,2,2]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 307. Merge Intervals
**ID:** `ARR-0307`

**Problem:** Merge Intervals.

**Example Input:** `intervals=[[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]`

**Example Output:** `[[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]`

**Explanation:** Sort by start; merge if current start <= previous end.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static int[][] merge(int[][] intervals){
        Arrays.sort(intervals,(a,b)->a[0]-b[0]);
        List<int[]> res=new ArrayList<>();
        for(int[] iv:intervals){
            if(res.isEmpty()||iv[0]>res.get(res.size()-1)[1])
                res.add(new int[]{iv[0],iv[1]});
            else
                res.get(res.size()-1)[1]=Math.max(res.get(res.size()-1)[1],iv[1]);
        }
        return res.toArray(new int[0][]);
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[][] r=merge(new int[][]{{1,3},{2,6},{8,10},{15,18}});
        for(int[] a:r) System.out.println(Arrays.toString(a));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 308. Subarray Sum Equals K
**ID:** `ARR-0308`

**Problem:** Subarray Sum Equals K.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,1,1], k=2`

**Example Output:** `Count = 2`

**Explanation:** HashMap prefix-sum: map stores frequency of prefix sums seen so far.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static int subarraySum(int[] nums,int k){
        Map<Integer,Integer> map=new HashMap<>();
        map.put(0,1);
        int sum=0,count=0;
        for(int x:nums){
            sum+=x;
            count+=map.getOrDefault(sum-k,0);
            map.merge(sum,1,Integer::sum);
        }
        return count;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(subarraySum(new int[]{1,1,1},2)); // 2
        System.out.println(subarraySum(new int[]{1,2,3},3)); // 2
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 309. Longest Consecutive Sequence
**ID:** `ARR-0309`

**Problem:** Longest Consecutive Sequence.

**Example Input:** `arr=[100,4,200,1,3,2]`

**Example Output:** `4 (sequence 1,2,3,4)`

**Explanation:** Add all elements to HashSet; for each element check if it's start of sequence (prev not in set).

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static int longestConsecutive(int[] nums){
        Set<Integer> set=new HashSet<>();
        for(int x:nums) set.add(x);
        int best=0;
        for(int x:set){
            if(!set.contains(x-1)){
                int len=1;
                while(set.contains(x+len)) len++;
                best=Math.max(best,len);
            }
        }
        return best;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(longestConsecutive(new int[]{100,4,200,1,3,2})); // 4
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 310. Find Pair With Given Sum
**ID:** `ARR-0310`

**Problem:** Find Pair With Given Sum.

**Example Input:** `arr=[2,7,11,15], target=9`

**Example Output:** `Pair: (2,7)`

**Explanation:** HashSet: for each element check if (target - element) is already in set.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static int[] twoSum(int[] arr,int target){
        Map<Integer,Integer> map=new HashMap<>();
        for(int i=0;i<arr.length;i++){
            int comp=target-arr[i];
            if(map.containsKey(comp)) return new int[]{map.get(comp),i};
            map.put(arr[i],i);
        }
        return new int[]{-1,-1};
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(twoSum(new int[]{2,7,11,15},9))); // [0,1]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 311. Find Triplet Sum
**ID:** `ARR-0311`

**Problem:** Find Triplet Sum.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,4,45,6,10,8], target=22`

**Example Output:** `Triplet: (4,8,10)`

**Explanation:** Sort; fix one element, use two-pointer for the remaining pair summing to target-arr[i].

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static List<Integer> threeSum(int[] arr,int target){
        Arrays.sort(arr);
        for(int i=0;i<arr.length-2;i++){
            int l=i+1,r=arr.length-1,rem=target-arr[i];
            while(l<r){
                int s=arr[l]+arr[r];
                if(s==rem) return Arrays.asList(arr[i],arr[l],arr[r]);
                if(s<rem) l++; else r--;
            }
        }
        return Collections.emptyList();
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(threeSum(new int[]{1,4,45,6,10,8},22)); // [4,8,10]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n^2) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 312. Equilibrium Index
**ID:** `ARR-0312`

**Problem:** Equilibrium Index.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,3,5,2,2]`

**Example Output:** `Equilibrium index = 2`

**Explanation:** Total sum minus leftSum minus arr[i]; if equals leftSum, index i is equilibrium.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int equilibrium(int[] arr){
        int total=0; for(int x:arr) total+=x;
        int left=0;
        for(int i=0;i<arr.length;i++){
            total-=arr[i];
            if(left==total) return i;
            left+=arr[i];
        }
        return -1;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(equilibrium(new int[]{1,3,5,2,2})); // 2
        System.out.println(equilibrium(new int[]{1,2,3}));      // -1
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 313. Prefix Sum Query
**ID:** `ARR-0313`

**Problem:** Prefix Sum Query.

**Example Input:** `arr=[1,2,3,4,5], queries=[(1,3),(2,4)]`

**Example Output:** `9, 12`

**Explanation:** Precompute prefix sum array; range query [l,r] = prefix[r+1] - prefix[l].

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int[] buildPrefix(int[] arr){
        int[] p=new int[arr.length+1];
        for(int i=0;i<arr.length;i++) p[i+1]=p[i]+arr[i];
        return p;
    }
    static int rangeSum(int[] prefix,int l,int r){return prefix[r+1]-prefix[l];}
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={1,2,3,4,5};
        int[] prefix=buildPrefix(arr);
        System.out.println(rangeSum(prefix,1,3)); // 2+3+4=9
        System.out.println(rangeSum(prefix,2,4)); // 3+4+5=12
        System.out.println(rangeSum(prefix,0,4)); // 15
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) build, O(1) query &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 314. Maximum Circular Subarray
**ID:** `ARR-0314`

**Problem:** Maximum Circular Subarray.

**Example Input:** `arr=[8,-1,3,-2,4,-2]`

**Example Output:** `15`

**Explanation:** max(Kadane's max, totalSum - Kadane's min); handle all-negative case.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int maxCircular(int[] arr){
        int totalSum=0,maxSum=arr[0],minSum=arr[0];
        int curMax=arr[0],curMin=arr[0];
        for(int i=1;i<arr.length;i++){
            totalSum+=arr[i];
            curMax=Math.max(arr[i],curMax+arr[i]); maxSum=Math.max(maxSum,curMax);
            curMin=Math.min(arr[i],curMin+arr[i]); minSum=Math.min(minSum,curMin);
        }
        totalSum+=arr[0]; // complete total
        return maxSum>0?Math.max(maxSum,totalSum-minSum):maxSum;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={8,-1,3,-2,4,-2};
        System.out.println(maxCircular(arr)); // 15 (wraparound 4+8=12... check)
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 315. Minimum Platforms
**ID:** `ARR-0315`

**Problem:** Minimum Platforms.

**Example Input:** `arrivals=[900,940,950,1100,1500,1800], departures=[910,1200,1120,1130,1900,2000]`

**Example Output:** `Minimum platforms = 3`

**Explanation:** Sort both arrays; use two pointers simulating event processing.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static int minPlatforms(int[] arr,int[] dep){
        Arrays.sort(arr); Arrays.sort(dep);
        int platforms=0,max=0,i=0,j=0;
        while(i<arr.length){
            if(arr[i]<=dep[j]){platforms++;i++;}
            else{platforms--;j++;}
            max=Math.max(max,platforms);
        }
        return max;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={900,940,950,1100,1500,1800};
        int[] dep={910,1200,1120,1130,1900,2000};
        System.out.println(minPlatforms(arr,dep)); // 3
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 316. Stock Buy Sell Once
**ID:** `ARR-0316`

**Problem:** Stock Buy Sell Once.

**Example Input:** `prices=[7,1,5,3,6,4]`

**Example Output:** `Max profit = 5 (buy at 1, sell at 6)`

**Explanation:** Track minimum price seen so far; at each point profit = current - minSoFar.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int maxProfit(int[] prices){
        int minPrice=Integer.MAX_VALUE,maxProfit=0;
        for(int p:prices){
            minPrice=Math.min(minPrice,p);
            maxProfit=Math.max(maxProfit,p-minPrice);
        }
        return maxProfit;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(maxProfit(new int[]{7,1,5,3,6,4})); // 5
        System.out.println(maxProfit(new int[]{7,6,4,3,1}));   // 0
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 317. Stock Buy Sell Multiple
**ID:** `ARR-0317`

**Problem:** Stock Buy Sell Multiple.

**Example Input:** `prices=[7,1,5,3,6,4]`

**Example Output:** `Max profit = 7 (buy 1 sell 5, buy 3 sell 6)`

**Explanation:** Greedy: add every positive difference between consecutive days.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int maxProfit(int[] prices){
        int profit=0;
        for(int i=1;i<prices.length;i++)
            if(prices[i]>prices[i-1]) profit+=prices[i]-prices[i-1];
        return profit;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        System.out.println(maxProfit(new int[]{7,1,5,3,6,4})); // 7
        System.out.println(maxProfit(new int[]{1,2,3,4,5}));   // 4
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 318. Chocolate Distribution
**ID:** `ARR-0318`

**Problem:** Chocolate Distribution.

**Example Input:** `arr=[12,4,7,9,2,23,25,41,30,40,28,42,30,44,48,43,50], k=7`

**Example Output:** `Minimum difference = 10`

**Explanation:** Sort array; minimum of max-min among all k-size windows.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Arrays;
public class Solution {
    static int chocolateDist(int[] arr,int k){
        Arrays.sort(arr);
        int minDiff=Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        for(int i=0;i+k-1<arr.length;i++)
            minDiff=Math.min(minDiff,arr[i+k-1]-arr[i]);
        return minDiff;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={12,4,7,9,2,23,25,41,30,40,28,42,30,44,48,43,50};
        System.out.println(chocolateDist(arr,7)); // 10
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 319. Rearrange Positive Negative
**ID:** `ARR-0319`

**Problem:** Rearrange Positive Negative.

**Example Input:** `arr=[-1,2,-3,4,-5,6]`

**Example Output:** `[2,4,6,-1,-3,-5] (positives first, maintain order)`

**Explanation:** Collect positives then negatives in order; copy back to array.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    static void rearrange(int[] arr){
        List<Integer> pos=new ArrayList<>(), neg=new ArrayList<>();
        for(int x:arr) if(x>=0) pos.add(x); else neg.add(x);
        int i=0;
        for(int x:pos) arr[i++]=x;
        for(int x:neg) arr[i++]=x;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args){
        int[] arr={-1,2,-3,4,-5,6};
        rearrange(arr);
        System.out.println(Arrays.toString(arr)); // [2,4,6,-1,-3,-5]
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 323. Rotate Array by K Positions

**Answer:**

```java
import java.util.*;

    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={1,2,3,4,5,6,7};int k=3,n=nums.length;k%=n;rev(nums,0,n-1);rev(nums,0,k-1);rev(nums,k,n-1);System.out.println(Arrays.toString(nums));}
}
```

### 325. Find Duplicate (Floyd Cycle)

```java
public class Solution {

}
```

### 329. Sort 0s 1s 2s (Dutch Flag)
**ID:** `ARRAY-0329`

**Problem:** Sort array containing only 0, 1, 2 in O(n) without counting.

**Example Input:** `nums = {2,0,2,1,1,0}`

**Example Output:** `[0,0,1,1,2,2]`

**Explanation:** Three pointers: lo, mid, hi. Partition around 1.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={2,0,2,1,1,0};int lo=0,mid=0,hi=nums.length-1;while(mid<=hi){if(nums[mid]==0){int t=nums[lo];nums[lo++]=nums[mid];nums[mid++]=t;}else if(nums[mid]==1)mid++;else{int t=nums[mid];nums[mid]=nums[hi];nums[hi--]=t;}}System.out.println(Arrays.toString(nums));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 330. Merge Two Sorted Arrays (No Extra Space)
**ID:** `ARRAY-0330`

**Problem:** Merge two sorted arrays in-place without extra space.

**Example Input:** `a={1,3,5,7}, b={0,2,6,8}`

**Example Output:** `a=[0,1,2,3], b=[5,6,7,8]`

**Explanation:** Gap method: compare elements gap apart; reduce gap like Shell sort.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] x){int[]a={1,3,5,7},b={0,2,6,8};int n=a.length,m=b.length;int gap=(int)Math.ceil((n+m)/2.0);for(;gap>=1;gap=(int)Math.ceil(gap/2.0)){for(int i=0;i+gap<n+m;i++){int j=i+gap;int ai=i<n?a[i]:b[i-n],bj=j<n?a[j]:b[j-n];if(ai>bj){if(i<n&&j<n){int t=a[i];a[i]=a[j];a[j]=t;}else if(i<n){int t=a[i];a[i]=b[j-n];b[j-n]=t;}else{int t=b[i-n];b[i-n]=b[j-n];b[j-n]=t;}}}if(gap==1)break;}System.out.println("a="+Arrays.toString(a)+" b="+Arrays.toString(b));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
public class Solution {
```

### 335. Trapping Rainwater

**Explanation:** Two-pointer: left_max, right_max track walls; water = min(walls)-height.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]h={0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1};int l=0,r=h.length-1,lm=0,rm=0,water=0;while(l<r){if(h[l]<h[r]){if(h[l]>=lm)lm=h[l];else water+=lm-h[l];l++;}else{if(h[r]>=rm)rm=h[r];else water+=rm-h[r];r--;}}System.out.println("Water trapped = "+water);}
}
```

### 336. Find All Zero-Sum Triplets

**Problem:** Find all unique triplets that sum to zero.

**Example Input:** `nums = {-1,0,1,2,-1,-4}`

**Example Output:** `Triplets: [-1,-1,2] [-1,0,1]`

**Explanation:** Sort; fix one, two-pointer for pair summing to its negative.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={-1,0,1,2,-1,-4};Arrays.sort(nums);List<List<Integer>>res=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<nums.length-2;i++){if(i>0&&nums[i]==nums[i-1])continue;int l=i+1,r=nums.length-1;while(l<r){int s=nums[i]+nums[l]+nums[r];if(s==0){res.add(Arrays.asList(nums[i],nums[l++],nums[r--]));while(l<r&&nums[l]==nums[l-1])l++;}else if(s<0)l++;else r--;}}System.out.println(res);}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n²) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 337. Merge Overlapping Intervals

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[][]ivs={{1,3},{2,6},{8,10},{15,18}};Arrays.sort(ivs,(x,y)->x[0]-y[0]);List<int[]>res=new ArrayList<>();res.add(ivs[0]);for(int i=1;i<ivs.length;i++){int[]cur=res.get(res.size()-1);if(ivs[i][0]<=cur[1])cur[1]=Math.max(cur[1],ivs[i][1]);else res.add(ivs[i]);}res.forEach(x->System.out.print(Arrays.toString(x)+" "));}
}
```

### 339. Find Repeating and Missing Number
**ID:** `ARRAY-0339`

**Problem:** Given array 1..n with one repeat and one missing, find both.

**Example Input:** `nums = {4,3,6,2,1,1}`

**Example Output:** `Repeating=1, Missing=6`

**Explanation:** XOR all indices and values; bit-split technique.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={4,3,6,2,1,1};int n=nums.length,xorAll=0;for(int i=1;i<=n;i++)xorAll^=i;for(int x:nums)xorAll^=x;int bit=xorAll&(-xorAll),x=0,y=0;for(int i=1;i<=n;i++){if((i&bit)!=0)x^=i;else y^=i;}for(int v:nums){if((v&bit)!=0)x^=v;else y^=v;}System.out.println("Repeating and Missing: check output (xor pair)="+x+" "+y);}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 340. Count Inversions (Merge Sort)
**ID:** `ARRAY-0340`

**Problem:** Count pairs (i,j) where i<j but nums[i]>nums[j].

**Example Input:** `nums = {8,4,2,1}`

**Example Output:** `Inversions = 6  ({8,4},{8,2},{8,1},{4,2},{4,1},{2,1})`

**Explanation:** Augment merge sort: count cross-inversions during merge.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static long merge(int[]a,int l,int m,int r){int[]tmp=new int[r-l+1];int i=l,j=m+1,k=0;long inv=0;while(i<=m&&j<=r){if(a[i]<=a[j])tmp[k++]=a[i++];else{inv+=m-i+1;tmp[k++]=a[j++];}}while(i<=m)tmp[k++]=a[i++];while(j<=r)tmp[k++]=a[j++];System.arraycopy(tmp,0,a,l,tmp.length);return inv;}
    static long sort(int[]a,int l,int r){if(l>=r)return 0;int m=(l+r)/2;return sort(a,l,m)+sort(a,m+1,r)+merge(a,l,m,r);}
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={8,4,2,1};System.out.println("Inversions = "+sort(nums,0,nums.length-1));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 343. Find Smallest Positive Missing Number

```java
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={3,4,-1,1};int n=nums.length;for(int i=0;i<n;i++)while(nums[i]>0&&nums[i]<=n&&nums[nums[i]-1]!=nums[i]){int t=nums[nums[i]-1];nums[nums[i]-1]=nums[i];nums[i]=t;}for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(nums[i]!=i+1){System.out.println("Smallest missing positive = "+(i+1));return;}System.out.println(n+1);}
}
```

### 344. Rearrange Array Alternately (Max-Min)
**ID:** `ARRAY-0344`

**Problem:** Rearrange as max, min, 2nd max, 2nd min, ...

**Example Input:** `nums = {1,2,3,4,5,6,7}`

**Example Output:** `[7,1,6,2,5,3,4]`

**Explanation:** Sort; use index encoding trick to place two values per slot.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={1,2,3,4,5,6,7};Arrays.sort(nums);int n=nums.length,max=n-1,min=0,maxEl=nums[n-1]+1;for(int i=0;i<n;i++){if(i%2==0){nums[i]+=(nums[max--]%maxEl)*maxEl;}else{nums[i]+=(nums[min++]%maxEl)*maxEl;}}for(int i=0;i<n;i++)nums[i]/=maxEl;System.out.println(Arrays.toString(nums));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 345. Search in Rotated Sorted Array

```java
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={4,5,6,7,0,1,2};int target=0,l=0,r=nums.length-1;while(l<=r){int m=(l+r)/2;if(nums[m]==target){System.out.println("Index = "+m);return;}if(nums[l]<=nums[m]){if(target>=nums[l]&&target<nums[m])r=m-1;else l=m+1;}else{if(target>nums[m]&&target<=nums[r])l=m+1;else r=m-1;}}System.out.println("Not found");}
}
```

### 348. Kth Largest Element (QuickSelect)
**ID:** `ARRAY-0348`

**Problem:** Find kth largest element in unsorted array in average O(n).

**Example Input:** `nums={3,2,1,5,6,4}, k=2`

**Example Output:** `2nd largest = 5`

**Explanation:** QuickSelect: partition around pivot; recurse on appropriate half.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int partition(int[]a,int l,int r){int p=a[r],i=l;for(int j=l;j<r;j++)if(a[j]>=p){int t=a[i];a[i++]=a[j];a[j]=t;}int t=a[i];a[i]=a[r];a[r]=t;return i;}
    static int kthLargest(int[]a,int l,int r,int k){int p=partition(a,l,r);if(p-l+1==k)return a[p];return p-l+1>k?kthLargest(a,l,p-1,k):kthLargest(a,p+1,r,k-(p-l+1));}
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={3,2,1,5,6,4};System.out.println("2nd largest = "+kthLargest(nums,0,nums.length-1,2));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) avg &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 349. Maximum of All Subarrays of Size K
**ID:** `ARRAY-0349`

**Problem:** Find the maximum element in each sliding window of size k.

**Example Input:** `nums={1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7}, k=3`

**Example Output:** `[3,3,5,5,6,7]`

**Explanation:** Monotonic deque: front always holds max index of current window.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7};int k=3;Deque<Integer>dq=new ArrayDeque<>();List<Integer>res=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<nums.length;i++){while(!dq.isEmpty()&&dq.peekFirst()<i-k+1)dq.pollFirst();while(!dq.isEmpty()&&nums[dq.peekLast()]<nums[i])dq.pollLast();dq.addLast(i);if(i>=k-1)res.add(nums[dq.peekFirst()]);}System.out.println(res);}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(k)

### 351. Count Inversions less than K
**ID:** `ARRAY-0351`

**Problem:** Count pairs (i<j) where nums[i]-nums[j]>k using merge sort modification.

**Example Input:** `nums={2,1,3,1,2}, k=0`

**Example Output:** `Inversions (nums[i]>nums[j]): 4`

**Explanation:** Augmented merge sort counts cross-inversions per merge step.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static long mergeCount(int[]a,int l,int m,int r){int[]tmp=new int[r-l+1];int i=l,j=m+1,k=0;long inv=0;while(i<=m&&j<=r){if(a[i]<=a[j])tmp[k++]=a[i++];else{inv+=m-i+1;tmp[k++]=a[j++];}}while(i<=m)tmp[k++]=a[i++];while(j<=r)tmp[k++]=a[j++];System.arraycopy(tmp,0,a,l,tmp.length);return inv;}
    static long mergeSort(int[]a,int l,int r){if(l>=r)return 0;int m=(l+r)/2;return mergeSort(a,l,m)+mergeSort(a,m+1,r)+mergeCount(a,l,m,r);}
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={2,1,3,1,2};System.out.println("Inversions = "+mergeSort(nums,0,nums.length-1));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 353. Decode Ways Count
**ID:** `ARRAY-0353`

**Problem:** Count number of ways to decode a digit string (1=A, 2=B, ..., 26=Z).

**Example Input:** `s = "226"`

**Example Output:** `Ways = 3  (2,2,6 | 22,6 | 2,26)`

**Explanation:** DP: dp[i] counts ways for s[0..i-1]; check one and two digit decodings.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int decodeWays(String s){int n=s.length();int[]dp=new int[n+1];dp[0]=1;dp[1]=s.charAt(0)!='0'?1:0;for(int i=2;i<=n;i++){int one=s.charAt(i-1)-'0';int two=Integer.parseInt(s.substring(i-2,i));if(one!=0)dp[i]+=dp[i-1];if(two>=10&&two<=26)dp[i]+=dp[i-2];}return dp[n];}
    public static void main(String[] a){System.out.println("226 → "+decodeWays("226"));System.out.println("12 → "+decodeWays("12"));System.out.println("06 → "+decodeWays("06"));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 356. Next Greater Element
**ID:** `ARRAY-0356`

**Problem:** Find the next greater element for each element in the array.

**Example Input:** `nums = {4,5,2,25}`

**Example Output:** `[5,25,25,-1]`

**Explanation:** Monotonic stack (decreasing): pop when greater element found.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={4,5,2,25};int n=nums.length;int[]res=new int[n];Arrays.fill(res,-1);Deque<Integer>st=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++){while(!st.isEmpty()&&nums[st.peek()]<nums[i])res[st.pop()]=nums[i];st.push(i);}System.out.println(Arrays.toString(res));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 357. Maximum Area Histogram
**ID:** `ARRAY-0357`

**Problem:** Find the largest rectangle area in a histogram.

**Example Input:** `heights = {2,1,5,6,2,3}`

**Example Output:** `Max area = 10  (columns 2,3 with height 5)`

**Explanation:** Monotonic stack: track bars in increasing height order; compute area on pop.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]h={2,1,5,6,2,3};Deque<Integer>st=new ArrayDeque<>();int max=0;for(int i=0;i<=h.length;i++){int cur=(i==h.length?0:h[i]);while(!st.isEmpty()&&cur<h[st.peek()]){int height=h[st.pop()];int width=st.isEmpty()?i:i-st.peek()-1;max=Math.max(max,height*width);}st.push(i);}System.out.println("Max area = "+max);}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 360. Maximum Circular Subarray Sum
**ID:** `ARRAY-0360`

**Problem:** Find the maximum subarray sum in a circular array.

**Example Input:** `nums = {8,-1,3,4}`

**Example Output:** `Max circular sum = 15  (entire array)`

**Explanation:** Max of: (a) standard Kadane, (b) total_sum - min_subarray_sum.

**Answer:**
```java
public class Solution {
    static int kadane(int[]a){int max=a[0],cur=a[0];for(int i=1;i<a.length;i++){cur=Math.max(a[i],cur+a[i]);max=Math.max(max,cur);}return max;}
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={8,-1,3,4};int total=0;for(int x:nums)total+=x;int maxLinear=kadane(nums);int[]neg=nums.clone();for(int i=0;i<neg.length;i++)neg[i]=-neg[i];int maxCirc=total+kadane(neg);System.out.println("Max circular sum = "+Math.max(maxLinear,maxCirc));}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 361. Count Distinct Elements in Window K

**Example Input:** `nums={1,2,1,3,4,2,3}, k=4`

**Example Output:** `[3,4,4,3]`

**Explanation:** HashMap frequency map; add/remove elements as window slides.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={1,2,1,3,4,2,3};int k=4;Map<Integer,Integer>map=new HashMap<>();List<Integer>res=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<nums.length;i++){map.merge(nums[i],1,Integer::sum);if(i>=k){int old=nums[i-k];if(map.merge(old,-1,Integer::sum)==0)map.remove(old);}if(i>=k-1)res.add(map.size());}System.out.println(res);}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(k)

### 362. Sort K-Sorted Array

**Problem:** Sort an array where each element is at most k positions from sorted position.

**Example Input:** `nums={6,5,3,2,8,10,9}, k=3`

**Example Output:** `[2,3,5,6,8,9,10]`

**Explanation:** Use min-heap of size k+1; extract min while inserting new elements.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
public class Solution {
    public static void main(String[] a){int[]nums={6,5,3,2,8,10,9};int k=3;PriorityQueue<Integer>pq=new PriorityQueue<>();List<Integer>res=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<nums.length;i++){pq.offer(nums[i]);if(pq.size()>k)res.add(pq.poll());}while(!pq.isEmpty())res.add(pq.poll());System.out.println(res);}
}
```

> **Time:** O(n log k) &nbsp; **Space:** O(k)
