### 1721. Exactly Once Producer
**ID:** `KFK-1721`

**Problem:** Exactly Once Producer.

**Example Input:** produce and consume in same transaction

**Example Output:** no duplicates even if producer retries

**Explanation:** enable.idempotence=true; transactional.id; KafkaTransactionManager; @Transactional wraps produce+consume.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

@Service
public class ExactlyOnceService {
    private final KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafka;
    ExactlyOnceService(KafkaTemplate<String,String> k) { kafka=k; }

    @Transactional("kafkaTransactionManager")
    public void processAndPublish(String input, String outputTopic) {
        // Consume happens outside; this just publishes with exactly-once
        kafka.send("processed-orders", "key", input+"-processed");
        System.out.println("Published exactly-once: "+input);
        // If exception: transaction aborted; consumer offset not committed
    }
}
// application.properties:
// spring.kafka.producer.transaction-id-prefix=order-tx-
// spring.kafka.producer.enable-idempotence=true
// spring.kafka.producer.acks=all
// spring.kafka.producer.retries=3
// spring.kafka.consumer.isolation-level=read_committed
```

### 1722. Partition Key Ordering
**ID:** `KFK-1722`

**Problem:** Partition Key Ordering.

**Example Input:** orders for same customer published

**Example Output:** same customer orders in order; different customers parallel

**Explanation:** Messages with same key always go to same partition; within partition: strict ordering guaranteed.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class OrderedProducerService {
    private final KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafka;
    OrderedProducerService(KafkaTemplate<String,String> k) { kafka=k; }

    public void publishOrder(Long customerId, Long orderId, String item) {
        // Key = customerId -> all orders for same customer -> same partition -> ordered
        String key = "customer-"+customerId;
        String value = String.format("{"orderId":%d,"customerId":%d,"item":"%s"}", orderId, customerId, item);
        kafka.send("orders", key, value);
        System.out.println("Published: key="+key+" orderId="+orderId);
    }
}
// Hash(key) % numPartitions = partition assignment
// customer-1 -> partition 0 (always)
// customer-2 -> partition 1 (always)
// Orders within a partition are consumed in order
// Orders across partitions consumed in parallel
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1724. Kafka Error Handler
**ID:** `KFK-1724`

**Problem:** Kafka Error Handler.

**Example Input:** consumer throws exception

**Example Output:** error logged; offset committed; processing continues

**Explanation:** DefaultErrorHandler with BackOff; SeekToCurrentErrorHandler; custom error handling logic.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord;
import org.springframework.kafka.annotation.KafkaListener;
import org.springframework.kafka.config.ConcurrentKafkaListenerContainerFactory;
import org.springframework.kafka.listener.DefaultErrorHandler;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.util.backoff.FixedBackOff;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Configuration class KafkaErrorConfig {
    @Bean
    public DefaultErrorHandler errorHandler() {
        DefaultErrorHandler handler = new DefaultErrorHandler(
            (record, ex) -> System.err.println("Failed after retries: "+record.value()+" err="+ex.getMessage()),
            new FixedBackOff(1000L, 3)); // retry 3x with 1s delay
        handler.addNotRetryableExceptions(IllegalArgumentException.class);
        return handler;
    }
}

@Service
class ErrorHandlingConsumer {
    @KafkaListener(topics="orders", groupId="error-demo")
    public void consume(ConsumerRecord<String,String> record) {
        if (record.value().contains("invalid"))
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid message");
        System.out.println("Processed: "+record.value());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1725. Kafka Streams Word Count
**ID:** `KFK-1725`

**Problem:** Kafka Streams Word Count.

**Example Input:** stream of sentences

**Example Output:** running word count per word in stream

**Explanation:** KStream.flatMapValues().groupBy().count(); topology processes in real-time; KTable for aggregation.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.*;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.kstream.*;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import java.util.Arrays; import java.util.Properties;

@Configuration
public class WordCountTopology {
    @Bean
    public KStream<String,String> wordCountStream(StreamsBuilder builder) {
        KStream<String,String> input = builder.stream("text-input");
        KTable<String,Long> counts = input
            .flatMapValues(value -> Arrays.asList(value.toLowerCase().split("\\s+")))
            .groupBy((key, word) -> word, Grouped.with(Serdes.String(), Serdes.String()))
            .count(Materialized.as("word-counts"));
        counts.toStream().to("word-count-output", Produced.with(Serdes.String(), Serdes.Long()));
        return input;
    }
}
// application.properties:
// spring.kafka.streams.application-id=word-count-app
// spring.kafka.streams.default.key.serde=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes$StringSerde
// spring.kafka.streams.default.value.serde=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes$StringSerde
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(unique words)
---

**ID:** `KFK-1726`

**Example Output:** latest profile per userId always available

**Explanation:** Log compaction keeps latest value per key; old values deleted; topic as key-value store.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.*;
import org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class UserProfileService {
    private final KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafka;
    UserProfileService(KafkaTemplate<String,String> k) { kafka=k; }

    public void updateProfile(Long userId, String name, String email) {
        String key = "user-"+userId;
        String value = String.format("{"id":%d,"name":"%s","email":"%s"}", userId, name, email);
        kafka.send("user-profiles", key, value); // compacted topic
        System.out.println("Profile updated: "+key);
    }

    public void deleteProfile(Long userId) {
        // Tombstone: null value marks key for deletion in compacted topic
        kafka.send("user-profiles", "user-"+userId, null);
        System.out.println("Tombstone sent for user-"+userId);
    }
}
// Kafka topic config: cleanup.policy=compact, min.cleanable.dirty.ratio=0.1
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1729. Kafka Windowed Aggregation
**ID:** `KFK-1729`

**Problem:** Kafka Windowed Aggregation.

**Example Input:** order events stream

**Example Output:** count orders per 5-minute window

**Explanation:** Kafka Streams TimeWindows; windowedBy().count(); results keyed by windowed key.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Serdes;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.*;
import org.apache.kafka.streams.kstream.*;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import java.time.Duration;

@Configuration
public class WindowedAggregationTopology {
    @Bean
    public KStream<String,String> windowedCount(StreamsBuilder builder) {
        KStream<String,String> orders = builder.stream("orders",
            Consumed.with(Serdes.String(), Serdes.String()));
        orders
            .groupByKey()
            .windowedBy(TimeWindows.ofSizeWithNoGrace(Duration.ofMinutes(5)))
            .count(Materialized.as("orders-per-5min"))
            .toStream()
            .peek((k,v) -> System.out.printf("Window [%s] count=%d%n", k.window().startTime(), v))
            .to("order-counts", Produced.with(WindowedSerdes.timeWindowedSerdeFrom(String.class,5*60*1000), Serdes.Long()));
        return orders;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(window)
---

### 1730. Kafka Transactional Consumer
**ID:** `KFK-1730`

**Problem:** Kafka Transactional Consumer.

**Example Input:** read-process-produce in one transaction

**Example Output:** no duplicates; no lost messages

**Explanation:** Read committed isolation; consume offset and produce in same transaction; atomic commit.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.*;
import org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.*;
import org.apache.kafka.common.TopicPartition;
import org.springframework.kafka.annotation.KafkaListener;
import org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

@Service
public class TransactionalConsumerProducer {
    private final KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafka;
    TransactionalConsumerProducer(KafkaTemplate<String,String> k) { kafka=k; }

    @KafkaListener(topics="raw-orders", groupId="tx-consumer")
    @Transactional("kafkaTransactionManager")
    public void processAndForward(String message) {
        System.out.println("Processing: "+message);
        // Enrich message
        String enriched = message.replaceAll("\}", ","processed":true}");
        kafka.send("enriched-orders", enriched);
        System.out.println("Forwarded enriched message");
        // Both consumer offset commit and producer send are in same transaction
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1732. Kafka Replay Messages
**ID:** `KFK-1732`

**Problem:** Kafka Replay Messages.

**Example Input:** replay orders from offset 0

**Example Output:** all historical messages reprocessed

**Explanation:** Reset consumer group offsets with kafka-consumer-groups.sh or AdminClient; reprocess from start.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.admin.*;
import org.apache.kafka.common.TopicPartition;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.*; import java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException;

@Service
public class KafkaReplayService {
    private final AdminClient adminClient;
    KafkaReplayService(AdminClient a) { adminClient=a; }

    public void replayFromBeginning(String groupId, String topic) throws ExecutionException, InterruptedException {
        // 1. Get topic partitions
        TopicDescription desc = adminClient.describeTopics(List.of(topic)).all().get().get(topic);
        Map<TopicPartition, OffsetAndMetadata> offsets = new HashMap<>();
        desc.partitions().forEach(p ->
            offsets.put(new TopicPartition(topic, p.partition()), new OffsetAndMetadata(0L)));
        // 2. Reset offsets to 0
        adminClient.alterConsumerGroupOffsets(groupId, offsets).all().get();
        System.out.println("Offsets reset to 0 for group="+groupId+" topic="+topic);
        // 3. Restart consumer group to reprocess from beginning
    }
}
// CLI: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092
//   --group order-processor --topic orders --reset-offsets --to-earliest --execute
```

> **Time:** O(partitions) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1734. Kafka Topic Partitioning
**ID:** `KFK-1734`

**Problem:** Kafka Topic Partitioning.

**Example Input:** determine optimal partition count

**Example Output:** throughput target achieved; consumers matched

**Explanation:** Partitions = max consumers; more partitions = more parallelism; consider message ordering needs.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.admin.*;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.kafka.config.TopicBuilder;

@Configuration
public class KafkaTopicConfig {
    // Create topics with NewTopics (Spring Boot auto-creates if admin configured)
    @Bean NewTopic ordersTopic() {
        return TopicBuilder.name("orders")
            .partitions(6)      // 6 partitions = max 6 parallel consumers
            .replicas(3)        // 3 replicas = fault tolerant
            .config("retention.ms","604800000")   // 7 days
            .config("cleanup.policy","delete")
            .build();
    }
    @Bean NewTopic profilesTopic() {
        return TopicBuilder.name("user-profiles")
            .partitions(3).replicas(2)
            .config("cleanup.policy","compact")   // compacted topic
            .build();
    }
}
// Partition formula: throughput / (throughput per partition)
// e.g. 600 msg/s target, 100 msg/s per partition = 6 partitions
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1735. Kafka Consumer Pause Resume
**ID:** `KFK-1735`

**Problem:** Kafka Consumer Pause Resume.

**Example Input:** DB slow during batch processing

**Example Output:** consumer paused; resumes when ready

**Explanation:** MessageListenerContainer.pause/resume(); prevents consumer poll timeout; graceful flow control.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.common.TopicPartition;
import org.springframework.kafka.annotation.KafkaListener;
import org.springframework.kafka.config.KafkaListenerEndpointRegistry;
import org.springframework.kafka.listener.MessageListenerContainer;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.Set;

@Service
public class PauseResumeConsumer {
    private final KafkaListenerEndpointRegistry registry;
    PauseResumeConsumer(KafkaListenerEndpointRegistry r) { registry=r; }

    @KafkaListener(id="pausable", topics="orders", groupId="pause-demo")
    public void consume(String message) {
        System.out.println("Processing: "+message);
    }

    public void pause() {
        MessageListenerContainer container = registry.getListenerContainer("pausable");
        if (container != null) { container.pause(); System.out.println("Consumer paused"); }
    }

    public void resume() {
        MessageListenerContainer container = registry.getListenerContainer("pausable");
        if (container != null) { container.resume(); System.out.println("Consumer resumed"); }
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
public class KafkaHeaderService {
```

```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerRecord;
import org.apache.kafka.common.header.internals.RecordHeader;
import org.springframework.kafka.annotation.KafkaListener;
import org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class MultiTenantKafkaService {
    private final KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafka;
    MultiTenantKafkaService(KafkaTemplate<String,String> k) { kafka=k; }

    public void publishForTenant(String tenantId, String orderId, String event) {
        String topic = "orders." + tenantId.toLowerCase();
        ProducerRecord<String,String> record = new ProducerRecord<>(topic, orderId, event);
        record.headers().add(new RecordHeader("tenantId", tenantId.getBytes()));
        kafka.send(record);
        System.out.println("Published to tenant topic: "+topic);
    }

    @KafkaListener(topicPattern="orders\..*", groupId="multi-tenant-processor")
    public void consumeAllTenants(String message,
                                   @org.springframework.messaging.handler.annotation.Header(KafkaHeaders.RECEIVED_TOPIC) String topic) {
        String tenant = topic.split("\.")[1];
        System.out.println("Tenant="+tenant+" event="+message);
    }
}
```

### 1738. Kafka Exactly Once Semantics
**ID:** `KFK-1738`

**Problem:** Kafka Exactly Once Semantics.

**Example Input:** producer sends; broker restarts mid-send

**Example Output:** no duplicate messages in topic

**Explanation:** Idempotent producer: enable.idempotence=true; sequences deduplicated per PID+partition.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.kafka.core.*;
import org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerConfig;
import org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer;
import java.util.*;

@Configuration
public class IdempotentProducerConfig {
    @Bean
    public ProducerFactory<String,String> idempotentFactory() {
        Map<String,Object> props = new HashMap<>();
        props.put(ProducerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG,"localhost:9092");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.KEY_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringSerializer.class);
        props.put(ProducerConfig.VALUE_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringSerializer.class);
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE_CONFIG, true);  // key setting
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ACKS_CONFIG, "all");               // all replicas
        props.put(ProducerConfig.RETRIES_CONFIG, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        props.put(ProducerConfig.MAX_IN_FLIGHT_REQUESTS_PER_CONNECTION, 5);
        return new DefaultKafkaProducerFactory<>(props);
    }
    @Bean public KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafkaTemplate() {
        return new KafkaTemplate<>(idempotentFactory());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1742. Kafka Seek To Timestamp
**ID:** `KFK-1742`

**Problem:** Kafka Seek To Timestamp.

**Example Input:** seek consumer to 1 hour ago

**Example Output:** only messages from last hour processed

**Explanation:** ConsumerSeekAware.onPartitionsAssigned(); seekToTimestamp() resets offset by timestamp.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord;
import org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.OffsetAndTimestamp;
import org.apache.kafka.common.TopicPartition;
import org.springframework.kafka.annotation.KafkaListener;
import org.springframework.kafka.listener.ConsumerSeekAware;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Instant; import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import java.util.Map; import java.util.stream.Collectors;

@Service
public class TimestampSeekConsumer implements ConsumerSeekAware {
    @Override
    public void onPartitionsAssigned(Map<TopicPartition,Long> assignments, ConsumerSeekCallback callback) {
        long oneHourAgo = Instant.now().minus(1, ChronoUnit.HOURS).toEpochMilli();
        Map<TopicPartition,Long> timestampMap = assignments.keySet().stream()
            .collect(Collectors.toMap(tp -> tp, tp -> oneHourAgo));
        callback.seekToTimestamp(timestampMap.keySet(), oneHourAgo);
        System.out.println("Seeking to 1 hour ago for "+assignments.keySet().size()+" partitions");
    }

    @KafkaListener(topics="orders", groupId="seek-demo")
    public void consume(ConsumerRecord<String,String> record) {
        System.out.println("ts="+record.timestamp()+" val="+record.value());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(partitions) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

## Redis Caching Tasks


### 1745. Cache Aside Pattern
**ID:** `RDS-1745`

**Problem:** Cache Aside Pattern.

**Example Input:** GET /products/1 (cold cache)

**Example Output:** DB hit on miss; cached for next request

**Explanation:** Cache Aside: check cache first; on miss load from DB; store in cache; evict on update.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.cache.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration;

record Product(Long id, String name, double price) {}

@Service
public class CacheAsideService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    CacheAsideService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public Product getProduct(Long id) {
        String key = "product:"+id;
        String cached = redis.opsForValue().get(key);
        if (cached != null) {
            System.out.println("Cache HIT: "+id);
            return parseProduct(cached);
        }
        System.out.println("Cache MISS: loading from DB");
        Product product = loadFromDb(id);
        redis.opsForValue().set(key, toJson(product), Duration.ofMinutes(30));
        return product;
    }

    public void updateProduct(Long id, Product product) {
        saveToDb(id, product);
        redis.delete("product:"+id);  // invalidate cache
    }

    private Product loadFromDb(Long id) { return new Product(id, "Laptop", 999.0); }
    private void saveToDb(Long id, Product p) { System.out.println("DB saved: "+id); }
    private String toJson(Product p) { return "{"id":"+p.id()+","name":""+p.name()+""}"; }
    private Product parseProduct(String json) { return new Product(1L,"Laptop",999.0); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 1746. Redis TTL Cache
**ID:** `RDS-1746`

**Problem:** Redis TTL Cache.

**Example Input:** cache set with 60s TTL

**Example Output:** key auto-expires; no stale data

**Explanation:** EXPIRE or SET PX; @Cacheable(cacheNames, unless); Spring Cache with RedisCacheConfiguration TTL.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.cache.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.cache.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.RedisConnectionFactory;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration; import java.util.*;

@Configuration @EnableCaching
class RedisCacheConfig {
    @Bean CacheManager cacheManager(RedisConnectionFactory cf) {
        RedisCacheConfiguration config = RedisCacheConfiguration.defaultCacheConfig()
            .entryTtl(Duration.ofSeconds(60))
            .disableCachingNullValues();
        Map<String, RedisCacheConfiguration> configs = Map.of(
            "products", config.entryTtl(Duration.ofMinutes(30)),
            "sessions", config.entryTtl(Duration.ofHours(2))
        );
        return RedisCacheManager.builder(cf).cacheDefaults(config).withInitialCacheConfigurations(configs).build();
    }
}

@Service class ProductCacheService {
    @Cacheable(value="products", key="#id")
    public String getProduct(Long id) {
        System.out.println("DB query for "+id);
        return "Product-"+id;
    }
    @CacheEvict(value="products", key="#id")
    public void update(Long id) { System.out.println("Cache evicted for "+id); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 1747. Distributed Lock
**ID:** `RDS-1747`

**Problem:** Distributed Lock.

**Example Input:** two services try to update same inventory simultaneously

**Example Output:** only one gets lock; other waits or fails

**Explanation:** Redisson RLock: tryLock with timeout; auto-expire on crash; reentrant; fair lock option.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.redisson.api.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;

@Service
public class InventoryLockService {
    private final RedissonClient redisson;
    InventoryLockService(RedissonClient r) { redisson=r; }

    public boolean deductStock(String productId, int qty) {
        RLock lock = redisson.getLock("lock:inventory:"+productId);
        boolean acquired = false;
        try {
            acquired = lock.tryLock(5, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS); // wait 5s, expire in 30s
            if (!acquired) { System.out.println("Could not acquire lock for "+productId); return false; }
            System.out.println("Lock acquired for "+productId);
            int current = getCurrentStock(productId);
            if (current < qty) { System.out.println("Insufficient stock"); return false; }
            updateStock(productId, current - qty);
            return true;
        } catch (InterruptedException e) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); return false; }
        finally { if (acquired && lock.isHeldByCurrentThread()) lock.unlock(); }
    }
    private int getCurrentStock(String id) { return 100; }
    private void updateStock(String id, int qty) { System.out.println("Stock updated: "+id+" = "+qty); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1748. Rate Limiter
**ID:** `RDS-1748`

**Problem:** Rate Limiter.

**Example Input:** API called 200x in 1 minute; limit is 100

**Example Output:** first 100 pass; rest rejected with 429

**Explanation:** Token bucket in Redis: INCR with EXPIRE per window; Redisson RRateLimiter; Lua atomic script.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration;

@Service
public class RedisRateLimiter {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    RedisRateLimiter(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public boolean isAllowed(String apiKey, int maxRequests, Duration window) {
        String key = "rate:"+apiKey+":"+windowBucket(window);
        Long count = redis.opsForValue().increment(key);
        if (count == 1) redis.expire(key, window);
        if (count <= maxRequests) {
            System.out.println("API key "+apiKey+" req #"+count+" ALLOWED");
            return true;
        }
        System.out.println("API key "+apiKey+" req #"+count+" BLOCKED (limit "+maxRequests+")");
        return false;
    }

    private String windowBucket(Duration window) {
        long epochSeconds = System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000;
        long windowSeconds = window.toSeconds();
        return String.valueOf((epochSeconds / windowSeconds) * windowSeconds);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(keys)
---

```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.security.SecureRandom; import java.time.Duration;

@Service
public class OtpService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    private final SecureRandom random = new SecureRandom();
    OtpService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public String generateOtp(String phone) {
        String otp = String.format("%06d", random.nextInt(1_000_000));
        String key = "otp:"+phone;
        Boolean set = redis.opsForValue().setIfAbsent(key, otp, Duration.ofMinutes(5));
        if (Boolean.FALSE.equals(set)) throw new IllegalStateException("OTP already sent; wait before retry");
        System.out.println("OTP generated for "+phone+" (demo: "+otp+")");
        return otp;
    }

    public boolean verifyOtp(String phone, String inputOtp) {
        String key = "otp:"+phone;
        String stored = redis.opsForValue().get(key);
        if (stored == null) { System.out.println("OTP expired or not found"); return false; }
        if (stored.equals(inputOtp)) {
            redis.delete(key); // use-once
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1750. Session Management

**Example Output:** any pod reads session; stateless service

**Explanation:** Spring Session with Redis: @EnableRedisHttpSession; session replicated; sticky session not needed.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.session.data.redis.config.annotation.web.http.*;
import org.springframework.session.*;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpSession;

@Configuration
@EnableRedisHttpSession(maxInactiveIntervalInSeconds=1800) // 30 min
class SessionConfig {}

@RestController class SessionController {
    @PostMapping("/login")
    public String login(@RequestParam String user, HttpSession session) {
        session.setAttribute("user", user);
        session.setAttribute("loginTime", System.currentTimeMillis());
        System.out.println("Session created: "+session.getId()+" for "+user);
        return "Logged in. SessionId="+session.getId();
    }
    @GetMapping("/profile")
    public String profile(HttpSession session) {
        String user = (String) session.getAttribute("user");
        if (user == null) return "401 Unauthorized";
        return "Hello "+user+" (session="+session.getId()+")";
    }
    @PostMapping("/logout")
    public String logout(HttpSession session) { session.invalidate(); return "Logged out"; }
}
// application.properties: spring.session.store-type=redis
```

### 1751. Leaderboard
**ID:** `RDS-1751`

**Problem:** Leaderboard.

**Example Input:** player scores submitted

**Example Output:** top 10 players returned in rank order

**Explanation:** Redis Sorted Set: ZADD scores player; ZREVRANGE 0 9 WITHSCORES; O(log n) insert.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.ZSetOperations;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.Set;

@Service
public class LeaderboardService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    private static final String KEY = "leaderboard:global";
    LeaderboardService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void addScore(String player, double score) {
        redis.opsForZSet().add(KEY, player, score);
        System.out.println("Score added: "+player+" = "+score);
    }

    public void incrementScore(String player, double delta) {
        redis.opsForZSet().incrementScore(KEY, player, delta);
    }

    public Set<ZSetOperations.TypedTuple<String>> getTopN(int n) {
        Set<ZSetOperations.TypedTuple<String>> top = redis.opsForZSet().reverseRangeWithScores(KEY, 0, n-1);
        int rank = 1;
        for (ZSetOperations.TypedTuple<String> entry : top)
            System.out.printf("#%d %s = %.0f%n", rank++, entry.getValue(), entry.getScore());
        return top;
    }

    public Long getRank(String player) {
        Long rank = redis.opsForZSet().reverseRank(KEY, player);
        return rank != null ? rank + 1 : null; // 1-based
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 1752. Cache Eviction Demo
**ID:** `RDS-1752`

**Problem:** Cache Eviction Demo.

**Example Input:** Redis maxmemory reached

**Example Output:** LRU evicts least-recently-used keys

**Explanation:** Redis maxmemory-policy: allkeys-lru, volatile-lru, allkeys-lfu; configure per use-case.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration;

@Service
public class CacheEvictionDemo {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    CacheEvictionDemo(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void demonstrateEvictionPolicies() {
        // volatile-lru: evict LRU keys with TTL set
        // allkeys-lru: evict LRU from all keys (no TTL needed)
        // allkeys-lfu: evict least-frequently-used (Redis 4+)
        // noeviction: return error when full (default)

        // Set keys with TTL (eligible for volatile-lru)
        redis.opsForValue().set("product:1","data1", Duration.ofMinutes(10));
        redis.opsForValue().set("product:2","data2", Duration.ofMinutes(5));

        // Access product:1 -> makes it "recently used"; product:2 evicted first
        redis.opsForValue().get("product:1");

        System.out.println("product:1 recently used; will survive LRU longer");
    }
}
// redis.conf:
// maxmemory 256mb
// maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
// maxmemory-samples 5  (LRU approximation sample size)
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(maxmemory)
---

### 1753. Write Through Cache
**ID:** `RDS-1753`

**Problem:** Write Through Cache.

**Example Input:** product updated in service

**Example Output:** both DB and cache updated atomically

**Explanation:** Write Through: update DB then cache (or cache first); ensures consistency; slightly slower writes.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import java.time.Duration;

@Service
public class WriteThroughService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    WriteThroughService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    @Transactional
    public void updateProduct(Long id, String name, double price) {
        // Step 1: Write to DB
        saveToDatabase(id, name, price);
        // Step 2: Write through to cache (same transaction for consistency)
        String key = "product:"+id;
        String json = String.format("{"id":%d,"name":"%s","price":%.2f}", id, name, price);
        redis.opsForValue().set(key, json, Duration.ofMinutes(30));
        System.out.println("Write-through: DB and cache updated for "+id);
    }

    public String readProduct(Long id) {
        String cached = redis.opsForValue().get("product:"+id);
        if (cached != null) return cached;
        return loadFromDatabase(id);
    }

    private void saveToDatabase(Long id, String name, double price) { System.out.println("DB saved: "+id); }
    private String loadFromDatabase(Long id) { return "{"id":"+id+"}"; }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

```java
@Service
public class ProductCacheInvalidationService {

    public String getProduct(Long id) {
        System.out.println("Loading from DB: "+id);
        return "product-"+id+"-data";
    }

    @CacheEvict(value="products", key="#id")
    public void updateProduct(Long id, String newData) {
        System.out.println("DB updated, cache evicted for: "+id);
        saveToDb(id, newData);
    }

    @CacheEvict(value="products", allEntries=true)
    public void clearAllProducts() {
        System.out.println("All product cache cleared");
    }

    @Caching(evict={
        @CacheEvict(value="products", key="#id"),
        @CacheEvict(value="productList", allEntries=true)
    })
    public void deleteProduct(Long id) {
        System.out.println("Product deleted, caches evicted: "+id);
    }

    private void saveToDb(Long id, String data) {}
}
```

```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.RedisConnectionFactory;
import org.springframework.data.redis.listener.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.listener.adapter.MessageListenerAdapter;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Configuration
class RedisPubSubConfig {
    @Bean MessageListenerAdapter adapter(NotificationSubscriber s) {
        return new MessageListenerAdapter(s, "onMessage");
    }
    @Bean RedisMessageListenerContainer container(RedisConnectionFactory cf, MessageListenerAdapter a) {
        RedisMessageListenerContainer c = new RedisMessageListenerContainer();
        c.setConnectionFactory(cf);
        c.addMessageListener(a, new ChannelTopic("notifications"));
        return c;
    }
}

@Service class NotificationSubscriber {
    public void onMessage(String message) { System.out.println("Received: "+message); }
}

@Service class NotificationPublisher {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    NotificationPublisher(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }
    public void publish(String message) { redis.convertAndSend("notifications", message); }
}
```

### 1756. Redis Pipeline
**ID:** `RDS-1756`

**Problem:** Redis Pipeline.

**Example Input:** batch 1000 GET operations

**Example Output:** single roundtrip; 10x faster than individual calls

**Explanation:** RedisTemplate executePipelined(); groups commands; single network trip; dramatically reduces latency.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.List;

@Service
public class RedisPipelineService {
    private final RedisTemplate<String,String> redis;
    RedisPipelineService(RedisTemplate<String,String> r) { redis=r; }

    public List<Object> batchGet(List<String> keys) {
        return redis.executePipelined((RedisCallback<Object>) conn -> {
            keys.forEach(key -> conn.stringCommands().get(key.getBytes()));
            return null; // null because pipeline collects results
        });
    }

    public void batchSet(java.util.Map<String,String> entries) {
        redis.executePipelined((RedisCallback<Object>) conn -> {
            entries.forEach((k,v) -> conn.stringCommands().set(k.getBytes(), v.getBytes()));
            return null;
        });
        System.out.println("Pipeline set "+entries.size()+" keys");
    }
}
// Without pipeline: n network roundtrips
// With pipeline:    1 network roundtrip for all n commands
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 1757. Redis Lua Script
**ID:** `RDS-1757`

**Problem:** Redis Lua Script.

**Example Input:** check stock and reserve atomically

**Example Output:** no race condition; script runs atomically

**Explanation:** EVAL script; Lua runs atomically in Redis; solves check-then-act race condition.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.script.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.List;

@Service
public class LuaScriptService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    LuaScriptService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    private static final String RESERVE_SCRIPT =
        "local stock = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1])) " +
        "if not stock then return -1 end " +
        "if stock < tonumber(ARGV[1]) then return 0 end " +
        "redis.call('DECRBY', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) " +
        "return 1";

    public int reserveStock(String productId, int qty) {
        DefaultRedisScript<Long> script = new DefaultRedisScript<>();
        script.setScriptText(RESERVE_SCRIPT);
        script.setResultType(Long.class);
        Long result = redis.execute(script, List.of("stock:"+productId), String.valueOf(qty));
        if (result == null || result == -1) { System.out.println("Stock key missing"); return -1; }
        if (result == 0) { System.out.println("Insufficient stock"); return 0; }
        System.out.println("Reserved "+qty+" of "+productId); return 1;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1758. Redis HyperLogLog
**ID:** `RDS-1758`

**Problem:** Redis HyperLogLog.

**Example Input:** count unique visitors per page

**Example Output:** approximate unique count; minimal memory

**Explanation:** PFADD adds elements; PFCOUNT returns approximate cardinality; uses ~12KB regardless of data size.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class UniqueVisitorService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    UniqueVisitorService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void trackVisit(String pageId, String userId) {
        redis.opsForHyperLogLog().add("visitors:"+pageId, userId);
    }

    public long getUniqueCount(String pageId) {
        long count = redis.opsForHyperLogLog().size("visitors:"+pageId);
        System.out.println("Unique visitors for "+pageId+": "+count+" (±0.81% error)");
        return count;
    }

    public long mergeAndCount(String... pageIds) {
        String[] sourceKeys = new String[pageIds.length];
        for (int i=0; i<pageIds.length; i++) sourceKeys[i]="visitors:"+pageIds[i];
        redis.opsForHyperLogLog().union("visitors:all", sourceKeys);
        return redis.opsForHyperLogLog().size("visitors:all");
    }
}
// HyperLogLog: O(1) space regardless of cardinality
// Accuracy: ~0.81% standard error
// Max 12KB per HyperLogLog key
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1759. Redis Bloom Filter
**ID:** `RDS-1759`

**Problem:** Redis Bloom Filter.

**Example Input:** check if product ID already processed

**Example Output:** false positives possible; no false negatives

**Explanation:** Bloom filter: space-efficient probabilistic set; EXIST check before DB lookup; Redisson RBloomFilter.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.redisson.api.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class BloomFilterService {
    private final RedissonClient redisson;
    BloomFilterService(RedissonClient r) { redisson=r; }

    public void initialize() {
        RBloomFilter<String> filter = redisson.getBloomFilter("processed-orders");
        filter.tryInit(1_000_000L, 0.01); // 1M items, 1% false positive rate
        System.out.println("Bloom filter initialized");
    }

    public void markProcessed(String orderId) {
        redisson.<String>getBloomFilter("processed-orders").add(orderId);
    }

    public boolean mightBeProcessed(String orderId) {
        boolean exists = redisson.<String>getBloomFilter("processed-orders").contains(orderId);
        if (exists) System.out.println("Might be processed: "+orderId+" (check DB to confirm)");
        else System.out.println("Definitely NOT processed: "+orderId);
        return exists;
    }
}
// False positive: bloom says "seen" but wasn't -> verify in DB
// False negative: impossible (bloom never misses a "seen" item)
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
import org.springframework.data.geo.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.RedisGeoCommands.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.GeoOperations;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.data.redis.domain.geo.GeoReference;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.List;

@Service
public class GeoSearchService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    GeoSearchService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void addRestaurant(String name, double lon, double lat) {
        redis.opsForGeo().add("restaurants", new Point(lon, lat), name);
    }

        Circle within = new Circle(new Point(lon, lat), new Distance(km, Metrics.KILOMETERS));
        GeoResults<GeoLocation<String>> results = redis.opsForGeo()
            .radius("restaurants", within,

        return results.getContent();
    }

    }
}
```

### 1761. Redis Stream
**ID:** `RDS-1761`

**Problem:** Redis Stream.

**Example Input:** event stream with consumer groups

**Example Output:** each consumer processes subset; events persisted

**Explanation:** XADD publishes; XREADGROUP reads; XACK acknowledges; persistent ordered event log.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.stream.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration; import java.util.*;

@Service
public class RedisStreamService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    RedisStreamService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public RecordId publish(String streamKey, Map<String,String> fields) {
        RecordId id = redis.opsForStream().add(MapRecord.create(streamKey, fields));
        System.out.println("Published to "+streamKey+" id="+id);
        return id;
    }

    public void createConsumerGroup(String stream, String group) {
        try {
            redis.opsForStream().createGroup(stream, ReadOffset.from("0"), group);
        } catch (Exception e) { System.out.println("Group exists: "+group); }
    }

    public List<MapRecord<String,Object,Object>> read(String stream, String group, String consumer, int count) {
        return redis.opsForStream().read(
            Consumer.from(group, consumer),
            StreamReadOptions.empty().count(count).block(Duration.ofSeconds(2)),
            StreamOffset.create(stream, ReadOffset.lastConsumed()));
    }

    public void ack(String stream, String group, RecordId recordId) {
        redis.opsForStream().acknowledge(stream, group, recordId);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 1762. Redis Sentinel High Availability
**ID:** `RDS-1762`

**Problem:** Redis Sentinel High Availability.

**Example Input:** primary Redis fails

**Example Output:** sentinel promotes replica; no downtime

**Explanation:** Redis Sentinel monitors; auto-failover; clients connect to sentinel for primary discovery.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.lettuce.LettuceConnectionFactory;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;

@Configuration
public class RedisSentinelConfig {
    @Bean LettuceConnectionFactory connectionFactory() {
        RedisSentinelConfiguration sentinel = new RedisSentinelConfiguration()
            .master("mymaster")
            .sentinel("sentinel1", 26379)
            .sentinel("sentinel2", 26380)
            .sentinel("sentinel3", 26381);
        sentinel.setPassword(RedisPassword.of("redispassword"));
        return new LettuceConnectionFactory(sentinel);
    }
    @Bean StringRedisTemplate redisTemplate(LettuceConnectionFactory cf) {
        return new StringRedisTemplate(cf);
    }
}
// Redis Sentinel topology:
// - 1 primary + 2 replicas (replication)
// - 3 sentinel processes (quorum monitoring)
// - quorum=2: 2 sentinels must agree on failure
// - After failover: sentinel updates config; clients reconnect to new primary
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1763. Redis Cluster Sharding
**ID:** `RDS-1763`

**Problem:** Redis Cluster Sharding.

**Example Input:** 10M keys stored across 6 nodes

**Example Output:** keys distributed; no single node bottleneck

**Explanation:** Redis Cluster: 16384 hash slots; CRC16(key) % 16384 selects slot; 3 primary + 3 replica nodes.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.lettuce.LettuceConnectionFactory;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import java.util.List;

@Configuration
public class RedisClusterConfig {
    @Bean LettuceConnectionFactory clusterFactory() {
        RedisClusterConfiguration cluster = new RedisClusterConfiguration(List.of(
            "node1:7000", "node2:7001", "node3:7002",
            "node4:7003", "node5:7004", "node6:7005"));
        cluster.setMaxRedirects(3);
        return new LettuceConnectionFactory(cluster);
    }
    @Bean StringRedisTemplate redisTemplate(LettuceConnectionFactory cf) {
        return new StringRedisTemplate(cf);
    }
}
// Hash tags: {userId}:profile and {userId}:settings -> same slot (same {userId})
// Without hash tags: keys may go to different slots
// CRC16("user:1001") % 16384 = slot 8765 -> node 2
// Data spreads automatically; resharding possible online
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(keys)

```java
import org.springframework.boot.ApplicationRunner;

class CacheWarmingConfig {

    }

@Service class CacheWarmupService {

        List<String> hotProducts = loadHotProductsFromDb();
        hotProducts.forEach(product -> {
            String id = product.split(":")[0];
            redis.opsForValue().set("product:"+id, product, Duration.ofHours(1));
        });
        System.out.println("Cache warmed with "+hotProducts.size()+" items");
    }

    private List<String> loadHotProductsFromDb() {
        return List.of("1:{"name":"Laptop"}", "2:{"name":"Phone"}", "3:{"name":"Tablet"}");

}
```

### 1765. Redis JSON Storage
**ID:** `RDS-1765`

**Problem:** Redis JSON Storage.

**Example Input:** store and query complex JSON

**Example Output:** field-level get/set without full deserialization

**Explanation:** RedisJSON module: JSON.SET, JSON.GET, JSON.MGET; path-based queries; atomic field updates.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import java.time.Duration;

@Service
public class RedisJsonService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
    RedisJsonService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void saveUser(Long id, Object user) throws Exception {
        String key = "user:json:"+id;
        redis.opsForValue().set(key, mapper.writeValueAsString(user), Duration.ofHours(1));
    }

    public <T> T getUser(Long id, Class<T> type) throws Exception {
        String json = redis.opsForValue().get("user:json:"+id);
        return json != null ? mapper.readValue(json, type) : null;
    }

    public void updateField(Long id, String field, String value) throws Exception {
        String key = "user:json:"+id;
        String json = redis.opsForValue().get(key);
        if (json != null) {
            java.util.Map<String,Object> map = mapper.readValue(json, java.util.Map.class);
            map.put(field, value);
            redis.opsForValue().set(key, mapper.writeValueAsString(map), Duration.ofHours(1));
        }
    }
}
// For native RedisJSON: use Jedis/Lettuce with JSON.SET path $ ...
// Dependency: redis-modules or Lettuce RedisJSON extension
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(json_size)

### 1766. Redis Counter Atomic
**ID:** `RDS-1766`

**Problem:** Redis Counter Atomic.

**Example Input:** concurrent requests increment view count

**Example Output:** exact count; no race condition

**Explanation:** INCR/INCRBY atomic; GET after INCR reads latest; MULTI/EXEC for transactional counter reset.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration;

@Service
public class AtomicCounterService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    AtomicCounterService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public long incrementPageView(String pageId) {
        String key = "views:"+pageId;
        Long count = redis.opsForValue().increment(key);
        System.out.println("Page "+pageId+" views: "+count);
        return count != null ? count : 0;
    }

    public long incrementWithTtl(String key, long expireSeconds) {
        Long count = redis.opsForValue().increment(key);
        if (count != null && count == 1) redis.expire(key, Duration.ofSeconds(expireSeconds));
        return count != null ? count : 0;
    }

    public long getDailyCount(String feature) {
        String key = feature+":"+java.time.LocalDate.now();
        return incrementWithTtl(key, 86400); // expire in 1 day
    }

    public long getAndReset(String key) {
        Long val = (Long) redis.execute(
            (org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisCallback<Object>) conn ->
                conn.stringCommands().getSet(key.getBytes(), "0".getBytes()));
        return val != null ? val : 0;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1767. Redis Queue FIFO
**ID:** `RDS-1767`

**Problem:** Redis Queue FIFO.

**Example Input:** tasks pushed; workers pop

**Example Output:** tasks processed in order; reliable queue

**Explanation:** LPUSH + BRPOP; BRPOP blocks until item available; RPOPLPUSH for reliable queue pattern.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Async;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Duration; import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;

@Service
public class RedisQueueService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    private static final String QUEUE = "task:queue";
    private static final String PROCESSING = "task:processing";
    RedisQueueService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void enqueue(String task) {
        redis.opsForList().leftPush(QUEUE, task);
        System.out.println("Enqueued: "+task+" size="+redis.opsForList().size(QUEUE));
    }

    public String dequeue(int timeoutSec) {
        String task = redis.opsForList().rightPopAndLeftPush(QUEUE, PROCESSING); // reliable
        if (task != null) System.out.println("Processing: "+task);
        return task;
    }

    public void acknowledge(String task) {
        redis.opsForList().remove(PROCESSING, 1, task);
        System.out.println("Acknowledged: "+task);
    }

    public Long queueSize() { return redis.opsForList().size(QUEUE); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)
---

### 1768. Redis Bit Operations
**ID:** `RDS-1768`

**Problem:** Redis Bit Operations.

**Example Input:** track daily login per user

**Example Output:** bitmap indicates which users logged in today

**Explanation:** SETBIT/GETBIT per user-day; BITCOUNT for total; BITOP AND/OR for cross-day analysis.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.LocalDate;

@Service
public class BitOperationsService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    BitOperationsService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void markLogin(Long userId) {
        String key = "logins:"+LocalDate.now();
        redis.opsForValue().setBit(key, userId, true);
        System.out.println("User "+userId+" login recorded");
    }

    public boolean didLogin(Long userId) {
        return Boolean.TRUE.equals(redis.opsForValue().getBit("logins:"+LocalDate.now(), userId));
    }

    public long dailyActiveUsers() {
        Long count = redis.execute(
            (org.springframework.data.redis.core.RedisCallback<Long>) conn ->
                conn.stringCommands().bitCount(("logins:"+LocalDate.now()).getBytes()));
        System.out.println("DAU: "+count);
        return count != null ? count : 0;
    }

    public boolean loginStreak(Long userId, int days) {
        for (int i=0; i<days; i++) {
            String key = "logins:"+LocalDate.now().minusDays(i);
            if (!Boolean.TRUE.equals(redis.opsForValue().getBit(key, userId))) return false;
        }
        return true;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(users/8)

### 1769. Redis TimeSeries
**ID:** `RDS-1769`

**Problem:** Redis TimeSeries.

**Example Input:** temperature readings every second

**Example Output:** time-range query; aggregation by minute

**Explanation:** RedisTimeSeries module: TS.ADD; TS.RANGE; TS.MRANGE; automatic aggregation rules.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Scheduled;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.*;

@Service
public class TimeSeriesService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    TimeSeriesService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public void recordTemperature(String sensorId, double celsius) {
        long ts = System.currentTimeMillis();
        // Native TS.ADD via execute (requires RedisTimeSeries module):
        // redis.execute(conn -> conn.execute("TS.ADD", "sensor:"+sensorId, ts+"", celsius+""));
        // Fallback using sorted set (timestamp as score):
        redis.opsForZSet().add("ts:temp:"+sensorId, celsius+":"+ts, ts);
        System.out.printf("Recorded: sensor=%s temp=%.1f ts=%d%n", sensorId, celsius, ts);
    }

    public List<String> queryRange(String sensorId, long fromMs, long toMs) {
        Set<String> readings = redis.opsForZSet().rangeByScore("ts:temp:"+sensorId, fromMs, toMs);
        System.out.println("Range query returned "+readings.size()+" readings");
        return readings != null ? new ArrayList<>(readings) : List.of();
    }

    public OptionalDouble averageTemp(String sensorId, long fromMs, long toMs) {
        return queryRange(sensorId, fromMs, toMs).stream()
            .mapToDouble(s -> Double.parseDouble(s.split(":")[0])).average();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 1770. Redis Conditional Update
**ID:** `RDS-1770`

**Problem:** Redis Conditional Update.

**Example Input:** update only if version matches

**Example Output:** optimistic locking; no lost updates

**Explanation:** WATCH + MULTI + EXEC; if key changed between WATCH and EXEC: transaction aborts.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.List;

@Service
public class OptimisticLockService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    OptimisticLockService(StringRedisTemplate r) { redis=r; }

    public boolean conditionalUpdate(String key, String expectedVersion, String newValue) {
        List<Object> results = redis.execute(new SessionCallback<List<Object>>() {
            @Override
            public <K,V> List<Object> execute(RedisOperations<K,V> ops) {
                ops.watch((K) key);
                String current = (String)(Object) ops.opsForValue().get(key);
                if (current == null || !current.startsWith(expectedVersion+":")) {
                    ops.unwatch(); return null;
                }
                ops.multi();
                ops.opsForValue().set((K) key, (V)(Object) newValue);
                return ops.exec();
            }
        });
        if (results == null || results.isEmpty()) {
            System.out.println("Conflict detected; update aborted");
            return false;
        }
        System.out.println("Update committed: "+key+" = "+newValue);
        return true;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1772. Redis Caching Strategy Comparison
**ID:** `RDS-1772`

**Problem:** Redis Caching Strategy Comparison.

**Example Input:** evaluate caching strategies for API

**Example Output:** right strategy selected based on read/write ratio

**Explanation:** Cache-aside for read-heavy; Write-through for consistency; Write-behind for write-heavy; Read-through transparent.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class CachingStrategyComparison {
    // 1. Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)
    //    - Read: check cache -> miss -> load DB -> store cache
    //    - Write: update DB -> invalidate cache
    //    - Best for: read-heavy, tolerates slight staleness
    //    - Risk: cache stampede on cold start

    // 2. Write-Through
    //    - Write: update DB + update cache atomically
    //    - Read: always hits cache (warm)
    //    - Best for: read-heavy, consistency critical
    //    - Risk: writes slower; cache may hold unused data

    // 3. Write-Behind (Write-Back)
    //    - Write: update cache immediately -> async DB write
    //    - Best for: write-heavy, can tolerate async
    //    - Risk: data loss if cache fails before DB write

    // 4. Read-Through
    //    - Cache sits in front of DB (library handles miss)
    //    - Application never talks to DB directly
    //    - Best for: simple reads, transparent caching

    public String recommend(int readRatio, int writeRatio, boolean consistencyRequired) {
        if (writeRatio > readRatio*2 && !consistencyRequired) return "Write-Behind";
        if (consistencyRequired) return "Write-Through";
        if (readRatio > writeRatio*5) return "Cache-Aside with long TTL";
        return "Cache-Aside with short TTL";
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1773. Redis Connection Pool
**ID:** `RDS-1773`

**Problem:** Redis Connection Pool.

**Example Input:** high concurrency; 1000 req/sec

**Example Output:** connections reused; no connection exhaustion

**Explanation:** Lettuce connection pool with GenericObjectPoolConfig; maxTotal/maxIdle/minIdle settings.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.lettuce.core.resource.ClientResources;
import org.apache.commons.pool2.impl.GenericObjectPoolConfig;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.lettuce.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;

@Configuration
public class RedisConnectionPoolConfig {
    @Bean LettuceConnectionFactory redisConnectionFactory() {
        RedisStandaloneConfiguration config = new RedisStandaloneConfiguration("localhost", 6379);
        GenericObjectPoolConfig<io.lettuce.core.api.StatefulRedisConnection<byte[],byte[]>> pool =
            new GenericObjectPoolConfig<>();
        pool.setMaxTotal(50);    // max connections
        pool.setMaxIdle(20);     // max idle connections
        pool.setMinIdle(5);      // min idle connections
        pool.setMaxWaitMillis(3000); // wait up to 3s for connection
        pool.setTestOnBorrow(true);  // validate on borrow
        LettucePoolingClientConfiguration poolConfig = LettucePoolingClientConfiguration.builder()
            .poolConfig(pool).build();
        return new LettuceConnectionFactory(config, poolConfig);
    }
    @Bean StringRedisTemplate template(LettuceConnectionFactory cf) { return new StringRedisTemplate(cf); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(pool)
---

### 1774. Redis Monitoring Metrics
**ID:** `RDS-1774`

**Problem:** Redis Monitoring Metrics.

**Example Input:** production Redis performance

**Example Output:** hit rate, memory, latency visible in Grafana

**Explanation:** INFO command metrics; Micrometer Redis metrics; redis_exporter for Prometheus; Grafana dashboard.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.micrometer.core.instrument.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Scheduled;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class RedisMonitoringService {
    private final StringRedisTemplate redis;
    private final MeterRegistry registry;
    private long hitCount=0, missCount=0;

    RedisMonitoringService(StringRedisTemplate r, MeterRegistry reg) {
        redis=r; registry=reg;
        Gauge.builder("redis.hit.rate", this, m -> m.hitCount*100.0/(m.hitCount+m.missCount+1))
            .description("Cache hit rate %").register(reg);
    }

    public String cachedGet(String key) {
        String val = redis.opsForValue().get(key);
        if (val != null) hitCount++; else missCount++;
        registry.counter("redis.operations","type",val!=null?"hit":"miss").increment();
        return val;
    }

    @Scheduled(fixedDelay=60_000)
    public void logMetrics() {
        long total = hitCount + missCount;
        double hitRate = total > 0 ? hitCount*100.0/total : 0;
        System.out.printf("Redis: hits=%d misses=%d hitRate=%.1f%%%n", hitCount, missCount, hitRate);
    }
}
// Redis INFO metrics: used_memory, keyspace_hits, keyspace_misses, connected_clients
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1781. Liveness Probe
**ID:** `OPS-1781`

**Problem:** Liveness Probe.

**Example Input:** pod stuck in deadlock; not responding

**Example Output:** Kubernetes restarts pod automatically

**Explanation:** livenessProbe httpGet /actuator/health/liveness; on failure pod restarted; different from readiness.

**Answer:**
```java
# deployment.yaml probe section:
# livenessProbe:
#   httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/liveness, port: 8080}
#   initialDelaySeconds: 60       # wait for startup
#   periodSeconds: 30
#   failureThreshold: 3
#   timeoutSeconds: 5

# Startup probe (for slow-starting apps):
# startupProbe:
#   httpGet: {path: /actuator/health/liveness, port: 8080}
#   failureThreshold: 30          # allow 30*10s=5min for startup
#   periodSeconds: 10

import org.springframework.boot.actuate.availability.*;
import org.springframework.boot.availability.*;

// Custom liveness indicator: detect deadlock
import org.springframework.boot.actuate.health.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component("deadlockCheck")
class DeadlockLivenessIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    @Override public Health health() {
        java.lang.management.ThreadMXBean tmx =
            java.lang.management.ManagementFactory.getThreadMXBean();
        long[] ids = tmx.findDeadlockedThreads();
        if (ids != null) return Health.down().withDetail("deadlocked_threads", ids.length).build();
        return Health.up().build();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1786. Blue Green Deployment
**ID:** `OPS-1786`

**Problem:** Blue Green Deployment.

**Example Input:** release v2 without downtime

**Example Output:** instant switch; v1 rollback available

**Explanation:** Two K8s deployments (v1/v2); Service selector switched; v1 stays for rollback.

**Answer:**
```java
# Kubernetes blue-green:
# 1. Deploy green (v2):
# kubectl apply -f deployment-v2.yaml  (order-service-green, selector: version=v2)
# 2. Verify green:
# kubectl port-forward svc/order-service-green 8081:80
# curl http://localhost:8081/actuator/health
# 3. Switch service to green:
# kubectl patch svc order-service -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"v2"}}}'
# 4. Monitor metrics (15 min)
# 5. Delete blue (or keep for rollback):
# kubectl delete deployment order-service-blue
# Rollback: kubectl patch svc order-service -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"v1"}}}'

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.boot.actuate.info.*;

class VersionInfoContributor implements InfoContributor {
    @Value("${app.version:unknown}") String version;
    @Value("${app.color:blue}") String color;
    @Override public void contribute(Info.Builder b) {
        b.withDetail("version", version).withDetail("color", color);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---
### 1787. Canary Deployment
**ID:** `OPS-1787`

**Problem:** Canary Deployment.

**Example Input:** 5% traffic to new version

**Example Output:** gradual rollout; monitor before full release

**Explanation:** Istio VirtualService weights; or K8s two deployments proportional replica counts; auto-rollback.

**Answer:**
```java
# Canary via Kubernetes replica proportion:
# order-service-stable: replicas: 19  (95%)
# order-service-canary: replicas: 1   (5%)
# Both selected by shared label app=order-service

# Istio precise canary (recommended):
# VirtualService:
#   http:
#   - match: [{headers: {x-canary: {exact: "true"}}}]
#     route: [{destination: {host: order-service, subset: canary}}]
#   - route:
#     - {destination: {host: order-service, subset: stable}, weight: 95}
#     - {destination: {host: order-service, subset: canary}, weight: 5}
# DestinationRule:
#   subsets:
#   - {name: stable, labels: {version: v1}}
#   - {name: canary, labels: {version: v2}}

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

@RestController class VersionController {
    @Value("${app.version:stable}") String version;
    @GetMapping("/version") public String version() { return version; }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

**ID:** `OPS-1792`

**Problem:** Pod Disruption Budget.

**Example Input:** rolling update or node drain

**Example Output:** minimum 2 pods always available

**Explanation:** PodDisruptionBudget prevents too many pods down at once; minAvailable or maxUnavailable.

**Answer:**
```java
# pdb.yaml:
# apiVersion: policy/v1
# kind: PodDisruptionBudget
# metadata: {name: order-service-pdb}
# spec:
#   minAvailable: 2          # at least 2 pods always running
#   selector: {matchLabels: {app: order-service}}

# Or use maxUnavailable:
# spec:
#   maxUnavailable: 1        # at most 1 pod down at a time

# PDB prevents:
# - kubectl drain taking too many pods at once
# - Rolling updates leaving insufficient capacity
# - Voluntary disruptions (maintenance, upgrades)

# kubectl get pdb order-service-pdb
# NAME               MIN AVAILABLE   MAX UNAVAILABLE   ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS
# order-service-pdb  2               N/A               1

public class PdbDemo {
    // Works with HPA: if minReplicas=3 and minAvailable=2, 1 pod can be disrupted
    // kubectl cordon node1  -> marks node unschedulable
    // kubectl drain node1 --ignore-daemonsets  -> PDB enforced here
}
```

```java
# FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder
# WORKDIR /app
# COPY pom.xml .
# RUN mvn dependency:go-offline -q  # cache dependencies as separate layer
# COPY src ./src
# RUN mvn package -DskipTests -q
# RUN java -Djarmode=layertools -jar target/*.jar extract

# Stage 2: Runtime
# FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine
# RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
# USER app
# WORKDIR /app
# COPY --from=builder /app/dependencies/ ./     # large, rarely changes
# COPY --from=builder /app/spring-boot-loader/ ./
# COPY --from=builder /app/snapshot-dependencies/ ./
# COPY --from=builder /app/application/ ./      # small, changes often
# ENTRYPOINT ["java","org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher"]

# .dockerignore: target/, .git/, *.md, .DS_Store

public class OptimizedDockerBuild {}
```

```java
#     - containerName: order
#       minAllowed: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
#       maxAllowed: {cpu: 2, memory: 2Gi}
#       controlledResources: [cpu, memory]

# VPA modes:
# Off:      only recommends; no changes
# Initial:  sets on pod creation only
# Recreate: restarts pods to apply new values
# Auto:     same as Recreate (in-place resize in future)

# kubectl describe vpa order-service-vpa
# -> Recommended requests: cpu=250m memory=512Mi

public class VPADemo {
```

### 1812. Observability Three Pillars
**ID:** `OPS-1812`

**Problem:** Observability Three Pillars.

**Example Input:** production issue to diagnose

**Example Output:** correlated logs, metrics, traces for root cause

**Explanation:** Metrics (Prometheus) + Logs (ELK) + Traces (Jaeger/Zipkin); correlation via traceId in all three.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.micrometer.tracing.*;
import org.slf4j.Logger; import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class ObservabilityService {
    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(ObservabilityService.class);
    private final Tracer tracer;
    ObservabilityService(Tracer t) { tracer=t; }

    public String processOrder(String orderId) {
        Span span = tracer.nextSpan().name("processOrder").start();
        try (Tracer.SpanInScope ws = tracer.withSpan(span)) {
            span.tag("orderId", orderId);
            log.info("Processing order={} traceId={}", orderId, span.context().traceId());
            // traceId auto-propagated to:
            // 1. Structured log (ELK searchable by traceId)
            // 2. HTTP downstream (B3/W3C headers)
            // 3. Jaeger distributed trace
            return "processed";
        } catch (Exception e) {
            span.error(e);
            throw e;
        } finally { span.end(); }
    }
}
// application.properties:
// management.tracing.sampling.probability=1.0
// management.zipkin.tracing.endpoint=http://jaeger:9411/api/v2/spans
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

**ID:** `OPS-1813`

**Problem:** Zero Downtime Database Migration.

**Explanation:** Flyway/Liquibase; expand-contract pattern: add nullable column first, backfill, then add constraint.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.flywaydb.core.Flyway;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.flyway.FlywayMigrationInitializer;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;

// Flyway migration files (src/main/resources/db/migration/):
// V1__create_orders.sql:
//   CREATE TABLE orders (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, total NUMERIC(10,2), created_at TIMESTAMP);

// V2__add_status_column.sql (backward compatible: nullable first):
//   ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(20);  -- nullable, app handles null

// V3__backfill_status.sql:
//   UPDATE orders SET status = 'COMPLETED' WHERE status IS NULL;

// V4__add_status_not_null.sql (after 100% traffic on new app):
//   ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN status SET NOT NULL;

// application.properties:
// spring.flyway.enabled=true
// spring.flyway.locations=classpath:db/migration
// spring.flyway.baseline-on-migrate=true

public class ZeroDowntimeMigrationDemo {
    // Step 1: Deploy V2 migration + new app code (handles both null and set status)
    // Step 2: Run V3 backfill
    // Step 3: Deploy V4 migration (all rows have status)
    // Expand-contract avoids breaking old app reading new schema
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
}
```

### 1816. Upload File To S3
**ID:** `AWS-1816`

**Problem:** Upload File To S3.

**Example Input:** user uploads profile image

**Example Output:** file stored in S3; presigned URL returned for download

**Explanation:** AWS SDK S3Client; PutObjectRequest; S3Presigner for temporary download URL.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.model.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.presigner.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.presigner.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.nio.file.Path; import java.time.Duration; import java.net.URL;

@Service
public class S3Service {
    private final S3Client s3;
    private final S3Presigner presigner;
    private final String bucket = "my-app-uploads";

    S3Service(S3Client s3, S3Presigner presigner) { this.s3=s3; this.presigner=presigner; }

    public String upload(String key, Path file, String contentType) {
        s3.putObject(PutObjectRequest.builder()
            .bucket(bucket).key(key).contentType(contentType)
            .serverSideEncryption(ServerSideEncryption.AES256).build(),
            file);
        return "s3://"+bucket+"/"+key;
    }

    public URL generatePresignedUrl(String key, Duration expiry) {
        GetObjectPresignRequest req = GetObjectPresignRequest.builder()
            .signatureDuration(expiry)
            .getObjectRequest(GetObjectRequest.builder().bucket(bucket).key(key).build()).build();
        return presigner.presignGetObject(req).url();
    }

    public void delete(String key) {
        s3.deleteObject(DeleteObjectRequest.builder().bucket(bucket).key(key).build());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(file_size)
---

### 1817. Connect App To RDS
**ID:** `AWS-1817`

**Problem:** Connect App To RDS.

**Example Input:** Spring Boot connects to AWS RDS PostgreSQL

**Example Output:** app reads/writes to managed DB; SSL enforced

**Explanation:** RDS endpoint in datasource URL; SSL required; credentials from Secrets Manager or env.

**Answer:**
```java
# application.properties:
# spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://${RDS_ENDPOINT}:5432/appdb?ssl=true&sslmode=require
# spring.datasource.username=${RDS_USERNAME}
# spring.datasource.password=${RDS_PASSWORD}
# spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
# spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=3000

import software.amazon.awssdk.services.secretsmanager.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.secretsmanager.model.*;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;

@Configuration
class RdsConfig {
    @Value("${aws.secretName:rds-credentials}") String secretName;

    @Bean String dbPassword() throws Exception {
        SecretsManagerClient client = SecretsManagerClient.create();
        GetSecretValueResponse resp = client.getSecretValue(
            GetSecretValueRequest.builder().secretId(secretName).build());
        JsonNode json = new ObjectMapper().readTree(resp.secretString());
        return json.get("password").asText();
    }
}
// IAM role for EC2/ECS: attach policy AmazonRDSFullAccess or custom VPC SG rule
// RDS in private subnet; app in same VPC; SG allows 5432 from app SG
```

### 1818. Use IAM Role
**ID:** `AWS-1818`

**Problem:** Use IAM Role.

**Example Input:** EC2 app needs to call S3 without hardcoded keys

**Example Output:** role attached; SDK auto-discovers credentials

**Explanation:** IAM Role attached to EC2/ECS; SDK DefaultCredentialsProvider chain; no keys in code.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.auth.credentials.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.regions.Region;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.S3Client;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;

@Configuration
class AwsConfig {
    @Bean S3Client s3Client() {
        return S3Client.builder()
            .region(Region.US_EAST_1)
            // DefaultCredentialsProvider automatically checks (in order):
            // 1. Environment vars AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
            // 2. System properties
            // 3. ~/.aws/credentials (local dev)
            // 4. ECS task role credentials
            // 5. EC2 instance profile role  <-- production
            .credentialsProvider(DefaultCredentialsProvider.create())
            .build();
    }
}
// IAM Role policy example (S3 read/write to specific bucket):
// {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{
//   "Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:PutObject","s3:DeleteObject"],
//   "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::my-app-uploads/*"
// }]}
// Attach role to EC2 via instance profile; to ECS via task role
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1819. Create VPC Basics
**ID:** `AWS-1819`

**Problem:** Create VPC Basics.

**Example Input:** isolate application in private network

**Example Output:** app in private subnet; DB inaccessible from internet

**Explanation:** VPC with public/private subnets; Internet Gateway for public; NAT Gateway for private outbound; SG rules.

**Answer:**
```java
# VPC Architecture:
# VPC CIDR: 10.0.0.0/16
# Public subnets:  10.0.1.0/24 (us-east-1a), 10.0.2.0/24 (us-east-1b)
# Private subnets: 10.0.3.0/24 (us-east-1a), 10.0.4.0/24 (us-east-1b)

# Components:
# Internet Gateway (IGW): public subnets -> internet
# NAT Gateway (1 per AZ): private subnets -> outbound internet (no inbound)
# Route tables:
#   public-rt:  0.0.0.0/0 -> IGW
#   private-rt: 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT GW

# Security Groups:
# alb-sg:   inbound TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0
# app-sg:   inbound TCP 8080 from alb-sg only
# db-sg:    inbound TCP 5432 from app-sg only

# Deployment:
```

```java
import com.amazonaws.services.lambda.runtime.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import java.util.*; import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;

@Component
public class OrderLambdaHandler implements RequestHandler<Map<String,Object>, Map<String,Object>> {
    private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();

    @Override
    public Map<String,Object> handleRequest(Map<String,Object> event, Context context) {
        LambdaLogger logger = context.getLogger();
        logger.log("Event: "+event.toString());
        logger.log("Remaining time: "+context.getRemainingTimeInMillis()+"ms");

        String orderId = (String) event.getOrDefault("orderId","unknown");
        // process order...
        Map<String,Object> response = new HashMap<>();
        response.put("statusCode", 200);
        response.put("orderId", orderId);
        response.put("status", "PROCESSED");
        response.put("requestId", context.getAwsRequestId());
        return response;
    }
}
// sam local invoke OrderFunction -e event.json (local test)
// Environment: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=lambda
// Memory: 512MB; Timeout: 30s; Concurrency: reserved=100
```

**ID:** `AWS-1824`

**Problem:** CloudWatch Logs.

**Example Input:** Lambda/ECS logs centralised

**Example Output:** logs queryable; alerts on errors; retention set

**Explanation:** CloudWatch log groups; Log Insights queries; metric filters for error counting; alarms.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.cloudwatch.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.cloudwatch.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Service
public class CloudWatchAlerting {
    private final CloudWatchClient cw;
    CloudWatchAlerting(CloudWatchClient cw) { this.cw=cw; }

    public void createErrorAlarm(String namespace, String metricName, String alarmName, String snsArn) {
        cw.putMetricAlarm(PutMetricAlarmRequest.builder()
            .alarmName(alarmName)
            .namespace(namespace).metricName(metricName)
            .statistic(Statistic.SUM)
            .period(300)          // 5 minutes
            .evaluationPeriods(1)
            .threshold(10.0)      // alert if 10+ errors in 5 min
            .comparisonOperator(ComparisonOperator.GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO_THRESHOLD)
            .alarmActions(snsArn) // SNS -> email/Slack
            .build());
    }
}
// CloudWatch Log Insights query:
// fields @timestamp, @message
// | filter @message like /ERROR/
// | stats count() as errorCount by bin(5m)
// | sort errorCount desc | limit 20

// application.properties (ECS):
// logging.group.aws_ecs.com.myapp=DEBUG  -> auto-shipped by awslogs driver
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(logs)
