### 1828. SQS Queue Producer
**ID:** `AWS-1828`

**Problem:** SQS Queue Producer.

**Example Input:** order service sends message to queue

**Example Output:** message in queue; consumer processes async

**Explanation:** SqsTemplate or SqsAsyncClient; SendMessageRequest with FIFO or Standard queue; visibility timeout.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.sqs.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.sqs.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import java.util.UUID;

@Service
public class SqsProducerService {
    private final SqsClient sqs;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
    private final String queueUrl;
    SqsProducerService(SqsClient sqs) {
        this.sqs=sqs;
        this.queueUrl = sqs.getQueueUrl(GetQueueUrlRequest.builder().queueName("order-queue.fifo").build()).queueUrl();
    }

    public String sendOrder(Object order) throws Exception {
        String body = mapper.writeValueAsString(order);
        SendMessageResponse resp = sqs.sendMessage(SendMessageRequest.builder()
            .queueUrl(queueUrl)
            .messageBody(body)
            .messageGroupId("orders")                      // FIFO grouping
            .messageDeduplicationId(UUID.randomUUID().toString())  // idempotency
            .build());
        System.out.println("Sent: "+resp.messageId());
        return resp.messageId();
    }
}
// Standard vs FIFO:
// Standard: unlimited throughput, at-least-once, best-effort ordering
// FIFO: 3000 msg/s, exactly-once, strict ordering per group
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.sns.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.sns.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import java.util.Map;

@Service
public class SnsNotificationService {
    private final SnsClient sns;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
    private final String topicArn;
    SnsNotificationService(SnsClient sns, String topicArn) { this.sns=sns; this.topicArn=topicArn; }

    public void notifyOrderShipped(String orderId, String userId) throws Exception {
        String message = mapper.writeValueAsString(Map.of("orderId",orderId,"userId",userId,"event","SHIPPED"));
        PublishResponse resp = sns.publish(PublishRequest.builder()
            .topicArn(topicArn)
            .message(message)
            .subject("Order Shipped: "+orderId)
            .messageAttributes(Map.of(
                "eventType", MessageAttributeValue.builder().dataType("String").stringValue("ORDER_SHIPPED").build()))
            .build());
        System.out.println("SNS published: "+resp.messageId());
    }
}
// SNS subscriptions on topic:
// - Email: user@email.com -> direct email
// - SQS: order-notifications.fifo -> async consumer
// - Lambda: push notification function
// - HTTP: webhook endpoint
```

### 1831. AWS SQS Consumer
**ID:** `AWS-1831`

**Problem:** AWS SQS Consumer.

**Example Input:** messages in SQS queue

**Example Output:** consumer processes; on error moves to DLQ

**Explanation:** @SqsListener (Spring Cloud AWS); visibility timeout; DLQ after maxReceiveCount failures.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.awspring.cloud.sqs.annotation.SqsListener;
import io.awspring.cloud.sqs.listener.acknowledgement.Acknowledgement;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import org.slf4j.Logger; import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

record OrderEvent(String orderId, String userId, double amount) {}

@Component
public class OrderQueueConsumer {
    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(OrderQueueConsumer.class);

    @SqsListener(value = "order-queue", acknowledgementMode = "MANUAL")
    public void consume(OrderEvent event, Acknowledgement ack) {
        try {
            log.info("Processing order: {}", event.orderId());
            processOrder(event);
            ack.acknowledge();  // delete from queue
        } catch (Exception e) {
            log.error("Failed orderId={} error={}", event.orderId(), e.getMessage());
            // DO NOT ack -> message returns after visibility timeout
            // After maxReceiveCount (e.g. 3) -> moves to DLQ automatically
        }
    }

    private void processOrder(OrderEvent e) {
        if ("INVALID".equals(e.orderId())) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Bad orderId");
        log.info("Order {} fulfilled for {} amount={}", e.orderId(), e.userId(), e.amount());
    }
}
// application.properties:
// spring.cloud.aws.sqs.listener.acknowledgement-mode=manual
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

**Example Output:** Lambda triggered; thumbnail generated

**Explanation:** S3 event notification -> Lambda trigger; S3Event parsed; read source; write thumbnail.

**Answer:**
```java
import com.amazonaws.services.lambda.runtime.*;
import com.amazonaws.services.lambda.runtime.events.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.core.sync.RequestBody;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.model.*;
import java.io.ByteArrayInputStream;

public class ThumbnailLambda implements RequestHandler<S3Event, String> {
    private final S3Client s3 = S3Client.create();

    @Override
    public String handleRequest(S3Event event, Context context) {
        event.getRecords().forEach(r -> {
            String bucket = r.getS3().getBucket().getName();
            String key = r.getS3().getObject().getUrlDecodedKey();
            context.getLogger().log("Processing: s3://"+bucket+"/"+key);

            // Download original
            byte[] original = s3.getObject(GetObjectRequest.builder().bucket(bucket).key(key).build())
                .readAllBytes();
            // Generate thumbnail (simplified - use ImageIO in real app)
            byte[] thumbnail = generateThumbnail(original);
            // Upload thumbnail
            String thumbKey = "thumbnails/"+key;
            s3.putObject(PutObjectRequest.builder().bucket(bucket).key(thumbKey).build(),
                RequestBody.fromBytes(thumbnail));
            context.getLogger().log("Thumbnail created: "+thumbKey);
        });
        return "OK";
    }
    private byte[] generateThumbnail(byte[] img) { return img; } // stub
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(image_size)

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.eventbridge.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.eventbridge.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import java.util.Map;

@Service
public class EventBridgePublisher {
    private final EventBridgeClient eventBridge;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
    EventBridgePublisher(EventBridgeClient eb) { eventBridge=eb; }

    public void publishOrderPlaced(String orderId, String userId, double amount) throws Exception {
        String detail = mapper.writeValueAsString(Map.of("orderId",orderId,"userId",userId,"amount",amount));
        PutEventsRequestEntry entry = PutEventsRequestEntry.builder()
            .source("com.myapp.orders")
            .detailType("OrderPlaced")
            .detail(detail)
            .eventBusName("order-events")
            .build();
        PutEventsResponse resp = eventBridge.putEvents(PutEventsRequest.builder().entries(entry).build());
        if (resp.failedEntryCount() > 0) throw new RuntimeException("EventBridge publish failed");
        System.out.println("Event published: OrderPlaced for "+orderId);
    }
}
// EventBridge Rules (console/CDK):
// Pattern: {source: ["com.myapp.orders"], detail-type: ["OrderPlaced"]}
// Target 1: inventory-lambda
// Target 2: notification-sqs
// Target 3: analytics-firehose
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

**ID:** `AWS-1834`

**Problem:** AWS Cognito Authentication.

**Explanation:** Cognito User Pool; tokens (ID/access/refresh); Spring Security validates JWT via JWKS endpoint.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configuration.EnableWebSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.oauth2.jwt.*;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;

@Configuration @EnableWebSecurity
class CognitoSecurityConfig {
    @Bean SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
                .requestMatchers("/public/**").permitAll()
                .anyRequest().authenticated())
            .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(j -> j.decoder(jwtDecoder())));
        return http.build();
    }

    @Bean JwtDecoder jwtDecoder() {
        // Cognito JWKS: https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}/.well-known/jwks.json
        String jwksUri = "https://cognito-idp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/us-east-1_ABC123/.well-known/jwks.json";
        return NimbusJwtDecoder.withJwkSetUri(jwksUri).build();
    }
}
// application.properties:
// spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri=https://cognito-idp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/us-east-1_ABC123
// Client: POST https://myapp.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/token -> access_token
// Header: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1835. DynamoDB Basic CRUD
**ID:** `AWS-1835`

**Problem:** DynamoDB Basic CRUD.

**Example Input:** store/retrieve user sessions in DynamoDB

**Example Output:** fast key-value access; auto-scaled

**Explanation:** DynamoDbClient; PutItem/GetItem/DeleteItem; EnhancedClient with @DynamoDbBean.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.enhanced.dynamodb.mapper.annotations.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Instant;

@DynamoDbBean
class UserSession {
    @DynamoDbPartitionKey String sessionId;
    String userId;
    long ttl;  // DynamoDB TTL attribute (epoch seconds)
    String data;
    // getters/setters required for EnhancedClient
    public String getSessionId() {return sessionId;} public void setSessionId(String s){sessionId=s;}
    public String getUserId() {return userId;} public void setUserId(String u){userId=u;}
    public long getTtl() {return ttl;} public void setTtl(long t){ttl=t;}
    public String getData() {return data;} public void setData(String d){data=d;}
}

@Service
class SessionRepository {
    private final DynamoDbTable<UserSession> table;
    SessionRepository(DynamoDbEnhancedClient client) {
        table = client.table("user-sessions", TableSchema.fromBean(UserSession.class));
    }
    public void save(UserSession s) { s.setTtl(Instant.now().plusSeconds(3600).getEpochSecond()); table.putItem(s); }
    public UserSession get(String id) { return table.getItem(Key.builder().partitionValue(id).build()); }
    public void delete(String id) { table.deleteItem(Key.builder().partitionValue(id).build()); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;

import org.springframework.data.redis.connection.lettuce.*;
import org.springframework.data.redis.core.StringRedisTemplate;
import io.lettuce.core.ClientOptions;

import java.time.Duration;

@Configuration
class ElastiCacheConfig {
    @Bean LettuceConnectionFactory connectionFactory() {
        // Cluster mode endpoint:
        RedisClusterConfiguration cluster = new RedisClusterConfiguration();
        cluster.clusterNode("my-cluster.abc123.clustercfg.use1.cache.amazonaws.com", 6379);
        cluster.setPassword(RedisPassword.of(System.getenv("REDIS_AUTH_TOKEN")));

        LettuceClientConfiguration clientConfig = LettuceClientConfiguration.builder()
            .useSsl()                               // in-transit encryption (required for ElastiCache)
            .clientOptions(ClientOptions.builder()
                .socketOptions(SocketOptions.builder().connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3)).build()).build())
            .commandTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
            .build();
        return new LettuceConnectionFactory(cluster, clientConfig);
    }
    @Bean StringRedisTemplate redisTemplate(LettuceConnectionFactory cf) { return new StringRedisTemplate(cf); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(keys)

### 1837. AWS RDS Multi AZ
**ID:** `AWS-1837`

**Problem:** AWS RDS Multi AZ.

**Example Input:** primary RDS fails

**Example Output:** automatic failover to standby; ~60s downtime

**Explanation:** RDS Multi-AZ: synchronous replication to standby; automatic failover; same endpoint (no DNS change).

**Answer:**
```java
# RDS Multi-AZ configuration:
# aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier prod-db --multi-az --apply-immediately

# Architecture:
# Primary: us-east-1a, 10.0.3.x (private subnet)
# Standby: us-east-1b, 10.0.4.x (private subnet, sync replica)
# Endpoint: prod-db.xyz.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com (DNS CNAME, unchanged on failover)
# Failover time: ~60-120 seconds; DNS TTL causes ~30s of connection errors

# HikariCP settings for RDS failover:
# spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=3000
# spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
# spring.datasource.hikari.keepalive-time=60000
# spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=1800000

import com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariDataSource;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;

@Configuration class RdsMultiAzConfig {
    @Bean HikariDataSource dataSource(@Value("${spring.datasource.url}") String url) {
        HikariDataSource ds = new HikariDataSource();
        ds.setJdbcUrl(url);
        ds.setConnectionTestQuery("SELECT 1");
        ds.setInitializationFailTimeout(-1); // retry on startup failure
        return ds;
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

```java
class OrderServiceStack extends Stack {
```

### 1840. AWS Parameter Store
**ID:** `AWS-1840`

**Problem:** AWS Parameter Store.

**Example Input:** application config in SSM Parameter Store

**Example Output:** spring boot reads config at startup; no restart needed

**Explanation:** SSM GetParameter; Spring Cloud AWS Parameter Store bootstrap; hierarchical paths by env.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.ssm.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.ssm.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct;

@Component
class ParameterStoreLoader {
    private final SsmClient ssm = SsmClient.create();

    @PostConstruct void loadParams() {
        String env = System.getenv("SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE");
        // Load parameters by path: /order-service/prod/
        GetParametersByPathResponse resp = ssm.getParametersByPath(GetParametersByPathRequest.builder()
            .path("/order-service/"+env+"/")
            .withDecryption(true).build());
        resp.parameters().forEach(p ->
            System.setProperty(p.name().substring(p.name().lastIndexOf('/')+1), p.value()));
        System.out.println("Loaded "+resp.parameters().size()+" parameters from SSM");
    }
}
// SSM parameters:
// /order-service/prod/spring.datasource.url    -> jdbc:postgresql://...
// /order-service/prod/app.feature.new-checkout -> true
// Type: SecureString (encrypted with KMS) for secrets; String for regular config
// Spring Cloud AWS:
// spring.config.import=aws-parameterstore:/order-service/${spring.profiles.active}/
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(params)

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.cloudwatch.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.cloudwatch.model.*;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Scheduled;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.time.Instant; import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

@Service
public class BusinessMetricsService {
    private final CloudWatchClient cw;
    private final AtomicLong orderCount = new AtomicLong();
    BusinessMetricsService(CloudWatchClient cw) { this.cw=cw; }

    public void recordOrder(String status) { orderCount.incrementAndGet(); }

    @Scheduled(fixedRate=60_000)
    public void flushMetrics() {
        long count = orderCount.getAndSet(0);
        cw.putMetricData(PutMetricDataRequest.builder()
            .namespace("OrderService")
            .metricData(MetricDatum.builder()
                .metricName("OrdersCreated")
                .value((double)count)
                .unit(StandardUnit.COUNT)
                .timestamp(Instant.now())
                .dimensions(Dimension.builder().name("Environment").value("prod").build()).build())
            .build());
        System.out.println("CloudWatch: OrdersCreated="+count);
    }
}
// CloudWatch Alarm: OrdersCreated < 10 in 5 min -> SNS alert
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1842. AWS Kinesis Data Stream
**ID:** `AWS-1842`

**Problem:** AWS Kinesis Data Stream.

**Example Input:** high-throughput click events

**Example Output:** events ingested; real-time analytics possible

**Explanation:** KinesisClient putRecord; partition key for shard routing; consumer with shard iterator.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.kinesis.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.kinesis.model.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.core.SdkBytes;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;
import java.util.Map;

@Service
public class KinesisProducer {
    private final KinesisClient kinesis;
    private final ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();
    private final String streamName = "click-events";
    KinesisProducer(KinesisClient kinesis) { this.kinesis=kinesis; }

    public String send(String userId, String pageId, String action) throws Exception {
        Map<String,Object> event = Map.of("userId",userId,"pageId",pageId,"action",action,"ts",System.currentTimeMillis());
        SdkBytes data = SdkBytes.fromByteArray(mapper.writeValueAsBytes(event));
        PutRecordResponse resp = kinesis.putRecord(PutRecordRequest.builder()
            .streamName(streamName)
            .data(data)
            .partitionKey(userId)   // same user -> same shard (ordered)
            .build());
        return resp.sequenceNumber();
    }
}
// Kinesis Firehose: buffer and batch to S3/Redshift
// KCL consumer: checkpoints to DynamoDB; at-least-once
// Shard capacity: 1MB/s in, 2MB/s out; split shards for scale
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1843. AWS Step Functions
**ID:** `AWS-1843`

**Problem:** AWS Step Functions.

**Example Input:** multi-step order workflow

**Example Output:** each step retried; failures handled; state visible

**Explanation:** Step Functions state machine; Lambda tasks; retry/catch; parallel states; human approval.

**Answer:**
```java
// AWS CDK Step Functions (Java):
import software.amazon.awscdk.services.stepfunctions.*;
import software.amazon.awscdk.services.stepfunctions.tasks.*;
import software.amazon.awscdk.services.lambda.*;
import software.constructs.Construct;

class OrderWorkflowConstruct extends Construct {
    OrderWorkflowConstruct(Construct scope, String id) {
        super(scope, id);
    }

    StateMachine createWorkflow(Function validateFn, Function paymentFn, Function fulfillFn) {
        LambdaInvoke validate = LambdaInvoke.Builder.create(this, "ValidateOrder")
            .lambdaFunction(validateFn).outputPath("$.Payload").build();
        LambdaInvoke payment = LambdaInvoke.Builder.create(this, "ProcessPayment")
            .lambdaFunction(paymentFn).outputPath("$.Payload")
            .retryOnServiceExceptions(true).build();
        LambdaInvoke fulfill = LambdaInvoke.Builder.create(this,"FulfillOrder")
            .lambdaFunction(fulfillFn).outputPath("$.Payload").build();
        Fail failed = Fail.Builder.create(this,"Failed").error("WorkflowFailed").build();

        Chain definition = Chain.start(validate)
            .next(payment).next(fulfill);

        return StateMachine.Builder.create(this,"OrderStateMachine")
            .definition(definition).timeout(software.amazon.awscdk.Duration.minutes(30)).build();
    }
}
// State machine JSON defines flow; each state has Retry, Catch, Next
```

> **Time:** O(steps) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1845. AWS X-Ray Distributed Tracing
**ID:** `AWS-1845`

**Problem:** AWS X-Ray Distributed Tracing.

**Example Input:** trace request across Lambda, SQS, RDS

**Example Output:** full call graph visible; bottleneck identified

**Explanation:** X-Ray SDK; @XRayEnabled; segments/subsegments auto-created; propagate via HTTP headers.

**Answer:**
```java
import com.amazonaws.xray.*;
import com.amazonaws.xray.entities.*;
import com.amazonaws.xray.spring.aop.*;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;

@Configuration @EnableXRay class XRayConfig {}

@Service @XRayEnabled
public class OrderService {
    public String createOrder(String userId, double amount) {
        Segment segment = AWSXRay.getCurrentSegment();
        segment.putAnnotation("userId", userId);
        segment.putMetadata("amount", amount);

        Subsegment dbSubseg = AWSXRay.beginSubsegment("database-call");
        try {
            saveOrder(userId, amount);
        } finally { AWSXRay.endSubsegment(); }

        Subsegment sqsSubseg = AWSXRay.beginSubsegment("sqs-publish");
        try {
            publishEvent(userId, amount);
        } finally { AWSXRay.endSubsegment(); }

        return "order-created";
    }
    private void saveOrder(String u, double a) { System.out.println("Saved"); }
    private void publishEvent(String u, double a) { System.out.println("Published"); }
}
// application.properties:
// cloud.aws.xray.enabled=true
// X-Ray daemon: sidecar container in ECS/EKS
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(segments)
---

### 1849. AWS CloudFront CDN
**ID:** `AWS-1849`

**Problem:** AWS CloudFront CDN.

**Example Input:** static assets and API responses cached globally

**Example Output:** low latency worldwide; S3 origin; API cache

**Explanation:** CloudFront distribution; S3 origin for static; ALB origin for API; cache policies; OAI for S3 security.

**Answer:**
```java
# CloudFront distribution (CDK):
import software.amazon.awscdk.services.cloudfront.*;
import software.amazon.awscdk.services.cloudfront.origins.*;
import software.amazon.awscdk.services.s3.*;
import software.constructs.Construct;

class CdnConstruct extends Construct {
    CdnConstruct(Construct scope, String id, Bucket staticBucket, String apiDomain) {
        super(scope, id);
        S3Origin s3Origin = S3Origin.Builder.create(staticBucket).build();
        HttpOrigin apiOrigin = HttpOrigin.Builder.create(apiDomain).build();
        Distribution.Builder.create(this,"AppCdn")
            .defaultBehavior(BehaviorOptions.builder()
                .origin(s3Origin)
                .cachePolicy(CachePolicy.CACHING_OPTIMIZED).build())
            .additionalBehaviors(java.util.Map.of(
                "/api/*", BehaviorOptions.builder()
                    .origin(apiOrigin)
                    .cachePolicy(CachePolicy.CACHING_DISABLED) // API: no cache
                    .allowedMethods(AllowedMethods.ALLOW_ALL).build(),
                "/static/*", BehaviorOptions.builder()
                    .origin(s3Origin)
                    .cachePolicy(CachePolicy.CACHING_OPTIMIZED).build()))
            .build();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(cached)

### 1851. AWS SQS Dead Letter Queue
**ID:** `AWS-1851`

**Problem:** AWS SQS Dead Letter Queue.

**Example Input:** messages fail processing

**Example Output:** DLQ captures; devs can inspect and replay

**Explanation:** SQS DLQ: maxReceiveCount on source queue; DLQ redrive policy; alarm on DLQ depth.

**Answer:**
```java
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.sqs.*;
import software.amazon.awssdk.services.sqs.model.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.List; import java.util.Map;

@Service
public class DlqManagementService {
    private final SqsClient sqs;
    private final String dlqUrl = "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456/order-queue-dlq";
    private final String mainUrl = "https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456/order-queue";
    DlqManagementService(SqsClient sqs) { this.sqs=sqs; }

    public List<Message> inspectDlq(int maxMessages) {
        return sqs.receiveMessage(ReceiveMessageRequest.builder()
            .queueUrl(dlqUrl).maxNumberOfMessages(maxMessages)
            .attributeNames(QueueAttributeName.ALL).build()).messages();
    }

    public void replayToDlq(String messageBody) {
        // Fix the message data, then replay to main queue
        sqs.sendMessage(SendMessageRequest.builder().queueUrl(mainUrl).messageBody(messageBody).build());
        System.out.println("Replayed to main queue");
    }

    public Long getDlqDepth() {
        String attr = sqs.getQueueAttributes(GetQueueAttributesRequest.builder()
            .queueUrl(dlqUrl).attributeNames(QueueAttributeName.APPROXIMATE_NUMBER_OF_MESSAGES).build())
            .attributes().get(QueueAttributeName.APPROXIMATE_NUMBER_OF_MESSAGES);
        return Long.parseLong(attr);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 1852. AWS Cost Optimization
**ID:** `AWS-1852`

**Problem:** AWS Cost Optimization.

**Example Input:** AWS bill too high

**Example Output:** unused resources identified; reservations applied

**Explanation:** Cost Explorer; Trusted Advisor; Savings Plans; right-sizing; S3 lifecycle; Reserved Instances.

**Answer:**
```java
# Cost optimization strategies:

# 1. Right-sizing EC2:
# aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name CPUUtilization
# If avg CPU < 20%: downsize t3.large -> t3.medium (save 50%)

# 2. Reserved Instances / Savings Plans:
# 1-year committed: 40% discount; 3-year: 60% discount
# Compute Savings Plan: covers EC2, Fargate, Lambda

# 3. S3 lifecycle rules:
# Current -> Infrequent Access after 30 days (40% savings)
# Infrequent Access -> Glacier after 90 days (80% savings)
# Delete after 365 days

# 4. Auto Scaling: scale down nights/weekends for dev environments
# aws autoscaling put-scheduled-action --auto-scaling-group-name dev-asg #   --scheduled-action-name scale-down-night --cron "0 20 * * *" --desired-capacity 0

# 5. NAT Gateway: expensive (~$32/month + data); use VPC endpoints for S3/DynamoDB (free)

public class CostOptimizationChecklist {
    // Enable Cost Anomaly Detection -> alert on unexpected spend
    // Use spot instances for batch/stateless: 70-90% savings
    // Delete unattached EBS volumes and unused EIPs
}
```

```java
# Multi-region architecture:
# Primary: us-east-1 (active)
# Secondary: ap-southeast-1 (standby/active for APAC)

# Data replication:
# RDS: aws rds create-db-instance-read-replica --source-db-instance-identifier prod-db #   --replication-source-identifier arn:...:prod-db --region ap-southeast-1
# S3: Bucket replication rule -> same bucket name in ap-southeast-1; CRR enabled
# DynamoDB: Global Tables -> aws dynamodb update-table --table-name orders #   --replica-updates [{Create:{RegionName:ap-southeast-1}}]

# Traffic routing (Route53):
# Latency-based routing: api.myapp.com -> us-east-1 ALB OR ap-southeast-1 ALB (lower latency wins)
# Failover routing: primary health check fails -> secondary

# Global Accelerator:
# Static anycast IPs; routes via AWS backbone (faster than internet)
# Automatic failover < 1 minute

public class MultiRegionDemo {}
```

### 1855. JUnit Basic Test
**ID:** `TST-1855`

**Problem:** JUnit Basic Test.

**Example Input:** add unit tests for calculator

**Example Output:** all tests pass; edge cases covered

**Explanation:** JUnit 5: @Test, @BeforeEach, @ParameterizedTest; assertions with AssertJ or JUnit.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class Calculator {
    int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
    int divide(int a, int b) {
        if (b == 0) throw new ArithmeticException("Cannot divide by zero");
        return a / b;
    }
}

class CalculatorTest {
    Calculator calc;
    @BeforeEach void setUp() { calc = new Calculator(); }
    @Test void testAdd() { assertEquals(5, calc.add(2, 3)); }
    @Test void testAddNegative() { assertEquals(-1, calc.add(2, -3)); }
    @Test void testDivide() { assertEquals(2, calc.divide(6, 3)); }
    @Test void testDivideByZero() {
        ArithmeticException ex = assertThrows(ArithmeticException.class, () -> calc.divide(10, 0));
        assertEquals("Cannot divide by zero", ex.getMessage());
    }
    @Test void testAll() {
        assertAll("calculator",
            () -> assertEquals(10, calc.add(5, 5)),
            () -> assertEquals(3, calc.divide(9, 3)));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1856. Mockito Mock Service
**ID:** `TST-1856`

**Problem:** Mockito Mock Service.

**Example Input:** OrderService depends on PaymentGateway

**Example Output:** test OrderService without calling real gateway

**Explanation:** @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension); @Mock, @InjectMocks; when().thenReturn(); verify().

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.*;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;

interface PaymentGateway { String charge(String userId, double amount); }
class OrderService {
    private final PaymentGateway gateway;
    OrderService(PaymentGateway g) { this.gateway=g; }
    String placeOrder(String userId, double amount) {
        String result = gateway.charge(userId, amount);
        if ("SUCCESS".equals(result)) return "ORDER_CREATED";
        throw new RuntimeException("Payment failed: "+result);
    }
}

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class OrderServiceTest {
    @Mock PaymentGateway gateway;
    @InjectMocks OrderService orderService;

    @Test void testSuccessfulOrder() {
        when(gateway.charge("u1", 100.0)).thenReturn("SUCCESS");
        assertEquals("ORDER_CREATED", orderService.placeOrder("u1", 100.0));
        verify(gateway, times(1)).charge("u1", 100.0);
    }

    @Test void testFailedPayment() {
        when(gateway.charge("u1", 100.0)).thenReturn("DECLINED");
        RuntimeException ex = assertThrows(RuntimeException.class, () -> orderService.placeOrder("u1", 100.0));
        assertTrue(ex.getMessage().contains("Payment failed"));
    }

    @Test void testNoInteraction() { verifyNoMoreInteractions(gateway); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import jakarta.persistence.*; import java.util.Optional;

@Entity class Order {

    Order(String u, double a, String s){userId=u;amount=a;status=s;}
}
interface OrderRepo extends org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<Order,Long>{}

@SpringBootTest @Transactional
class OrderIntegrationTest {
    @Autowired OrderRepo repo;
    @Test void testSaveAndFind() {
        Order saved = repo.save(new Order("user1", 250.0, "PENDING"));
        Assertions.assertNotNull(saved.id);
        Optional<Order> found = repo.findById(saved.id);
        Assertions.assertTrue(found.isPresent());
        Assertions.assertEquals("user1", found.get().userId);
        Assertions.assertEquals("PENDING", found.get().status);
```

### 1859. Repository Test
**ID:** `TST-1859`

**Problem:** Repository Test.

**Explanation:** @DataJpaTest: in-memory H2; only JPA layer loaded; test custom queries and derived methods.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import jakarta.persistence.*; import java.util.Optional;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository;
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.Query;

@Entity class User {
    @Id @GeneratedValue Long id;
    String email; String name; boolean active;
    User(){}
    User(String e,String n,boolean a){email=e;name=n;active=a;}
}
interface UserRepository extends JpaRepository<User,Long> {
    Optional<User> findByEmail(String email);
    @Query("SELECT u FROM User u WHERE u.active=true") java.util.List<User> findActiveUsers();
}

@DataJpaTest class UserRepositoryTest {
    @Autowired UserRepository repo;
    @BeforeEach void setUp() {
        repo.save(new User("alice@example.com","Alice",true));
        repo.save(new User("bob@example.com","Bob",false));
    }
    @Test void testFindByEmail() {
        Optional<User> u = repo.findByEmail("alice@example.com");
        Assertions.assertTrue(u.isPresent());
        Assertions.assertEquals("Alice", u.get().name);
    }
    @Test void testFindActiveUsers() {
        java.util.List<User> active = repo.findActiveUsers();
        Assertions.assertEquals(1, active.size());
        Assertions.assertEquals("alice@example.com", active.get(0).email);
    }
    @Test void testNotFound() {
        Assertions.assertFalse(repo.findByEmail("unknown@x.com").isPresent());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
```

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.orm.jpa.DataJpaTest;
import org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertyRegistry;
import org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertySource;
import org.testcontainers.containers.PostgreSQLContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.*;

@DataJpaTest @Testcontainers
class OrderRepositoryPGTest {
    @Container
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine")
        .withDatabaseName("testdb").withUsername("test").withPassword("test");

    @DynamicPropertySource
    static void configureProperties(DynamicPropertyRegistry registry) {
        registry.add("spring.datasource.url",     postgres::getJdbcUrl);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.username", postgres::getUsername);
        registry.add("spring.datasource.password", postgres::getPassword);
    }

    @Autowired OrderRepository repo;

    @Test void testRealPostgresInsert() {
        Order o = repo.save(new Order("u1", 150.0, "PENDING"));
        Assertions.assertNotNull(o.getId());
        Assertions.assertEquals("PENDING", repo.findById(o.getId()).orElseThrow().getStatus());
    }
}
// Dependencies: testcontainers:junit-jupiter, testcontainers:postgresql
```

```java
import com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.junit5.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.web.client.RestTemplate;
import static com.github.tomakehurst.wiremock.client.WireMock.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@WireMockTest(httpPort = 8089)
class PaymentClientTest {
    RestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();

    @Test void testChargeSuccess(WireMockRuntimeInfo wmRuntimeInfo) {
        // Stub POST /payments -> 200 SUCCESS (using escaped JSON string)
        String successBody = "{"status":"SUCCESS","transactionId":"TXN-123"}";
        stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/payments"))
            .withRequestBody(matchingJsonPath("$.amount", equalTo("100.0")))
            .willReturn(aResponse()
                .withStatus(200)
                .withHeader("Content-Type","application/json")
                .withBody(successBody)));

        String url = wmRuntimeInfo.getHttpBaseUrl() + "/payments";
        String resp = restTemplate.postForObject(url,
            java.util.Map.of("userId","u1","amount",100.0), String.class);
        assertTrue(resp.contains("SUCCESS"));
        verify(1, postRequestedFor(urlEqualTo("/payments")));
    }

    @Test void testChargeTimeout(WireMockRuntimeInfo wmRuntimeInfo) {
        stubFor(post(urlEqualTo("/payments")).willReturn(aResponse().withFixedDelay(5000).withStatus(200)));
        assertThrows(Exception.class, () ->
            restTemplate.postForObject(wmRuntimeInfo.getHttpBaseUrl()+"/payments",
                java.util.Map.of("amount",50.0), String.class));
    }
}
```

```java
import au.com.dius.pact.consumer.dsl.*;
import au.com.dius.pact.consumer.junit5.*;
import au.com.dius.pact.core.model.annotations.Pact;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import org.springframework.web.client.RestTemplate;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@ExtendWith(PactConsumerTestExt.class)
@PactTestFor(providerName = "user-service")
class OrderServiceContractTest {
    @Pact(consumer = "order-service")
    RequestResponsePact getUserPact(PactDslWithProvider builder) {
        return builder
            .given("user 1 exists")
            .uponReceiving("get user by id")
            .path("/users/1").method("GET")
            .willRespondWith().status(200)
            .body(new PactDslJsonBody()
                .integerType("id", 1)
                .stringType("name", "Alice")
                .stringType("email", "alice@x.com"))
            .toPact();
    }

    @Test @PactTestFor(pactMethod = "getUserPact")
    void testGetUser(MockServer mockServer) {
        RestTemplate rt = new RestTemplate();
        String resp = rt.getForObject(mockServer.getUrl() + "/users/1", String.class);
        assertTrue(resp.contains("Alice"));
    }
}
// Provider test verifies the pact: @Provider("user-service") @PactFolder("pacts")
// mvn pact:verify -> confirms provider satisfies consumer expectations
```

### 1865. Parameterized Test
**ID:** `TST-1865`

**Problem:** Parameterized Test.

**Example Input:** multiple input combinations tested

**Example Output:** all param sets pass

**Explanation:** @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource, @MethodSource, @ValueSource; DRY test cases.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.params.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class MathUtils {
    static int factorial(int n) { return n<=1 ? 1 : n*factorial(n-1); }
    static boolean isPalindrome(String s) { return s.equals(new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString()); }
}

class ParameterizedTests {
    @ParameterizedTest @CsvSource({"0,1","1,1","2,2","3,6","4,24","5,120"})
    void testFactorial(int n, int expected) { assertEquals(expected, MathUtils.factorial(n)); }

    @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(strings = {"racecar","madam","level","noon"})
    void testPalindromes(String word) { assertTrue(MathUtils.isPalindrome(word)); }

    @ParameterizedTest @MethodSource("nonPalindromes")
    void testNonPalindromes(String word) { assertFalse(MathUtils.isPalindrome(word)); }

    static java.util.stream.Stream<String> nonPalindromes() {
        return java.util.stream.Stream.of("hello","world","java");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n!) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 1866. Exception Testing
**ID:** `TST-1866`

**Example Input:** service throws typed exceptions on invalid input

**Example Output:** exception type and message verified

**Explanation:** assertThrows with JUnit 5; test exception message, cause, type hierarchy.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class InsufficientFundsException extends RuntimeException {
    private final double deficit;
    InsufficientFundsException(double d) { super("Insufficient funds: deficit="+d); deficit=d; }
    double getDeficit() { return deficit; }
}

class BankAccount {
    private double balance;
    BankAccount(double b) { balance=b; }
    void withdraw(double amount) {
        if (amount > balance) throw new InsufficientFundsException(amount - balance);
        balance -= amount;
    }
}

class ExceptionTest {
    @Test void testInsufficientFunds() {
        BankAccount acc = new BankAccount(100.0);
        InsufficientFundsException ex = assertThrows(InsufficientFundsException.class,
            () -> acc.withdraw(150.0));
        assertEquals(50.0, ex.getDeficit(), 0.001);
        assertTrue(ex.getMessage().contains("50.0"));
    }
    @Test void testNegativeWithdraw() {
        BankAccount acc = new BankAccount(100.0);
        assertDoesNotThrow(() -> acc.withdraw(0.0));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
@EmbeddedKafka(partitions=1, topics={"order-events"}, brokerProperties={"listeners=PLAINTEXT://localhost:9092"})
class KafkaProducerTest {
    @Autowired KafkaTemplate<String,String> kafkaTemplate;
    @Autowired TestConsumer consumer;

    @Test void testSendMessage() throws Exception {
        kafkaTemplate.send("order-events", "key1", "{"orderId":"ORD-001"}");
        boolean received = consumer.latch.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        Assertions.assertTrue(received, "Message not received within 10s");
        Assertions.assertTrue(consumer.lastMessage.contains("ORD-001"));
    }
}

@Component class TestConsumer {
    CountDownLatch latch = new CountDownLatch(1);
    String lastMessage;
    @KafkaListener(topics="order-events", groupId="test-group")
    void consume(String message) { lastMessage = message; latch.countDown(); }
}
```

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.cache.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertyRegistry;
import org.springframework.test.context.DynamicPropertySource;
import org.testcontainers.containers.GenericContainer;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.*;

@SpringBootTest @Testcontainers
class RedisCacheTest {
    @Container static GenericContainer<?> redis = new GenericContainer<>("redis:7-alpine").withExposedPorts(6379);

    @DynamicPropertySource static void redisProps(DynamicPropertyRegistry r) {
        r.add("spring.data.redis.host", redis::getHost);
        r.add("spring.data.redis.port", () -> redis.getMappedPort(6379));
    }

    @Autowired UserCacheService service;

    @Test void testCacheHit() {
        service.callCount = 0;
        service.getUser(1L); service.getUser(1L); service.getUser(1L);
        Assertions.assertEquals(1, service.callCount, "Should only call DB once");
    }

    @Test void testCacheEviction() {
        service.getUser(2L);
        service.evict(2L);
        service.callCount = 0;
        service.getUser(2L);
        Assertions.assertEquals(1, service.callCount);
    }
}

@Service @EnableCaching class UserCacheService {
    int callCount = 0;
    @Cacheable("users") public String getUser(Long id) { callCount++; return "user-"+id; }
    @CacheEvict("users") public void evict(Long id) {}
}
```

```java
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Async;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.EnableAsync;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.concurrent.*;

@SpringBootTest class AsyncServiceTest {
    @Autowired EmailService emailService;

    @Test void testAsyncEmail() throws Exception {
        CompletableFuture<String> future = emailService.sendEmail("user@test.com", "Hello");
        String result = future.get(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        Assertions.assertEquals("SENT", result);
    }

    @Test void testAsyncException() {
        CompletableFuture<String> future = emailService.sendEmail("invalid", "test");
        Assertions.assertThrows(ExecutionException.class, () -> future.get(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS));
    }

@Service @EnableAsync class EmailService {
    @Async public CompletableFuture<String> sendEmail(String to, String body) {
        if (!to.contains("@")) return CompletableFuture.failedFuture(new IllegalArgumentException("Bad email"));
        try { Thread.sleep(100); } catch (InterruptedException e) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); }
        return CompletableFuture.completedFuture("SENT");
    }
```

### 1874. Custom Validation Test
**ID:** `TST-1874`

**Example Output:** 400 returned; validator logic works

**Answer:**

```java
import jakarta.validation.*;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import java.lang.annotation.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@Documented @Constraint(validatedBy = AgeValidator.class)
@Target(ElementType.FIELD) @Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
@interface ValidAge { String message() default "Age must be 18-120"; Class<?>[] groups() default {}; Class<? extends Payload>[] payload() default {}; }

class AgeValidator implements ConstraintValidator<ValidAge,Integer> {
    public boolean isValid(Integer age, ConstraintValidatorContext ctx) {
        return age != null && age >= 18 && age <= 120;
    }
}

record UserDto(@NotBlank String name, @ValidAge Integer age) {}

class CustomValidationTest {
    static Validator validator;
    @BeforeAll static void setup() { validator = Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory().getValidator(); }

    @Test void testValidAge() { assertTrue(validator.validate(new UserDto("Alice", 25)).isEmpty()); }
    @Test void testTooYoung() {
        var violations = validator.validate(new UserDto("Bob", 10));
        assertFalse(violations.isEmpty());
        assertEquals("Age must be 18-120", violations.iterator().next().getMessage());
    }
    @Test void testNullAge() { assertFalse(validator.validate(new UserDto("Carol", null)).isEmpty()); }
    @Test void testBlankName() { assertFalse(validator.validate(new UserDto("", 25)).isEmpty()); }
}
```

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@SpringBootTest class TransactionRollbackTest {
    @Autowired TransferService transferService;
    @Autowired AccountRepository accountRepo;

    @Test @Transactional void testSuccessfulTransfer() {
        Long from = accountRepo.save(new Account("Alice", 1000.0)).getId();
        Long to   = accountRepo.save(new Account("Bob",   500.0)).getId();
        transferService.transfer(from, to, 200.0);
        assertEquals(800.0, accountRepo.findById(from).orElseThrow().getBalance(), 0.001);
        assertEquals(700.0, accountRepo.findById(to).orElseThrow().getBalance(), 0.001);
    }

    @Test @Transactional void testRollbackOnInsufficient() {
        Long from = accountRepo.save(new Account("Alice", 100.0)).getId();
        Long to   = accountRepo.save(new Account("Bob",   500.0)).getId();
        assertThrows(IllegalStateException.class, () -> transferService.transfer(from, to, 500.0));
        assertEquals(100.0, accountRepo.findById(from).orElseThrow().getBalance(), 0.001);
        assertEquals(500.0, accountRepo.findById(to).orElseThrow().getBalance(), 0.001);
    }
}
```

### 1876. Rate Limiting Test
**ID:** `TST-1876`

**Problem:** Rate Limiting Test.

**Example Input:** endpoint allows 10 req/min per user

**Example Output:** 11th request returns 429

**Explanation:** Test rate limiter with time control; Bucket4j or Resilience4j; mock clock for speed.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;
import java.time.*; import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;

class InMemoryRateLimiter {
    private final int max;
    private final Duration window;
    private final java.util.Map<String, java.util.Deque<Instant>> buckets = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    InMemoryRateLimiter(int max, Duration window) { this.max=max; this.window=window; }

    boolean isAllowed(String key) {
        Instant now = Instant.now();
        Instant cutoff = now.minus(window);
        buckets.compute(key, (k, q) -> {
            if (q==null) q=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>();
            while (!q.isEmpty() && q.peekFirst().isBefore(cutoff)) q.pollFirst();
            return q;
        });
        java.util.Deque<Instant> q = buckets.get(key);
        if (q.size() >= max) return false;
        q.addLast(now);
        return true;
    }
}

class RateLimiterTest {
    @Test void testAllowsUpToLimit() {
        InMemoryRateLimiter rl = new InMemoryRateLimiter(5, Duration.ofSeconds(60));
        for (int i=0; i<5; i++) assertTrue(rl.isAllowed("user1"), "Request "+(i+1)+" should be allowed");
        assertFalse(rl.isAllowed("user1"), "6th request should be rate-limited");
    }
    @Test void testDifferentUsersIndependent() {
        InMemoryRateLimiter rl = new InMemoryRateLimiter(2, Duration.ofSeconds(60));
        assertTrue(rl.isAllowed("user1")); assertTrue(rl.isAllowed("user2"));
        assertTrue(rl.isAllowed("user1")); assertFalse(rl.isAllowed("user1"));
        assertTrue(rl.isAllowed("user2"));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(users*reqs)
---

### 1877. Circuit Breaker Test
**ID:** `TST-1877`

**Problem:** Circuit Breaker Test.

**Example Input:** external service fails; circuit opens

**Example Output:** fallback returned; circuit prevents cascade

**Explanation:** Resilience4j CircuitBreaker; @CircuitBreaker; test state transitions CLOSED->OPEN->HALF_OPEN.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.github.resilience4j.circuitbreaker.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class CircuitBreakerTest {
    @Test void testCircuitOpens() {
        CircuitBreakerConfig config = CircuitBreakerConfig.custom()
            .failureRateThreshold(50).slidingWindowSize(4)
            .waitDurationInOpenState(java.time.Duration.ofMillis(100)).build();
        CircuitBreaker cb = CircuitBreaker.of("test", config);
        AtomicInteger callCount = new AtomicInteger();

        for (int i=0; i<4; i++) {
            int fi = i;
            try { cb.executeRunnable(() -> { callCount.incrementAndGet(); if (fi < 3) throw new RuntimeException("down"); }); }
            catch (Exception ignored) {}
        }
        assertEquals(CircuitBreaker.State.OPEN, cb.getState());
        System.out.println("Failure rate: "+cb.getMetrics().getFailureRate());
    }

    @Test void testFallback() {
        CircuitBreaker cb = CircuitBreaker.of("test2",
            CircuitBreakerConfig.custom().slidingWindowSize(2).failureRateThreshold(50).build());
        cb.transitionToOpenState();
        String result = cb.executeWithFallback(() -> "real", ex -> "fallback");
        assertEquals("fallback", result);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(window)
---

### 1878. Retry Logic Test
**ID:** `TST-1878`

**Problem:** Retry Logic Test.

**Example Input:** flaky HTTP call retried automatically

**Example Output:** succeeds after 2 failures; verify retry count

**Explanation:** Resilience4j Retry or Spring-Retry; test with mock that fails N times then succeeds.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.github.resilience4j.retry.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class RetryTest {
    @Test void testRetrySucceedsAfterFailures() {
        AtomicInteger attempt = new AtomicInteger(0);
        RetryConfig config = RetryConfig.custom()
            .maxAttempts(4).waitDuration(java.time.Duration.ofMillis(10)).build();
        Retry retry = Retry.of("test", config);

        String result = retry.executeSupplier(() -> {
            int a = attempt.incrementAndGet();
            System.out.println("Attempt "+a);
            if (a < 3) throw new RuntimeException("Transient error");
            return "SUCCESS";
        });
        assertEquals("SUCCESS", result);
        assertEquals(3, attempt.get());
    }

    @Test void testMaxRetriesExhausted() {
        RetryConfig config = RetryConfig.custom().maxAttempts(2).waitDuration(java.time.Duration.ofMillis(1)).build();
        Retry retry = Retry.of("test2", config);
        assertThrows(RuntimeException.class, () ->
            retry.executeRunnable(() -> { throw new RuntimeException("Always fails"); }));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(attempts) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.batch.core.*;
import org.springframework.batch.test.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@SpringBootTest class BatchJobTest {
    @Autowired JobLauncherTestUtils jobLauncherTestUtils;
    @Autowired JobRepositoryTestUtils jobRepositoryTestUtils;

    @BeforeEach void clearJobHistory() { jobRepositoryTestUtils.removeJobExecutions(); }

    @Test void testImportJob() throws Exception {
        JobExecution exec = jobLauncherTestUtils.launchJob();
        assertEquals(BatchStatus.COMPLETED, exec.getStatus());
        assertEquals(ExitStatus.COMPLETED, exec.getExitStatus());
    }

    @Test void testStepExecution() throws Exception {
        JobExecution exec = jobLauncherTestUtils.launchStep("importStep");
        StepExecution step = exec.getStepExecutions().iterator().next();
        assertEquals(BatchStatus.COMPLETED, exec.getStatus());
        assertTrue(step.getReadCount() > 0, "Should have read records");
        assertEquals(step.getReadCount(), step.getWriteCount(), "All read records written");
        assertEquals(0, step.getSkipCount(), "No records skipped");
        System.out.println("Read: "+step.getReadCount()+" Written: "+step.getWriteCount());
    }
}
```

### 1883. Cache Invalidation Test
**ID:** `TST-1883`

**Problem:** Cache Invalidation Test.

**Example Input:** update product; cache cleared; next read fresh

**Example Output:** stale data not returned

**Explanation:** Spring Cache @CachePut / @CacheEvict; test via direct cache access or repeated calls.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.cache.*;
import org.springframework.cache.annotation.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@SpringBootTest class CacheInvalidationTest {
    @Autowired ProductCacheService service;
    @Autowired CacheManager cacheManager;

    @Test void testCachePut() {
        service.update(1L, "Widget v2");
        String cached = (String) cacheManager.getCache("products").get(1L).get();
        assertEquals("Widget v2", cached);
    }

    @Test void testCacheEvict() {
        service.get(1L);
        assertNotNull(cacheManager.getCache("products").get(1L));
        service.evict(1L);
        assertNull(cacheManager.getCache("products").get(1L));
    }

    @Test void testCacheUsedOnRepeatedGet() {
        service.callCount = 0;
        service.get(2L); service.get(2L); service.get(2L);
        assertEquals(1, service.callCount, "DB should be hit only once");
    }
}

@Service @EnableCaching class ProductCacheService {
    int callCount = 0;
    @Cacheable("products") public String get(Long id) { callCount++; return "Product-"+id; }
    @CachePut(value="products", key="#id") public String update(Long id, String name) { return name; }
    @CacheEvict("products") public void evict(Long id) {}
}
```

### 1884. Multi-Tenant Test
**ID:** `TST-1884`

**Problem:** Multi-Tenant Test.

**Example Input:** requests from different tenants isolated

**Example Output:** tenant A cannot see tenant B data

**Explanation:** TenantContext with ThreadLocal; @DataJpaTest with tenant filter; verify row-level isolation.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class TenantContext {
    private static final ThreadLocal<String> TENANT = new ThreadLocal<>();
    static void set(String t) { TENANT.set(t); }
    static String get() { return TENANT.get(); }
    static void clear() { TENANT.remove(); }
}

class TenantAwareService {
    private final java.util.Map<String, java.util.List<String>> db = new java.util.HashMap<>();
    void addRecord(String data) {
        db.computeIfAbsent(TenantContext.get(), k -> new java.util.ArrayList<>()).add(data);
    }
    java.util.List<String> getRecords() {
        return db.getOrDefault(TenantContext.get(), java.util.List.of());
    }
}

class MultiTenantTest {
    TenantAwareService service = new TenantAwareService();
    @AfterEach void cleanup() { TenantContext.clear(); }

    @Test void testTenantIsolation() {
        TenantContext.set("tenant-A");
        service.addRecord("A-Data-1"); service.addRecord("A-Data-2");
        TenantContext.set("tenant-B");
        service.addRecord("B-Data-1");

        TenantContext.set("tenant-A");
        assertEquals(2, service.getRecords().size());
        assertTrue(service.getRecords().stream().allMatch(d -> d.startsWith("A")));

        TenantContext.set("tenant-B");
        assertEquals(1, service.getRecords().size());
        assertTrue(service.getRecords().get(0).startsWith("B"));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(tenants*records)
---

### 1886. WebSocket Test
**ID:** `TST-1886`

**Problem:** WebSocket Test.

**Example Input:** client sends message; server broadcasts

**Example Output:** all connected clients receive message

**Explanation:** @SpringBootTest with RANDOM_PORT; StompClient; subscribeAndAwait; verify payload.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.test.web.server.LocalServerPort;
import org.springframework.messaging.converter.StringMessageConverter;
import org.springframework.messaging.simp.stomp.*;
import org.springframework.web.socket.client.standard.StandardWebSocketClient;
import org.springframework.web.socket.messaging.WebSocketStompClient;
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class WebSocketTest {
    @LocalServerPort int port;

    @Test void testBroadcast() throws Exception {
        WebSocketStompClient client = new WebSocketStompClient(new StandardWebSocketClient());
        client.setMessageConverter(new StringMessageConverter());
        BlockingQueue<String> messages = new LinkedBlockingQueue<>();

        StompSession session = client.connect("ws://localhost:"+port+"/ws",
            new StompSessionHandlerAdapter(){}).get(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        session.subscribe("/topic/orders", new StompFrameHandler() {
            public java.lang.reflect.Type getPayloadType(StompHeaders h) { return String.class; }
            public void handleFrame(StompHeaders h, Object p) { messages.offer((String)p); }
        });
        session.send("/app/order", "NEW_ORDER");
        String msg = messages.poll(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
        assertNotNull(msg, "Should receive broadcast");
        assertTrue(msg.contains("NEW_ORDER"));
        session.disconnect();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(clients) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1888. CQRS Test
**ID:** `TST-1888`

**Problem:** CQRS Test.

**Example Input:** command and query sides tested separately

**Example Output:** write model and read model independent

**Explanation:** Command handler tested for state change; Query handler tested for read path; no cross-coupling.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;
import java.util.*;

record CreateProductCommand(String name, double price){}
record ProductCreatedEvent(String id, String name, double price){}

class ProductCommandHandler {
    private final List<ProductCreatedEvent> store;
    ProductCommandHandler(List<ProductCreatedEvent> store) { this.store=store; }
    ProductCreatedEvent handle(CreateProductCommand cmd) {
        if (cmd.price() < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Negative price");
        ProductCreatedEvent evt = new ProductCreatedEvent(UUID.randomUUID().toString(), cmd.name(), cmd.price());
        store.add(evt);
        return evt;
    }
}

class ProductQueryHandler {
    private final List<ProductCreatedEvent> store;
    ProductQueryHandler(List<ProductCreatedEvent> store) { this.store=store; }
    Optional<ProductCreatedEvent> findByName(String name) {
        return store.stream().filter(p -> p.name().equals(name)).findFirst();
    }
    List<ProductCreatedEvent> findAll() { return Collections.unmodifiableList(store); }
}

class CqrsTest {
    List<ProductCreatedEvent> eventStore = new ArrayList<>();
    ProductCommandHandler cmd = new ProductCommandHandler(eventStore);
    ProductQueryHandler qry = new ProductQueryHandler(eventStore);

    @Test void testCreateAndQuery() {
        cmd.handle(new CreateProductCommand("Widget", 9.99));
        assertEquals(1, qry.findAll().size());
        assertTrue(qry.findByName("Widget").isPresent());
    }
    @Test void testNegativePrice() {
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> cmd.handle(new CreateProductCommand("Bad",-1)));
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(events)
---

### 1889. Saga Pattern Test
**ID:** `TST-1889`

**Problem:** Saga Pattern Test.

**Example Input:** order saga: reserve inventory, charge payment

**Example Output:** saga compensates on payment failure

**Explanation:** Choreography saga; test compensation transactions triggered on failure.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean;

class InventoryService {
    AtomicBoolean reserved = new AtomicBoolean(false);
    AtomicBoolean released = new AtomicBoolean(false);
    void reserve(String id) { reserved.set(true); }
    void release(String id) { released.set(true); }
}

class PaymentService {
    boolean shouldFail;
    PaymentService(boolean fail) { shouldFail=fail; }
    void charge(String id, double amount) {
        if (shouldFail) throw new RuntimeException("Payment declined");
    }
}

class OrderSaga {
    private final InventoryService inv; private final PaymentService pay;
    OrderSaga(InventoryService i, PaymentService p) { inv=i; pay=p; }
    String execute(String id, double amount) {
        inv.reserve(id);
        try { pay.charge(id, amount); return "ORDER_COMPLETED"; }
        catch (Exception e) { inv.release(id); return "ORDER_FAILED"; }
    }
}

class SagaTest {
    @Test void testSuccessfulSaga() {
        InventoryService inv = new InventoryService();
        assertEquals("ORDER_COMPLETED", new OrderSaga(inv, new PaymentService(false)).execute("ORD-1", 100.0));
        assertTrue(inv.reserved.get()); assertFalse(inv.released.get());
    }
    @Test void testCompensation() {
        InventoryService inv = new InventoryService();
        assertEquals("ORDER_FAILED", new OrderSaga(inv, new PaymentService(true)).execute("ORD-2", 100.0));
        assertTrue(inv.released.get(), "Inventory should be released on failure");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(steps) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

### 1890. Idempotency Test
**ID:** `TST-1890`

**Problem:** Idempotency Test.

**Example Input:** duplicate order request not processed twice

**Example Output:** exactly-once semantics; idempotency key

**Explanation:** IdempotencyKey checked; second call returns cached result without DB insert.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;
import java.util.*; import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

class IdempotentOrderService {
    private final Map<String,String> processedKeys = new HashMap<>();
    private final AtomicInteger dbInserts = new AtomicInteger(0);

    String createOrder(String idempotencyKey, String userId, double amount) {
        if (processedKeys.containsKey(idempotencyKey)) {
            System.out.println("Idempotency hit: "+idempotencyKey);
            return processedKeys.get(idempotencyKey);
        }
        String orderId = "ORD-" + dbInserts.incrementAndGet();
        processedKeys.put(idempotencyKey, orderId);
        return orderId;
    }
}

class IdempotencyTest {
    IdempotentOrderService service = new IdempotentOrderService();

    @Test void testDuplicateRequest() {
        String key = UUID.randomUUID().toString();
        String first  = service.createOrder(key, "u1", 100.0);
        String second = service.createOrder(key, "u1", 100.0);
        String third  = service.createOrder(key, "u1", 100.0);
        assertEquals(first, second); assertEquals(first, third);
        assertEquals(1, service.dbInserts.get(), "DB should be written only once");
    }

    @Test void testDifferentKeys() {
        String r1 = service.createOrder("key-1","u1",100.0);
        String r2 = service.createOrder("key-2","u1",100.0);
        assertNotEquals(r1, r2);
        assertEquals(2, service.dbInserts.get());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(keys)
---

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;

class FeatureFlagService {
    private final Map<String,Boolean> flags = new HashMap<>();
    void set(String flag, boolean value) { flags.put(flag,value); }

}

class CheckoutService {
    private final FeatureFlagService flags;
    CheckoutService(FeatureFlagService f) { flags=f; }
    String checkout(String userId, double amount) {

        return "OLD_CHECKOUT_"+userId+"_"+amount;
    }

class FeatureFlagTest {
```

```java
// JMeter DSL (jmeter-java-dsl):
import us.abstracta.jmeter.javadsl.core.TestPlanStats;
import static us.abstracta.jmeter.javadsl.JmeterDsl.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import java.time.Duration;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class LoadTest {
    @Test void testOrderEndpointLoad() throws Exception {
        // Use plain string for JSON body (avoid Java text block triple-quote issues)
        String body = "{"userId":"u1","amount":99.99}";
        TestPlanStats stats = testPlan(
            threadGroup(50, 60,
                httpSampler("http://localhost:8080/orders")
                    .post(body, org.apache.http.entity.ContentType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            ),
            htmlReporter("target/jmeter-report")
        ).run();

        assertTrue(stats.overall().errorsCount() < stats.overall().samplesCount() * 0.001,
            "Error rate should be < 0.1%");
        assertTrue(stats.overall().sampleTimePercentile99().compareTo(Duration.ofMillis(500)) < 0,
            "P99 should be < 500ms");
        System.out.printf("Total: %d, Errors: %d, P95: %s%n",
            stats.overall().samplesCount(), stats.overall().errorsCount(),
            stats.overall().sampleTimePercentile95());
    }
}
// Alternative: k6 load testing: k6 run script.js --vus 50 --duration 60s
```

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class Discount {
    static double apply(double price) { return price > 100 ? price * 0.9 : price; }
}

class WeakDiscountTest {
    @Test void testDiscount_WEAK() {
        // WEAK: mutant changing > to >= still passes this test
        assertTrue(Discount.apply(200) < 200);
    }
    @Test void testDiscount_STRONG_boundary() {
        // STRONG: kills boundary mutant (> vs >=)
        assertEquals(100.0, Discount.apply(100.0), 0.001);  // at boundary, no discount
        assertEquals(100.0 * 0.9, Discount.apply(101.0), 0.001);  // just above, discount applied
    }
}
```

## Production Debugging Scenarios


### 1895. Debug CPU Spike
**ID:** `DBG-1895`

**Problem:** Debug CPU Spike.

**Example Input:** Java service consuming 95% CPU suddenly

**Example Output:** identify hot method; reduce load

**Explanation:** top/jstack for thread dump; jprofile/async-profiler; find CPU-bound loop or busy wait.

**Answer:**
```java
// Step 1: Identify high-CPU threads via jstack
// ps aux | grep java -> PID 12345
// jstack 12345 > thread-dump.txt
// Look for threads in RUNNABLE state consuming CPU

// Step 2: Convert decimal TID to hex, find in thread-dump
// printf '%x
' <tid>  -> search in dump

// Step 3: Async Profiler (flamegraph)
// ./profiler.sh -d 30 -f /tmp/flamegraph.html 12345
// Open flamegraph to pinpoint hot method

// Common CPU spike causes:
// 1. Infinite loop (while(true) with no sleep)
// 2. Regex backtracking catastrophically
// 3. Synchronized method under high contention
// 4. Tight retry loop without backoff

// Example fix: add sleep to prevent busy-wait
class CPUSpikeDebug {
    // BAD: busy-wait
    static void badWait(boolean[] flag) {
        while (!flag[0]) { /* spins CPU */ }
    }

    // GOOD: use LockSupport or wait/notify
    static void goodWait(Object lock) throws InterruptedException {
        synchronized (lock) {
            lock.wait(100);  // releases CPU during wait
        }
    }

    // JVM flags for CPU profiling:
    // -XX:+PrintGCDetails -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps
    // -agentlib:hprof=cpu=samples,interval=20,depth=3
    // jcmd <PID> VM.native_memory -> memory regions
    // jcmd <PID> GC.heap_info -> heap summary
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("CPU debugging: use async-profiler or JFR");
        System.out.println("JFR: jcmd <PID> JFR.start duration=60s filename=/tmp/rec.jfr");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(threads)
---

### 1896. Debug Memory Leak
**ID:** `DBG-1896`

**Problem:** Debug Memory Leak.

**Example Input:** heap grows until OOM; application crashes

**Example Output:** identify leaking object; fix retention

**Explanation:** Enable GC logs; take heap dump with jmap; analyze with Eclipse MAT or VisualVM.

**Answer:**
```java
// Step 1: JVM flags to capture heap dump on OOM
// -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/tmp/heap.hprof
// -Xms512m -Xmx2g -verbose:gc -XX:+PrintGCDetails

// Step 2: Force heap dump manually
// jmap -dump:format=b,file=/tmp/heap.hprof <PID>
// jcmd <PID> GC.heap_dump /tmp/heap.hprof

// Step 3: Analyze with MAT -> Dominator Tree, Leak Suspects

// Common memory leak patterns in Java:
import java.util.*;

class MemoryLeakDemo {
    // LEAK 1: Static collection grows unbounded
    static Map<String, byte[]> CACHE = new HashMap<>();
    static void leak1(String key) {
        CACHE.put(key, new byte[1024 * 1024]);  // never removed!
    }

    // FIX 1: Use bounded cache (Guava Cache / Caffeine)
    // Cache<String,byte[]> cache = Caffeine.newBuilder().maximumSize(1000).expireAfterWrite(1, HOURS).build();

    // LEAK 2: Listener not deregistered
    static List<Object> listeners = new ArrayList<>();
    static void leak2(Object listener) { listeners.add(listener); /* never removed */ }

    // FIX 2: WeakReference listeners or explicit deregister
    static List<WeakReference<Object>> safeListeners = new ArrayList<>();
    static void addSafeListener(Object l) { safeListeners.add(new WeakReference<>(l)); }

    // LEAK 3: ThreadLocal not cleaned up
    static ThreadLocal<List<String>> TL = new ThreadLocal<>();
    static void leak3() { TL.set(new ArrayList<>()); /* never TL.remove() */ }

    // FIX 3: Always call TL.remove() in finally block
    static void safe3() {
        TL.set(new ArrayList<>());
        try { /* use TL.get() */ }
        finally { TL.remove(); }
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(heap)
---

### 1897. Analyze Thread Dump
**ID:** `DBG-1897`

**Problem:** Analyze Thread Dump.

**Example Input:** application hanging; no progress

**Example Output:** identify deadlock or blocked threads

**Explanation:** jstack <PID>; look for BLOCKED/WAITING; find deadlock in summary; fix lock ordering.

**Answer:**
```java
// Generate thread dump:
// jstack <PID> > dump.txt
// kill -3 <PID>   (sends SIGQUIT, prints to stdout on many JVMs)
// jcmd <PID> Thread.print

// Thread states to look for:
// RUNNABLE  - executing (CPU usage)
// BLOCKED   - waiting for monitor lock (potential deadlock)
// WAITING   - in Object.wait() or LockSupport.park()
// TIMED_WAITING - sleeping or timed wait

// Example deadlock in dump:
// Thread-1: locked <0x00000001> waiting for <0x00000002>
// Thread-2: locked <0x00000002> waiting for <0x00000001>
// Java-level deadlock: -> deadlock detected

import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;

class DeadlockDemo {
    static ReentrantLock lockA = new ReentrantLock();
    static ReentrantLock lockB = new ReentrantLock();

    // DEADLOCK: Thread1 holds A, waits for B; Thread2 holds B, waits for A
    static void thread1() { lockA.lock(); lockB.lock(); /* work */ lockB.unlock(); lockA.unlock(); }
    static void thread2() { lockB.lock(); lockA.lock(); /* work */ lockA.unlock(); lockB.unlock(); }

    // FIX: consistent lock ordering
    static void fixedThread1() { lockA.lock(); lockB.lock(); /* work */ lockB.unlock(); lockA.unlock(); }
    static void fixedThread2() { lockA.lock(); lockB.lock(); /* work */ lockB.unlock(); lockA.unlock(); }

    // FIX 2: tryLock with timeout
    static void safeThread() throws InterruptedException {
        while (true) {
            if (lockA.tryLock()) {
                try {
                    if (lockB.tryLock()) {
                        try { /* work */ return; }
                        finally { lockB.unlock(); }
                    }
                } finally { lockA.unlock(); }
            }
            Thread.sleep(10);  // backoff before retry
        }
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(threads) &nbsp; **Space:** O(threads)

### 1900. Kafka Duplicate Messages
**ID:** `DBG-1900`

**Problem:** Kafka Duplicate Messages.

**Example Input:** consumer processes same message twice

**Example Output:** exactly-once or idempotent consumer

**Explanation:** Enable idempotent producer; use transactions; consumer deduplication by message ID.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.*;
import org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.*;
import java.util.*;

class KafkaDeduplication {
    // FIX 1: Idempotent producer (dedup on producer side)
    static Properties idempotentProducerProps() {
        Properties props = new Properties();
        props.put(ProducerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, "localhost:9092");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE_CONFIG, true);   // dedup within session
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ACKS_CONFIG, "all");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.RETRIES_CONFIG, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
        props.put(ProducerConfig.MAX_IN_FLIGHT_REQUESTS_PER_CONNECTION, 5);
        return props;
    }

    // FIX 2: Exactly-once semantics (Kafka Transactions)
    static void exactlyOnceProducer() {
        Properties props = idempotentProducerProps();
        props.put(ProducerConfig.TRANSACTIONAL_ID_CONFIG, "order-producer-1");
        KafkaProducer<String,String> producer = new KafkaProducer<>(props);
        producer.initTransactions();
        try {
            producer.beginTransaction();
            producer.send(new ProducerRecord<>("orders", "key", "value"));
            producer.commitTransaction();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            producer.abortTransaction();
        }
    }

    // FIX 3: Consumer-side deduplication (idempotent processing)
    private static final Set<String> processedIds = Collections.synchronizedSet(new HashSet<>());

    static void idempotentConsume(ConsumerRecord<String,String> record) {
        String msgId = record.topic() + "-" + record.partition() + "-" + record.offset();
        if (processedIds.add(msgId)) {
            processOrder(record.value());  // only process if new
        } else {
            System.out.println("Duplicate skipped: " + msgId);
        }
    }

    static void processOrder(String value) { System.out.println("Processing: "+value); }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(msgIds)
---

### 1901. Redis Cache Stampede
**ID:** `DBG-1901`

**Problem:** Redis Cache Stampede.

**Example Input:** cache expires; thousands of DB queries simultaneously

**Example Output:** use lock or probabilistic refresh

**Explanation:** Cache stampede: all threads miss cache simultaneously; solutions: mutex lock, early refresh.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
import java.util.function.Supplier;

class CacheStampedeSolutions {
    // Problem: cache expires at T, all 1000 concurrent requests miss and hit DB

    // SOLUTION 1: Mutex Lock (distributed lock via Redisson)
    // Only first request fetches from DB; others wait
    static String getWithMutex(String key, Supplier<String> dbFetch, RedissonClient redisson) {
        String cached = redis.get(key);
        if (cached != null) return cached;

        RLock lock = redisson.getLock("lock:" + key);
        try {
            lock.lock(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
            cached = redis.get(key);  // double-check after acquiring lock
            if (cached != null) return cached;
            cached = dbFetch.get();   // only one thread fetches from DB
            redis.setex(key, 300, cached);
            return cached;
        } finally { lock.unlock(); }
    }

    // SOLUTION 2: Probabilistic Early Expiration (no lock needed)
    // Refresh before expiry based on random probability
    static String getWithPER(String key, Supplier<String> dbFetch, long ttlSeconds) {
        String cached = redis.get(key);
        long ttlRemaining = redis.ttl(key);

        // Probability to refresh increases as TTL approaches 0
        double beta = 1.0;
        boolean shouldRefresh = -beta * Math.log(Math.random()) > ttlRemaining;

        if (cached == null || shouldRefresh) {
            String fresh = dbFetch.get();
            redis.setex(key, ttlSeconds, fresh);
            return fresh;
        }
        return cached;
    }

    // SOLUTION 3: Staggered TTL (add jitter to avoid synchronized expiry)
    static long ttlWithJitter(long baseTtl) {
        return baseTtl + (long)(Math.random() * baseTtl * 0.1);  // +0-10% jitter
    }

    // Mock redis for compilation
    static class redis { static String get(String k){return null;} static void setex(String k,long t,String v){} static long ttl(String k){return 60;} }
    interface RedissonClient { RLock getLock(String k); }
    interface RLock { void lock(long t, TimeUnit u); void unlock(); }
    interface RedissonClient2 {}
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

```java
    // Allocation rate reduction:
    static String formatDate_BAD(java.time.LocalDate d) {

    static String formatDate_GOOD(java.time.LocalDate d, StringBuilder sb) {

    }
```
